stories.title: Police officer found dead in Saryu River:Facial injuries raise questions over accident or murder; body sent for examination
stories.summary: The mystery of SSI Ajay Gond's death, who was posted in Basti, is deepening. The post-mortem report shows injury marks all over the face. There are also injury marks on the nose and both ears. Additionally, some water was found in the stomach. However, the exact cause of death could not be determined. For this, viscera has been sent for examination. Along with this, a part of the chest bone and brain has also been sent for examination. Police have obtained the CDR of the inspector. According to this, his last conversation was with his wife Ranjita and a court follower from the police station named Neeraj. Meanwhile, in CCTV footage, Inspector Ajay was seen going alone towards Ayodhya. However, the approximately 60 km distance between where his bike was found and where his body was discovered has complicated the mystery. Police are trying to find answers to how the bike reached Basti. Actually, Inspector Ajay Gond had been missing since February 5. His wife and family members have called it a planned murder, but haven't accused anyone specifically. There are also allegations of negligence against the police. The family says that if the police had taken action immediately after filing the missing person report, perhaps Ajay would have been alive. Read how far police investigation has reached in inspector's death case and what are family's allegations... Know the complete matter The body of Inspector Ajay Kumar Gond, posted at Parshurampur police station in Basti district, was found in the Saryu river of Ayodhya on February 8. Ajay lived in Basti with his wife and 2 children. He had left the police station during duty on the evening of February 5. After that, there was no trace of him. The next day after going missing, on February 6, the inspector's bike was found near the Kuano river in Basti. Inspector Ajay was last seen in CCTV footage riding a bike with a sanitation worker. Inspector's wife Ranjita Gond said - Ajay left for the police station on February 5 after having tea and breakfast. After Parshurampur Station Officer Vishwa Mohan Rai went on leave, my husband was in charge of the police station. He had talked to me at 3:30 in the afternoon. According to the police station constables, around 5 PM, Inspector Ajay left somewhere on a bike with a sanitation worker posted at the station. A video of him leaving the police station has also emerged. Ranjita said that she called between 8 to 9 PM at night, but the phone was switched off. About 3 hours after the search operation ended, at 7 PM information was received that a body was spotted in the Saryu river in Tighura Majha village under Darshan Nagar police station area of Ayodhya. Ayodhya police reached the spot on information from villagers. The body was identified as that of Inspector Ajay Gond. Read investigation so far Police working to retrieve CCTV footage of route taken by inspector Police obtained inspector Ajay's CDR. This confirmed that Ajay Gond last spoke on phone with his wife and then with Neeraj, a supporter from Parashurampur police station. Police have obtained CCTV footage up to 5 kilometers before the location where his body was found. Police are connecting all the subsequent footage to trace the inspector's movement. Additionally, based on injury marks found in the postmortem report, police are now investigating this from a murder angle as well. Not able to focus on studies: Son The inspector's brother-in-law Vijay Kumar said - The fee of Rs 90,000 for elder son Amit, who was studying in Kanpur, was deducted from wife Ranjita's account. This money was to be deposited in a few days. However, during this time the son told his mother that he was not able to focus on studies here. Asked not to deposit the fees. But Ranjita had already taken one lakh rupees from her husband. On her son's request, before the money could be deducted from the account, she had sent the money back to her husband's account. She kept only Rs 10,000 with herself. There was a family dispute over expenses for sister's wedding It is reported that the police officer's teacher sister's wedding was also fixed. All brothers were contributing money for the sister's wedding. However, officer Ajay was saying he would contribute less money considering his expenses. This matter was also causing disputes in the family. Wife asked - How did the bike end up near Kuano river According to the police complaint filed by Ranjita Gond, when she called the police station on February 6, she spoke to a constable. He informed that Ajay sir has been missing since last evening. After this, Ranjita informed her family members about this. Searched everywhere, but there was no trace of him anywhere. After this, on February 6, Daroga Ajay's bike was found at Amhat Ghat of Kuano river, 60 km away from the police station. The last location of his personal mobile and CUG number was also here. Ranjita also said that Ajay had received threats earlier during his posting at Dubauliya police station in a case involving the death of a minor child. The wife has also demanded investigation of the case from this angle. Now read what wife Ranjita Gond said... My husband SSI Ajay Kumar Gond was posted at Parashurampur police station. He went missing between 4 to 5 PM on February 5th. His bike that was found at Amhat Ghat was placed there to mislead the police. I suspect that my husband was held captive. He was in or around the police station area only, as he had not gone anywhere else. Someone trustworthy in this area has betrayed him. The most tragic thing is that I was not informed about his disappearance by the police station. The next day between 9 to 10 AM when I called him as usual, that's when I learned that he had been missing since the previous evening. When I asked the police station staff why they didn't track his location or call details, I didn't get any satisfactory answer. Three days of search, no clues found in Kuwano After finding Sub-Inspector Ajay's bike on February 6, police suspected he had drowned. Considering this, police conducted a continuous 3-day search operation in Kuwano river with SDRF Gorakhpur team. Eight rounds of motor boat searches were conducted in approximately 2 km area from Amhat Ghat to Bhadreshwarnath, but no clues were found. After this, the operation was stopped around 4 PM on February 8. News came from Ayodhya after 3 hours About 3 hours after the search operation ended, at 7 PM information was received that a body was spotted in the Saryu river in Tighura Majha village under Darshan Nagar police post area of Ayodhya. Ayodhya police reached the spot on information from villagers. The body was identified as that of Inspector Ajay Gond. Now read what ADM Arun Kumar, the younger brother of the inspector, said I have served as SDM and currently am an ADM. Despite this, I received no cooperation. I demand that the entire police station should be suspended. Murder case (Section 302) should be registered against 4 people and action should be taken against the CO of Harraiya. The way the CO spoke to me and tried to frame my brother, I will not tolerate it. This is not suicide, it's a planned murder. If needed, I will go to the Chief Minister, note this down. I don't want to talk to the Captain. Until my demands are met, I won't leave from here. My brother has died, not yours. I am in pain, a lot of pain. Inspector's father said - Kidnapping followed by murder Inspector Ajay Gond's father Ramchandra Prasad said that this incident happened on the 5th at 6 PM. We were informed about this by daughter-in-law Ranjita on 6th at 10 AM. It is still not clear what action the police is taking. We suspect that he was coming home alone on his bike from Parashurampur police station. He was kidnapped somewhere before that and then murdered. Police department, CO and SP were all in constant contact regarding this matter. In the family, younger brother is ADM, elder is supervisor Ajay Gond from Muradih village of Deoria was a 2016 batch police inspector. He got married to Ranjita in 2006. They have 2 sons Amit Raj and Utkarsh Raj. The elder son is studying in Kanpur, while his wife and younger son live with him in a rented house in Misraulia locality of Basti. Ajay's father is also a retired police inspector. Ajay was third among 4 siblings. Elder brother Dilip Kumar Gond works as a supervisor in the health department. Younger brother Arun Kumar Gond is an ADM. His sister Shashi Prabha is a government teacher. Shashi Prabha's marriage was fixed. Family members were busy with wedding preparations.

stories.title: Girl flees home leaving snake skin behind in Auraiya:Says ‘married my lover, don’t harass family’
stories.summary: In Auraiya, a young woman who ran away from home amid rumours of becoming a ‘nagin’ released a video on Thursday. She wore a yellow saree, with sindoor in her parting, a bindi on her forehead, and a mangalsutra around her neck. The woman said she married of her own choice and requested that no one harass her lover or his family. The video also shows her with her husband. The clip was posted via her partner’s Instagram account. The girl’s father had filed a case against unknown persons for allegedly luring her away. The police, taking the matter seriously, formed three teams to trace her. Authorities are using the Instagram ID to track her location. The incident falls under the Fafund police station area, village Seenganpur. Now know the full story... Rakesh Valmiki from Seenganpur village has five daughters and two sons. Four daughters are married. His youngest daughter, Rina (21), studied up to eighth grade at a local school and had a relationship with a village youth, Shyam Ji Sharma. Her family had arranged her marriage elsewhere, but she wanted to marry her lover. She planned her escape in a dramatic, film-like manner. On the night of February 10, she wrapped a snake skin in her clothes and left it on her bed before leaving home. When her family discovered it the next morning, rumours spread that she had become a ‘nagin’. Rina did not have her own phone and communicated using her mother’s keypad device. Police traced a number connected to a young man. Since the incident, the man’s family’s phones have been switched off and the house remains locked. Rina left a snake skin on her bed before fleeing Three months ago, she had visited the Sheshnag temple in Kumhel, Mainpuri, and brought back a Sheshnag idol. She frequently talked about seeing snakes in dreams and lying near them at night. Following her escape, crowds of relatives and villagers gathered at her home. Wedding video goes viral on Instagram On Thursday around 2 PM, Rina posted videos via her lover Shyam Ji Sharma’s Instagram account “Jai Mahakaal.” The first video was 11 seconds, the second 34 seconds long. In the first video, Reena is with her lover. She is saying that I am married, this is my husband, if anything happens to his family members, my family members will be blamed. In the second video, she is saying I got married of my own free will. It was my wish to marry him only. I myself told him that we will get married today. I myself forced for the marriage. These are his photos. You can see. I have married of my own will. No one else is involved in this. Please don't torture anyone, this is all I want. Police said - Location is being traced Station in-charge Ajay Kumar said- Three teams have been formed to search for the young woman. Attempts are being made to trace the location through Instagram ID and mobile number with the help of surveillance. Investigation of the case is ongoing.

stories.title: 'Muslims cannot sing Vande Mataram':Maulana Madani in Saharanpur says forcing it violates Constitution, not patriotism but politics
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, the organization’s president Maulana Arshad Madani said Muslims do not prevent anyone from singing or playing Vande Mataram, but some verses depict the motherland as a deity. “We cannot sing this song because we worship only Allah. Including anyone else in our worship goes against our beliefs. Making Vande Mataram mandatory is a direct attack on the spirit of the Constitution, religious freedom, and democratic values,” he said. On social media platform X, he added that forcing a Muslim to sing the song violates Article 25 of the Constitution and multiple Supreme Court rulings. Mandating the song is not a demonstration of patriotism but a political, communal agenda aimed at diverting attention from core issues. The central government on Thursday issued an order making it mandatory to give Vande Mataram the same respect as the national anthem, “Jana Gana Mana.” All six stanzas of the song, totaling 3 minutes and 10 seconds, are to be sung, whereas previously only the first two stanzas were performed. Maulana Madani’s key points: True patriotism shown through sacrifice Love for the nation is measured not in slogans but through deeds and sacrifice. Historic examples of Muslim participation and Jamiyat Ulema-e-Hind’s struggles illustrate this. Such orders weaken peace, unity, democratic values, and the spirit of the Constitution. Direct attack on democratic principles Making Vande Mataram mandatory is an open attack on the Constitution, religious freedom, and democratic principles. One stanza addresses the nation as Goddess Durga, using worship words that conflict with Muslim religious beliefs. No certificate needed to prove patriotism The Supreme Court has ruled that no citizen can be forced to sing the national song or anthem against their religious beliefs. Patriotism and worship are separate. Muslims do not need any certificate to prove their love for the country. Muslim contribution to independence Jamiyat leaders played a key role in opposing the Partition. Post-independence, their efforts to maintain the nation’s unity remain significant. According to Madani, the government deliberately raises such controversies to distract from inflation, unemployment, and other core issues, which is not patriotism but politics to retain power. Decision to sing only two stanzas historically Citing historical records, Madani noted that on 26 October 1937, Rabindranath Tagore advised Jawaharlal Nehru to accept only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram as the national song, as the remaining lines conflicted with monotheistic beliefs. The Congress Working Committee agreed on 19 October 1937, and Parliament discussions reinforced this view. The current attempt seeks to make the entire song compulsory. Standing protocol for Vande Mataram New guidelines require everyone to stand during Vande Mataram at official events, schools, and formal occasions. The order was issued on 28 January, reported in media on 11 February. PTI reports that when Vande Mataram and Jana Gana Mana are performed together, Vande Mataram comes first, with all present standing at attention. While a complete list of occasions is not specified, it is the first time detailed protocol has been issued. Occasions include presidential arrival, flag hoisting The song will be mandatory at flag hoisting, presidential and gubernatorial arrivals, speeches, and other official ceremonies. It can also be sung collectively at non-formal events with ministers or key dignitaries, provided respect and decorum are maintained. Civilian award ceremonies, including Padma awards, with presidential presence, will also feature Vande Mataram. Parade tableau at Republic Day 2026 Delhi’s Kartavya Path hosted the 77th Republic Day parade with Vande Mataram as the theme. The Culture Ministry presented a tableau celebrating the song’s 150th anniversary, winning the Best Tableau award. The tableau included Tagore’s composition, colonial-era recordings by a famous Marathi singer, and a Gen Z group performing the song. The lower panel displayed Tagore’s image, and the central section featured performers in traditional attire representing India’s cultural diversity.

'Police weak, education ruined, market sold to America':Akhilesh Yadav slams BJP; flags Agra neglect, budget failures claims
stories.summary: SP president Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the BJP government, alleging deterioration of policing, education, and the economy in Uttar Pradesh, while accusing the Centre of “handing over the Indian market to America”. Akhilesh Yadav arrived in Agra on Thursday evening to attend a wedding ceremony, where he was accorded a grand welcome by party workers. Speaking to journalists, the Samajwadi Party chief raised concerns over the Union and state budgets, civic neglect in Agra, and what he described as the BJP’s failure on governance fronts. He alleged that the condition of the police in Uttar Pradesh has worsened and took a swipe at the Chief Minister, saying, “In UP, the palm is hot and the police are soft.” He further criticised the state of infrastructure, traffic congestion, and garbage disposal in Agra, including the lack of arrangements for the upkeep of the Taj Mahal. Five major statements by Akhilesh Yadav 1. No relief for Agra’s shoe industry Akhilesh said the recently announced Delhi and Lucknow budgets had ignored the common man. He claimed Agra’s shoe industry received no relief despite repeated demands. He also alleged that there was no effective budgetary provision for cleaning the Yamuna river. “The Yamuna remains as it was. It could not even be cleaned,” he said. 2. Tourism can make Agra a trillion-rupee economy Calling Agra a city with immense tourism potential, Akhilesh said it could contribute trillions to the economy if developed properly. Despite being listed under the Smart Cities programme, he claimed roads remain broken, drains are open, garbage is scattered, and traffic congestion has made life difficult for residents. He added that during winters, Agra’s AQI often matches Delhi’s levels, yet the government has failed to provide relief on pollution, employment, or inflation. He accused the BJP of encouraging land mafias and favouring select individuals in development projects and cleaning tenders. 3. ‘Entire market handed over to America’ The SP chief alleged that secret deals between the BJP-led Centre and the United States would benefit the rich while harming the poor. “The deal with America suggests we have handed over our entire market,” he said, adding that the government must clarify which agricultural products will be imported. He also questioned the relief given to potato farmers in Agra and criticised rising electricity costs and poor health services. 4. BJP following ‘divide and rule’ policy Referring to the PDA (Picchda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) alliance, Akhilesh said the BJP was unsettled and resorting to “divide and rule”, a policy he compared to British colonial tactics. He claimed that most development in Agra, including the Metro and areas around the Taj Mahal, was done during Samajwadi Party governments. He alleged that the BJP had merely renamed the Mughal Museum to the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum, while facilities such as air conditioning there had deteriorated. 5. Education system ruined in a decade Akhilesh said that despite a combined education budget of nearly ₹1 lakh crore for primary and secondary education, the BJP government had “ruined” the education system over the past ten years. He alleged school closures, declining education quality, and ineffective skill development programmes. He also claimed the government has failed to provide even clean drinking water to Agra residents.

stories.title: Doctor drives around Prayagraj with woman’s body:Alleged death from wrong injection, she was three months pregnant
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, a doctor drove around the city for two hours with the body of a woman. The family was not informed about her death. She was three months pregnant. The relatives alleged that the woman died after the doctor administered the wrong injection. Initially, the doctor claimed that the woman had fainted and that she was being taken to another hospital for treatment. Instead, the body was placed in a car and driven around the city for nearly two hours. When the family became suspicious, they tracked the car and followed it. When the relatives reached the vehicle, they discovered the woman’s body inside. The car was then taken directly to the police outpost, at which point the doctor abandoned the car and fled. The family refused to retrieve the body for five hours. The incident occurred in the Phulpur police station area. The complete matter in detail... The incident took place at Dr. Sukhdev’s clinic in Narai village, Phulpur. The clinic is run by Dr. Sukhdev, his wife Dr. Meera, their daughter Dr. Deep Shikha, and her husband Dr. Subhashchandra, all of whom treat patients. Angura Devi (25) from the nearby village of Ata, who was three months pregnant, visited the clinic with her husband Rajaram. Rajaram said his wife was experiencing abdominal pain on Wednesday evening. With no one at home, she went alone to the clinic to get medicine. The doctors examined her and allegedly administered the wrong injection. Around 7:30 pm, Angura died after the injection. Dr. Meera then called Rajaram, claiming that Angura had fainted and that they were taking her to another hospital. Doctor couple fled leaving body in car Rajaram stated that upon learning of the situation, he rushed to the clinic. On arrival, he found Angura missing. When questioned, he was informed that Dr. Meera and her husband, Dr. Subhash, had taken her away in a car. Following phone communication, the family drove to intercept them. Around 10 pm, near the Rahimapur intersection, they caught up with the car and discovered Angura’s lifeless body inside. The family brought the doctor to the Phulpur police outpost, where the commotion continued until 11 pm. During this time, Dr. Deep Shikha and her husband left the car and escaped. After the incident, angry relatives caused a further commotion while transporting the body to the village. The body remained in the car, leading to renewed protests in the morning. Police officers arrived at the scene and eventually took custody of the body. The family filed a formal complaint against the doctors, and statements were recorded. Sanjay Kumar, the woman’s father, said that the body was found in a car near Rahimapur intersection. “We were informed by the clinic that our daughter’s condition had suddenly worsened and that she was being taken to the city. Upon hearing this, we went searching for her. Two to three hours later, we found her body in a car near Rahimapur intersection,” he said.

stories.title: Man trapped in pit for 12 hours dies:Bike fell into waterlogged ditch; no streetlights at accident spot, say police
stories.summary: A 25-year-old man died after remaining trapped for nearly 12 hours in a muddy pit along the Aroura-Shivli road in Kanpur Dehat district. The incident occurred on Tuesday evening, but came to light on Thursday after a video surfaced. The victim, identified as Dhirendra Kumar (25), a resident of Bhawanipur village under Rasulabad police station limits, worked as a welder at Panki Power House. Fell into waterlogged pit with bike According to family members, Dhirendra left for home on his motorcycle around 6 pm on Tuesday but did not return. Unbeknownst to anyone, his bike had skidded off the road near Kadari village and plunged into a deep, muddy pit allegedly dug for pipeline work. He remained trapped in the sludge throughout the cold night, reportedly crying out for help, but no one noticed him. See pictures of the incident Farmers spot him in the morning Around 6 am on Wednesday, farmers heading to their fields spotted him in the pit and alerted the village head. Village pradhan Ankush Kumar, Vijay Kumar and other locals pulled him out of the mud. At the time of rescue, he was still breathing. Villagers cleaned his face, poured water on him and lit a fire using straw to warm his cold, stiff body. When he showed no signs of improvement, they called a 102 ambulance and rushed him to Shivli Community Health Centre. Doctors, however, declared him dead on arrival. Congress wrote on X - Dhirendra fell victim to the system's negligence Family informed by police Dhirendra’s brother, Brijendra Kumar, said the family was informed by police the next morning about the accident. When they reached the hospital, they found him dead. No streetlights at accident spot Shivli Kotwali in-charge Praveen Yadav said preliminary investigation suggests that the motorcycle went out of control and fell into the pit, which was significantly below road level and not visible in the dark. “There are no streetlights on the Rura-Shivli route, leading to frequent accidents in the area,” he said.

No privilege motion against Rahul Gandhi, BJP MP moves notice seeking LoP’s disqualification The Centre will not move a privilege motion against Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, though the words used in his speech delivered on Wednesday are likely to be expunged, sources said. This comes a day after Union Minister Kiren Rijiju said that BJP members in the Lok Sabha would move a privilege notice against Rahul Gandhi for "misleading the House and making baseless statements." 2. The explosion, which took place on 10 November 2025, killed 15 people. The National Investigation Agency is leading the probe and had earlier described the network behind the attack as a white-collar terror module. 5. 'Judge sir, I want my husband back':Actor Pawan Singh's wife Jyoti Singh breaks down in court “Judge sir, it has been seven years since my marriage. stories.title: Jamal posed as Rahul to run sex racket:Victims say he promised jobs, filmed obscene clips and coerced them
stories.summary: Jalaluddin alias Changur Baba may be in jail in an illegal conversion case, but his associates are still active, according to allegations. One such aide is said to be operating a spa centre and a girls’ café in Lucknow. He allegedly brought women from districts across Uttar Pradesh and from Delhi on the pretext of jobs and friendship. At the café, he is accused of giving them intoxicants and filming explicit videos while they were drugged. The videos were then allegedly used to blackmail them and force them into prostitution in the name of “service”, compelling them to continue. On Wednesday (11 February), one of the women approached a police station. Soon after, several others arrived. Members of Hindu organisations and social workers also reached the station, after which the matter surfaced. After receiving information, Dainik Bhaskar reached the location, spoke to victims, the NGO operator who helped them, and an eyewitness who claimed he saw Changur Baba’s photograph inside the café and spa. The women alleged the operator used coded phrases such as “Screenshot sent, send the goods.” What the women said… Got café job as part-time work A woman from Amethi said she came to Lucknow to prepare for UP Police recruitment and was searching for part-time work. During this time she met two men, Rahul and Qamar Hayat Idrisi, who arranged a job for her at Brown Girl Café. She said she became close to Rahul. She alleged Rahul used to call her to his room. One day he gave her beer and recorded an objectionable video while she was intoxicated. He then allegedly blackmailed her by threatening to make the video viral. Made nude videos after giving intoxicants A Delhi woman said she was a minor four years ago and was looking for work due to financial problems. While searching online she came into contact with Rahul. She alleged he took her from Delhi to Ajmer and then to Lucknow, where he kept her at different locations before arranging work for her at a spa centre. She said he told her the job involved only calling and entry work, but after starting she discovered prostitution was taking place there. She alleged that one day he mixed an intoxicant in her drink, filmed a nude video while she was unconscious, and then threatened to release it, forcing her into sexual acts. Rescuer’s account… Girls came to study or work, lost contact with families Risha Tufail, who runs an NGO that rescues women from such situations, said they had been visiting the police station for four days. Three months ago, families of two or three girls reported their daughters had gone out to study but their phones were switched off. They were not answering calls or speaking to relatives. Acting on the families’ information, she said they visited Brown Girl Café, sat inside and observed the environment, where they allegedly found coded communication. For instance, after sending a girl’s photo, they would say, “Screenshot sent, send the goods.” Boy entered after girl, behaved obscenely and left Risha said a girl entered the café carrying a bag with a flight sticker. Shortly after, a boy entered and behaved obscenely with her inside. When they left, two more girls joined them and all four departed together. She said she took two girls to the police station, after which police went to raid the spa centre and Brown Girl Café. However, the accused had already been alerted and fled after locking the premises. Police are searching for them. Accused posed as Hindu to trap women Risha alleged that after everyone left, they inquired about the operator known as Rahul and found his real name to be Kamru Jamal. She said he had several photos dressed as a devotee of Lord Shiva and showed girls selfies taken near Shiva temples. By presenting himself as a Hindu, he allegedly gained their trust. She claimed he brought girls from Bihar, Delhi, Jharkhand and other places and forced them into sexual acts. His associate Qamar Hayat Idrisi is also accused of exploiting women after intoxicating them. Both allegedly threatened to send videos to victims’ families. A photograph of Changur Baba was also displayed in the spa, and they were described as his followers.

stories.title: UP to form dedicated OBC panel before panchayat polls:Government files affidavit in HC; reservation only after survey report
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has informed the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court that it will constitute a dedicated Other Backward Classes (OBC) Commission ahead of the upcoming panchayat elections, in line with Supreme Court guidelines. The assurance was given through an affidavit during the hearing of a petition challenging the powers of the existing Backward Classes Commission. A Division Bench of Justice Rajan Roy and Justice Avadhesh Choudhary was hearing the matter. The State told the court that reservation of seats in panchayats would be determined on the basis of the report submitted by the proposed dedicated commission. It said the move was necessary to comply with Supreme Court directions, which make it mandatory to have a dedicated commission before conducting local body elections. In the previous panchayat elections, a commission headed by a retired High Court judge had been constituted following court orders. Reservations were finalised on the basis of its report, after which the elections were conducted. The next round of panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh is proposed between April and July. Challenge to existing commission The petition questioning the authority of the current Backward Classes Commission was filed after its original tenure ended in October 2025. The State government subsequently extended the commission’s term till October 2026. Counsel for the petitioner, Moti Lal Yadav, argued that the existing commission does not have the legal authority to conduct a survey. He submitted that had the commission’s original three-year tenure not expired, it could have undertaken the reservation-related survey. The proposed dedicated commission will now conduct a rapid survey of backward classes across the State. The survey is intended to assess the actual population of OBCs, on the basis of which panchayat seat reservations will be determined. Polls after report Referring to Supreme Court guidelines, the government’s counsel said that panchayat or local body elections can be held only after a Backward Classes Commission with a three-year tenure, or a dedicated commission, submits its report. The State government made it clear that the dates for the panchayat elections would be announced only after the final report of the dedicated commission is received. According to the government, the exercise would ensure transparency and legal certainty in the reservation process. Reservation-related disputes have repeatedly led to legal hurdles in the past. Officials believe that the constitution of a dedicated commission would significantly reduce the scope for such challenges and help ensure the smooth conduct of the panchayat elections.

stories.title: Yashveer Maharaj tells Hindus to do 'love jihad':Says bring 25–30 Muslim girls for one Hindu girl in return
stories.summary: In Baghpat on Thursday, Yashveer Maharaj said that if someone takes away one Hindu daughter through “love jihad”, people should not stop chasing them. He said they should keep fighting until the girl is brought back. He added that in return for one daughter, bring 25–30 of theirs. When that happens, no so-called “love jihadi” will dare to look at Hindu daughters or sisters, because, according to him, there is no affection without fear. Yashveer Maharaj made these remarks at a large Hindu gathering. He often remains in the news because of his statements. He runs a Yoga Sadhana Ashram in Muzaffarnagar. In 2024, he had sat on a protest demanding that shopkeepers on the Kanwar Yatra route in Muzaffarnagar display name plates. Later, the government issued an order making name plates mandatory, but the Supreme Court subsequently stayed that order. ‘Hindus should also do love jihad’ Yashveer Maharaj said Hindus should also carry out “love jihad”. If a Hindu girl goes to another religion, every effort should be made to bring her back. He said if their daughters are brought, they should be treated with such respect that they willingly leave the burqa and come here. Bring their daughters, but don’t mistreat them He said bring their daughters but do not harass them. Treat them so respectfully that they themselves say they want to come to Sanatan. If they want to leave the burqa, come here; if they want freedom from halala, come here. He added that even if a girl has a speech defect, bring her — she too will be accepted and will praise Sanatan. Remove police from Hyderabad and we will show you Referring to a past remark attributed to Akbaruddin Owaisi about removing police for 15 minutes, Yashveer said that in Muzaffarnagar when police were removed for 15 minutes, hundreds gathered in religious camps. He said try removing police from Hyderabad for 15 minutes and Hindus will march there. He added that this country does not belong to mullahs and clerics but to Veer Shivaji. Who is Yashveer Maharaj… Swami Yashveer runs the ‘Yoga Sadhana Ashram’ in Baghra village, about 15 km from Muzaffarnagar. The ashram was established in 2015. It also has the Mahant Avaidyanath Bhavan, whose foundation stone was laid by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath when he was the MP from Gorakhpur. Last year, Yashveer claimed that a dhaba named “Pandit Dhaba” in Muzaffarnagar was owned by a Muslim and that staff names there had been changed. After that, he announced he would place pictures of Lord Varaha and saffron flags at hotels and dhabas along the Kanwar Yatra route up to Haridwar. He later reached the Narsan border on the Uttar Pradesh–Uttarakhand boundary with supporters, but Uttarakhand Police stopped him. In protest, he sat on a dharna on the highway.

stories.title: Judicial probe into ‘half encounters’:Deoband magistrate questions injured inmates in jail; prisoners allege staged shootings
stories.summary: Amid continuing scrutiny of police encounters in Uttar Pradesh, a magistrate court in Deoband has taken the unusual step of directly examining inmates who were injured in alleged “half encounters”, following sharp observations by the Allahabad High Court on encounter practices. Within a week of the High Court’s remarks, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Parvinder Singh visited Deoband Jail and questioned prisoners who had sustained gunshot injuries during police actions. The inmates were asked to stand in a line as the magistrate interacted with them individually. According to a video of the visit that has since surfaced, one prisoner alleged that he was picked up by the police while on his way to court for a scheduled hearing in a case pending against him, and was later shown as injured in a staged “half encounter”. The development comes days after the Allahabad High Court made strong observations on the need for accountability and transparency in police encounter cases, a subject that has repeatedly drawn judicial attention in the State. Read the conversation between ACJM and injured prisoner ACGM: How was the shot fired? Prisoner: We had a court date in Saharanpur. We were coming from Baghpat. As soon as we reached Shamli Park, the police picked us up. They took us to the police post. There I was given electric shocks. They made us confess, but I didn't confess. After that, in the evening they took us to the jungle and also brought a bike from the police station. That's where I was shot in the leg. ACGM: Where were you shot? Prisoner: Below the leg. ACGM: Please explain everything in detail? Prisoner: First we were made to lie on the ground, legs were lowered and cloth was placed on top. Then shots were fired from about 8 inches above. After that firing was done with a country-made pistol. ACGM: Did you fire yourself? Prisoner: Yes. ACGM (to second youth): Did this happen to you too? Second youth: (showing his legs) Yes. Now read what the Allahabad High Court said about the encounter? UP Police doing half encounters for promotion On January 30, the Allahabad High Court expressed strong displeasure over UP Police's 'half encounter' method. The court said that police officers were unnecessarily firing bullets just for praise, early promotion and social media appreciation. The High Court had issued guidelines on 6 points. Justice Arun Kumar Deshwal's bench had given a clear warning. If police do not follow Supreme Court guidelines in encounters, the district's SP-SSP and Commissioner will be personally held guilty of contempt of court. Court said - Punishing accused is not police's job High Court had said - Only judiciary has the right to punish the accused, not the police. India is a democratic country. Here the law works according to the constitution, not based on personal thinking. The court had also said that in many cases police officers deliberately shoot below the knee in the accused's leg. So that the case can be called a 'half encounter' and they can take credit for bravery. In the eyes of law, this method is completely unacceptable. The court gave this strict order while accepting a bail petition of an accused. Supreme Court also expressed displeasure over ignoring PUCL guidelines High Court said - Supreme Court has made guidelines in PUCL (People's Union for Civil Liberties) vs State of Maharashtra (2014) case. Despite this, UP police is repeatedly ignoring these rules. The court had clearly stated that police cannot be allowed to take law into their hands for praise or rewards. stories.title: Wrestling jibe in UP Assembly:Khanna tells SP MLA to fight minister; Ragini–Nandi clash sparks uproar
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Legislature’s budget session entered its fourth day on Wednesday. In the Legislative Council, Deputy Chief Minister Brijesh Pathak lashed out at Samajwadi Party MLC Ashutosh Sinha. Pathak said, “It is not his fault; this is the culture of his leader.” He added, “Hospitals do not run on buildings alone. They committed wrongdoing. I am using the word ‘wrongdoing’ because when they build hospitals, they give the contracts to their own relatives. They constructed buildings only to loot money.” The Deputy CM also narrated an anecdote to drive home his point. He said: “In our village, when a buffalo’s calf dies, people make a dummy to extract milk. But these people put a cow’s calf in front of a buffalo and still try to extract milk.” Samajwadi Party MLC Ashutosh Sinha said that a medical college was built in Kannauj. He stated that the hospital building was completed in 2016, but it has not become operational even after several years. He questioned why the government was adopting a “double standard” on the issue. Deputy Chief Minister Brijesh Pathak reacted sharply to Sinha’s remarks, leading to heated exchanges in the Council. Uproar in the Assembly during Question Hour Meanwhile, the Legislative Assembly witnessed disorder during Question Hour. Minister Nand Gopal Nandi rose to respond to questions raised by SP MLA Ragini Sonkar, but began by reading out her own question. Speaker Satish Mahana intervened and asked him to stick to the reply. The minister made a metaphor-laden remark while responding, which angered Ragini Sonkar. As the exchange escalated, the Speaker again intervened and asked the minister to give a direct answer. The minister then shifted to talking about the investors’ summit, prompting Mahana to point out that the details were already on record. The minister went on to criticise the Samajwadi Party, saying its politics begins on Instagram reels and ends on Facebook. This led to further uproar. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna later stood up and replied to the questions. ‘Everyone has taken to poetry now’ SP MLA from Chitrakoot Anil Pradhan raised issues related to farmers and recited a poem in the House. Reacting to this, Speaker Satish Mahana remarked that “nowadays, everyone seems to have developed a taste for poetry”. Minister Dinesh Pratap Singh loses temper Minister Dinesh Pratap Singh lost his temper while responding to a question by SP MLA R K Verma. He said the government had worked on agriculture-related schemes in every Assembly constituency. When SP MLAs protested, he said that merely saying “no, no” would not work and claimed he had documents to prove the government’s work. He thumped his chest and said that even if the opposition was not concerned about the public, the government certainly was. Law and order debate SP MLA Ragini Sonkar later criticised the state’s law and order situation, alleging that women, youth, unemployed people and farmers had become the “targets” of the government. She referred to an incident in Prayagraj in which four youths from the Khatik community were killed, questioning the police version of events and raising concerns over custodial deaths in Uttar Pradesh. SP MLA Atul Pradhan also raised issues related to alleged police excesses in Meerut and Sardhana, claiming promises of compensation and land had not been fulfilled. Replying to these points, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna said NCRB data showed a decline in crime in the state. He said the deaths of the four youths in Prayagraj were due to drowning, that an FIR had been registered, and that financial assistance and housing support had been provided to their families. He added that action had been taken in the Meerut case as per rules. Debate on sports spending During a discussion on sports, SP MLA Kamal Akhtar remarked that someone who had never even played traditional games had been made Sports Minister, triggering laughter in the House. Sports Minister Girish Yadav responded by saying he had been active in sports, while Finance Minister Suresh Khanna joked about organising a wrestling bout, prompting the Speaker to intervene. SP MLA Sachin Yadav later pointed out that while a sports budget of ₹980 crore had been proposed for 2025–26, only ₹185 crore had been spent, questioning how athletes could be developed with such low utilisation. Fresh clash over Kannauj medical college Earlier, Ashutosh Sinha had said that despite buildings being ready, patients were being forced to go elsewhere for cancer and heart treatment as the Kannauj medical college was not functioning. In reply, Brijesh Pathak alleged that only buildings were constructed earlier without proper planning, and that doctors were not appointed. He accused the previous government of corruption in awarding contracts, triggering strong protests from SP members, who demanded certain remarks be expunged from the record. The exchange ended amid loud sloganeering and repeated interventions by the Chair.

stories.title: 'Judge sir, I want my husband back':Actor Pawan Singh's wife Jyoti Singh breaks down in court, seeks ₹10 crore as maintenance
stories.summary: “Judge sir, it has been seven years since my marriage. Till today, I have received neither my husband’s love nor money for my maintenance. I want to live with my husband. If he does not want to live together, then I should be given ₹10 crore as maintenance.” This was stated by Jyoti Singh, wife of Bhojpuri actor Pawan Singh, during a hearing at the Family Court in Arrah Civil Court. The details were shared by her lawyer Vishnudhar Pandey while speaking to Bhaskar. The case relates to divorce proceedings in which the court is currently focusing on reconciliation, giving both sides a chance to resolve their differences through mutual consent. Jyoti Singh reaches court, Pawan Singh absent Jyoti Singh reached Ara Civil Court on Wednesday for the hearing. She waited at the court for some time for Pawan Singh, but he did not arrive. After waiting, she left the court visibly emotional. Jyoti appeared in court wearing sindoor, indicating that she still considers herself married. “I want to live only with my husband” According to lawyer Vishnudhar Pandey, Jyoti Singh clearly told the judge that she wanted to live with her husband and was seeking reconciliation. She told the court that at every hearing she only gets the next date. Despite appearing personally each time, she said her husband neither reaches court on time nor takes any clear decision. The hearing was scheduled at Vikramganj Court, but Pawan Singh did not appear. Jyoti told the judge that if he wanted, he could have come, but her silence and suffering continued to be ignored. “Seven years of marriage, only pain” During the hearing, Jyoti Singh broke down and told the judge that in seven years of marriage she had only faced mental stress and uncertainty. She said she did not receive emotional support, financial help, or her rights as a wife. Each visit to court was made with hope for reconciliation or a clear decision, but she was left waiting every time. Folding her hands, Jyoti Singh made one request to the court: “My Lord, I only want justice.” Lawyer says Pawan Singh unwell Lawyer Vishnudhar Pandey said the Family Court had directed both parties to be present as part of reconciliation efforts. Jyoti Singh appeared, but Pawan Singh did not. Pawan Singh’s lawyer informed the court that he was unwell and that his blood pressure had increased. The court was told that he was admitted to a hospital, though details of the hospital were not shared. Through a video call, one of his associates showed him lying on a hospital bed. The lawyer added that Jyoti Singh’s wish to live with her husband could not be discussed in detail in open court. No maintenance for past 4–5 years Jyoti Singh’s lawyer said that for the last four to five years, she has not received any maintenance or regular expenses from her husband. Even the application filed for interim maintenance has not seen any concrete progress so far. The lawyer requested the court to ensure that Jyoti Singh is granted maintenance and necessary expenses. The judge stated that the court would first examine the possibility of reconciliation. Only after that would it decide on maintenance and related financial matters. Next hearing on February 24 Vishnudhar Pandey alleged that Pawan Singh was avoiding facing his wife in court. He said it would be seen on February 24 whether Pawan Singh appears or comes up with another reason for absence. “I can’t work or move freely,” says Jyoti Singh Jyoti Singh told the court that it has been seven years since her marriage and she is unable to work or move freely. Wherever she goes, people gather to see her because she is known as Pawan Singh’s wife. She said that in Jharkhand, Bihar, Purvanchal and other regions, people recognise her, which creates difficulties even when she tries to work in private companies. Jyoti Singh mentally exhausted, says lawyer Speaking to Bhaskar, Vishnudhar Pandey said Jyoti Singh is mentally exhausted and was crying continuously in court. He said seven years have passed, but she still hopes for justice. He added that earlier, both parties were absent on two hearing dates. On February 24, the court will speak directly to both Jyoti Singh and Pawan Singh to understand the dispute and explore whether reconciliation is possible. If reconciliation fails, the divorce process will move forward, and a decision may come within four to five months. Background of the case Pawan Singh’s first wife Neelam Singh died by suicide in 2015. Later, his name was linked with Bhojpuri actress Akshara Singh. Pawan Singh married Jyoti Singh, daughter of Rambabu Singh from Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh, on March 7, 2018, in a grand ceremony at a hotel in Ballia. However, the marriage soon ran into trouble. Serious allegations made by Jyoti Singh In a written application to the court, Jyoti Singh has made serious allegations against her husband. She claimed that within a month of marriage, Pawan Singh would consume alcohol, verbally and physically abuse her, and subject her to continuous harassment. She also alleged that she was forced to undergo abortion twice. According to the application, Jyoti Singh has been living at her parental home in Ballia since two months after the marriage. She has sought interim maintenance from the Family Court.

stories.title: Stormy scenes mark 4th day of UP budget session:Dy CM, ministers clash with SP members over hospitals, crime record and sports
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh legislature’s budget session witnessed heated exchanges on its fourth day, with sharp confrontations between the ruling BJP and the Samajwadi Party (SP) in both the Legislative Council and the Assembly. Deputy CM hits out at SP MLC In the Legislative Council, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak lashed out at SP MLC Ashutosh Sinha during a debate over a medical college in Kannauj. Sinha claimed that the hospital building was constructed in 2016 but has not been made operational, questioning the government’s approach. Responding angrily, Pathak said running a hospital required more than constructing a building. He alleged irregularities, claiming contracts were handed to relatives and that public money was misused. He accused the previous regime of building structures without ensuring proper functioning. Uproar during Question Hour In the Assembly, chaos erupted during Question Hour when Minister Nand Gopal Nandi rose to answer SP MLA Ragini Sonkar’s query. He initially began reading from her question, prompting Speaker Satish Mahana to intervene. An exchange followed, with the minister making remarks that triggered objections from Sonkar. The Speaker repeatedly asked the minister to confine himself to the question. As tempers flared, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna eventually intervened and addressed the queries. Minister Dinesh Pratap Singh reacts sharply Another heated moment came when Minister Dinesh Pratap Singh responded to SP MLA RK Verma on agricultural schemes. Amid protests from SP members, the minister asserted that development work had been undertaken in every constituency. He challenged opposition members to verify the data, stating that the government had documentary proof of expenditure and implementation. The remarks led to further sloganeering inside the House. Debate over sports budget allocation SP MLA Engineer Sachin Yadav questioned the utilisation of the sports budget. He said that while Rs 980 crore was proposed for 2025–26, only Rs 185 crore had been spent. He also pointed out zero allocations for several facilities, including Fatehpur Sports College, Kannauj sports ground, hostels at Green Park in Kanpur, Saifai Stadium and a swimming pool in Prayagraj. He added that sports colleges lack permanent trainers and cited Haryana’s superior medal tally in the Khelo India Youth Games despite Uttar Pradesh being much larger. Crime record and political sparring SP MLC Mukul Yadav raised issues concerning religious sentiments, while BJP leader Swatantra Dev Singh countered by claiming a decline in serious crime since 2017. He said no major riots had occurred in the state after the BJP came to power. An SP member retorted that if those responsible for riots were now in the ruling party, unrest would naturally decline. The exchange led to further disruption, after which SP members staged a walkout.

stories.title: Mother-in-law who marries son-in-law in Aligarh reaches police station:Says she wants to live life her own way after eloping with brother-in-law
stories.summary: In a very strange development from Aligarh, the woman who left her husband and eloped with her daughter’s would-be groom just 10 days before the wedding is back in the spotlight. Nearly ten months after the incident first surfaced, the case has taken a fresh turn. On Wednesday, the son-in-law, who is now legally her husband, approached the police station with a complaint. He alleged that his wife had run away with her brother-in-law. However, the police termed it a matter linked to Bihar and sent him back. After the complaint surfaced, the woman arrived at the police station on Thursday, covering her face with a veil. She dismissed the allegations of eloping with her brother-in-law as false. She admitted that deciding to live with her son-in-law was a mistake and said she now wants to live life on her own terms. Thirty-eight-year-old Anita Devi first made headlines when she disappeared on April 6, 2025. Police traced and detained her on April 18. Counselling was conducted at the police station, but instead of returning to her husband, she chose to go with Rahul, her daughter’s would-be groom. She had been living with him since then. Son-in-law says mother-in-law cheated him, read the complaint in full Son-in-law Rahul submitted a complaint at Dado police station on Wednesday. In his application, he stated that he travels to Bihar to sell clothes through door-to-door vending. Around 15 days ago, his wife reconnected with her brother-in-law. He claimed to have listened to an audio recording of their phone conversation. According to Rahul, the audio clip reveals that the two were planning to live together. He alleged that they had even conspired to poison him and flee. On February 6, his wife, who is also his former mother-in-law, betrayed him and left with her brother-in-law. He further claimed that she took Rs 2 lakh in cash and jewellery with her, and demanded that the police trace and arrest her. Woman appears, says her decision proved wrong After the matter surfaced in the media, the woman reached the police station on Thursday. She admitted that she had left her children and gone with her son-in-law, a decision she now deeply regrets. She said her choice had turned out to be wrong. She alleged that Rahul threatened and harassed her and was involved in trafficking women. She said she now wants to live separately from Rahul and earn her livelihood through labour work. She wishes to stay close to her children, but alleged that Rahul has stopped her from meeting them. She accused him of assaulting her and taking away her jewellery and cash, following which she decided to leave him. The one-year-old elopement story with son-in-law in three points 1) Eloped with son-in-law 10 days before daughter’s wedding Anita’s first husband is Jitendra Kumar, and their daughter Shivani lives in Manoharpur Kayasth village under Madraak police station limits. Jitendra had fixed Shivani’s marriage with Rahul, a resident of Riya Nagla village under Dado police station area, for April 16, 2025. Rahul worked as a supervisor in a private company in Rudrapur, Uttarakhand. Ten days before the wedding, on April 6, 2025, Shivani’s mother Anita suddenly went missing from home. Around the same time, Rahul left his house saying he was going to buy clothes, but did not return. After leaving Aligarh, both switched off their mobile phones. 2) Surrendered at police station after FIR was filed Family members searched extensively but found no trace of the two. Five days later, Rahul called his father and told him not to look for him as he would not return. It was then that his family realised that his would-be mother-in-law was also missing. The families lodged a complaint with the police. Teams conducted raids in Bihar and several other states as part of the search operation. On April 18, both appeared at Dado police station and surrendered. Police took them into custody and questioned them. 3) Refused to return to husband, began living with son-in-law During questioning, it emerged that the two had travelled nearly 2,826 kilometres over 10 days. Apart from Uttar Pradesh, they had hidden in Nepal, Delhi and Bihar. Counselling sessions lasting four hours were conducted at the police station. The woman was advised to return to her husband, but she clearly refused. Anita said she had been suppressing her wishes for 20 years and was often mistreated. Unable to tolerate it any longer, she left home. She stated that she did not want to go back to her husband. After this, police released both of them. Since then, she had been living with her son-in-law. First husband remarries, daughter’s wedding still not fixed Anita’s first husband, Jeetu, remarried a month ago. However, their daughter’s marriage has still not been finalised. The daughter has said that they have completely cut off ties with Anita and do not wish to receive any information about her anymore.

stories.title: Woman flees with jewelry worth ₹65 lakhs in shawl:Husband steals from jeweler's safe in Jhansi gives to his wife, says, 'Wanted to be rich man'
stories.summary: A young man who had been working at a jewelry shop in Jhansi for 18 years stole jewelry worth ₹65 lakhs and ₹3.10 lakhs cash. After the theft, he called his wife and handed over all the stolen goods to her. His wife concealed the jewelry and cash in a shawl and took it away. When the jewelry shop owner opened the safe, the jewelry and cash were missing. The young man was present at home, so the owner did not suspect him. Police also questioned the young man based on suspicion, to which he said - "You can ask my owner. It's been 18 years, I've never stolen even 10 rupees." Then the police let him go. After this, police scanned CCTV cameras installed around the house. In the footage, a woman was seen carrying jewelry hidden in a shawl. When police showed the footage to the shopkeeper, it was discovered that the woman was the servant's wife. Later during interrogation, the servant said that he wanted to become a wealthy person. That's why he committed the theft. This incident occurred on February 3rd and the video has emerged today. Jeweler has two shops Anil Kumar Sahu, a resident of Maharajpura in Premnagar police station area, is a jeweler and has one shop at home, while the second shop is located in Sipri Bazaar. Anil said, “Sunil Ahirwar, a resident of Schoolpura locality in Nagra, had been working at my house for about 18 years. On February 3, I went to the farmhouse, while my son was at the Sipri Bazaar shop. My wife was present in the upper room.” I accidentally forgot the safe key at home. When I returned, I found that the safe key was inserted. Upon suspicion, when I opened the safe, jewelry worth 65 lakhs and cash amounting to 3 lakhs 10 thousand 700 rupees were missing. After this, I filed a complaint at the police station on Feb 11. Stole jewelry in 1:27 minutes CO Sadar Ramvir Singh said - Upon receiving information about the theft, Premnagar Station Officer Tulsiram Pandey and his team became active. Since the safe's lock was open, the servant Sunil was initially suspected, but he was denying committing the theft. Therefore, CCTV cameras installed around Anil's house were examined. Sunil's wife Preeti was seen in the footage. On February 3rd at 5:35:55 PM, she was seen running towards Anil's house. After 1 minute 27 seconds, that is at 5:37:22 PM, she was seen returning. In the footage, she was seen hiding jewelry and cash inside a shawl. After this, Sunil and Preeti were strictly interrogated. Both confessed to the theft. Police recovered all the jewelry and cash. Called wife on phone Accused Ramvir told police - After seeing the safe key in the house, greed arose in my mind. I also wanted to become a big person. If I had stolen the jewelry and run away, everyone would have suspected me. So I called my wife Preeti behind the house on the phone. Then opened the safe and took out all the jewelry and cash. Threw all the goods from the roof and gave it to my wife, who took it home and hid it in fan covers and other places. I stayed at home. When the owner opened the safe, the jewelry was missing, but since I was at home, no one suspected. However, the theft was caught later.

stories.title: I am facing a cocktail attack, says Avimukteshwaranand:Rambhadracharya's disciple Ashutosh Maharaj alleges Shankaracharya sexually exploited 20 minors
stories.summary: Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's disciple Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj has accused Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand of sexually exploiting 20 children in his camp. After this, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said that such allegations have been made which are difficult even to imagine. Ashutosh Brahmachari filed a complaint in Prayagraj's Special POCSO Court on February 8 alleging that Shankaracharya abuses children under the guise of gurukul. To substantiate his allegations, Ashutosh Brahmachari also presented 2 children. The lawyer of Avimukteshwaranand filed a reply on February 10 to the court notice. After this, serious allegations were made against Ashutosh Maharaj. Now on February 20, lawyers from both sides will appear in court. On the allegations of Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand in Varanasi. Read what he said... Question: A sexual harassment case against you has reached the court? Shankaracharya: See, ever since we started raising our voice for the protection of cows, the government and some people are not liking it. First we were insulted, our people were threatened and beaten up. When that didn't work, extremely disgusting allegations were made. Such allegations that civilized society cannot even imagine, but truth cannot be affected. We have given all evidence in court. Question: If the allegations are false, what action would you like to take? Shankaracharya: Under section 22 of the POCSO Act, if someone makes false allegations with malicious intent, action can be taken against them. The court has accepted our evidence. A notice has been issued to the concerned person to respond on the 20th. We have complete faith in the judiciary. Question: You challenged the Chief Minister, is this happening because of that? Shankaracharya: We did not give any personal challenge to the Chief Minister. We only said that cow should be declared as 'Rajy Mata' and cow meat export should be stopped. If we make this demand, what's wrong with that? Question: There are allegations that you have assets disproportionate to your income? Shankaracharya: This is just an allegation. When the investigation happens, the truth will come out. The question is what is our income? We are not salaried employees. We neither hold any government position, nor do we receive any salary. The allegation of having assets disproportionate to income applies to those who have regular income. As Shankaracharya, we don't have personal property. It seems like a list of allegations has been prepared and they are being made one by one. This is like a 'cocktail' attack being carried out by a group. Question: Can all four Shankaracharyas sit together? Shankaracharya: Let the time come, everyone will sit together. Currently there are allegations against us. The court will separate truth from falsehood. In such cases, decisions should come quickly. Also, the law states that in such cases, one's identity should not be made public, yet some people are doing so. This makes it clear that their objective is not resolution, but defamation. Question: Why are non-Hindus restricted from entering Badrinath-Kedarnath? Shankaracharya: The dignity of the temple should remain protected. Earlier, there was a clear board at Kashi Vishwanath Temple - Entry is prohibited for those who do not follow Arya Dharma. That board was in Hindi, Sanskrit and English. Now that board has been removed. We demand that the traditional board should be reinstated. The dignity of the temple can only be maintained when the person visiting understands and accepts that dignity. Now know what allegations Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj made First complained to Police Commissioner, then went to court 6 days after Mauni Amavasya on January 24, Ashutosh Maharaj filed 2 complaints against Avimukteshwaranand with the Police Commissioner of Prayagraj. In the first complaint, he alleged that minor children are kept in Avimukteshwaranand's camp and gurukul. They are made to do personal service, gather crowds, work at events and carry palanquins. There are also concerns about sexual exploitation of children. Children were made to work even in large events like the Magh Mela. This violates child rights and labor laws. There are suspicions of illegal weapons in the camp. Investigation should be done into assets exceeding income and multiple bank accounts. The role of a person named Mukundanand should be investigated. What did he allege in 2nd complaint? In the second complaint, Ashutosh Maharaj accused Avimukteshwaranand of creating fake letterheads and documents. He said that in the Magh Mela area, Avimukteshwaranand is claiming himself to be the Shankaracharya of Jyotish Peeth. He is sending letters to officials using letterheads and documents made in the name of "Jyotish Peeth/Shri Shankaracharya Camp". These letterhead-letters are fake and misleading. They are being used to mislead the administration and general public. These letterheads have the date January 24, 2026 (Magh Shukla Panchami). Using this date, letters were issued in the name of "Sri Shankaracharya Camp", whose validity has been questioned. Read the case filed by Ashutosh Maharaj in court When the administration took no action on Ashutosh Maharaj's complaint, he filed a case in court on February 8. In it, he wrote - On behalf of my trust, a grand yagna of Mata Shakumbhari Devi is being performed at the Magh Mela for the liberation of Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi. Two disciples came to my camp who are minors. They made several revelations before me. They expressed their desire to become my disciples. Said they are unsafe. They asked me for police protection and legal assistance. The children told me that Avimukteshwaranand and his associates kept us with them. Committed misconduct many times. This was done for a year. Misconduct was also done in the mela area during Mahakumbh-2025. During Magh Mela-2026, both children were again subjected to misconduct. Avimukteshwaranand's disciples would pressure the children by saying this is guru-seva. This will bring blessings. The children also revealed that they were asked to sleep with Avimukteshwaranand. Both children came to our camp when they got the chance. After this, a complaint was filed at Jhunsi police station on January 24. On January 25, complaints were emailed to the Police Commissioner and Police Superintendent Magh Mela. On January 27, a complaint was sent by post to the Police Superintendent Magh Mela. However, no FIR was registered. After this, I started receiving threats. Who is Ashutosh Maharaj? Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj was born in a Pandit family in Kandla town of Shamli district. His father Rajendra Pandey worked as a conductor in private buses running on Delhi Road. Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj was associated with the committee of the ancient Shakambhari Siddhapeeth temple in Kandla. Currently, he is also the manager. His family's uncle Pradeep Pandey is the priest in the temple. In 2022, he took initiation from Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, since then he has been living a life of asceticism.

stories.title: ₹1 lakh aid for girls’ weddings in UP:₹400 crore allocated for scooter scheme; key highlights of the final pre-poll budget
stories.summary: The Yogi government presented its biggest budget yet before the 2027 assembly elections. This is the government's 10th budget, which is 9.12 lakh crore. This is 12% more than last year. In the financial year 2025-26, a budget of 8.7 lakh crore was presented. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna made the biggest effort to appeal to women in the budget. Now daughters will receive Rs 1 lakh 1 thousand instead of 51 thousand for marriage. Additionally, announcements were made to launch new schemes worth 43 thousand crores. Stray cattle becomes a major issue during elections. A budget provision of 2000 crores has been made for their maintenance. To attract the largest youth segment, a promise of providing 10 lakh jobs was made. Under the CM Youth Entrepreneur Scheme, loans up to 5 lakh rupees will be available without interest and without guarantee. Meritorious female students will be distributed scooters worth 400 crore rupees. Although this provision was also made in last year's budget, it wasn't given to anyone. 3 Universities, 14 Medical Colleges will open There are 60 medical colleges in the state, 14 new ones will be opened. 3 universities will also be started. A budget of 2374 crore rupees has been given for free tablets and smartphones for students. 7 cities will be made smart. Yogi government has given 25% of the budget to infrastructure. 12% to agriculture, 12.50 to 15% to higher and basic education, while 6-8% amount has been given to health. New residential schemes will be launched UP Housing Development Board will launch new residential schemes to provide houses to the middle class. North-East corridor will be built with 34 thousand crores. This will go from Gorakhpur to Saharanpur via Nepal border. Jewar International Airport will now have 5 runways instead of 2. Ayodhya and Naimisharanya get 100-100 crores The government allocated 225 crore rupees for AI (Artificial Intelligence). Special attention was given to religious tourism again. 100-100 crore rupees will be given for the development of Ayodhya and Naimisharanya. The government will also renovate major temples in the state. Additionally, 800 crore rupees have been given for the development of Meerut, Mathura-Vrindavan and Kanpur Development Authorities. 100 crores allocated for new Legislative Building A new Legislative Building will be constructed on Sahara City land in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. It will house both the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council. It will also have chambers for ministers and adequate infrastructure for staff. A provision of 100 crore rupees has been made in the budget for this. Read, what announcements were made sector-wise in the budget… Their hopes were dashed Read what the expert said about the budget CA Ashish Pathak says, 'CM Yogi has stated the budget theme as "Safe Women, Capable Youth, Prosperous Farmers, Work for Every Hand, Uttar Pradesh Enriched through Technical Investment". That's why no direct election promises were made in the budget. However, the government has talked about major schemes for youth, women, farmers and employment to strengthen political hold from cities to villages. Now the government can make game-changing and populist announcements for these people through supplementary budget in the monsoon session. These groups will push the government's election chariot.

stories.title: Lamborghini crash case:Industrialist's son gets bail hours after arrest, police fail to justify remand 4 days after the incident
stories.summary: Shivam Mishra, son of Kanpur tobacco businessman KK Mishra and the main accused in the Lamborghini crash case, was granted relief by a Kanpur court on Thursday after being arrested earlier in the day. Mishra was presented in court after a routine medical check. The accused secured bail after furnishing a bond of Rs 20,000. Court rejects police remand plea According to the accused’s lawyer, Anant Sharma, the police sought a 14-day remand in court. However, the judge questioned the need for remand. The investigating officer reportedly failed to provide a convincing reason, leading the court to reject the remand application. Shivam was arrested at around 8 am from outside his residence. Police claimed he had not been cooperating with the investigation and had attempted to evade arrest. They said they received information that he was trying to flee in an ambulance, following which he was taken into custody. Court appearance and Health concerns After undergoing a medical examination, Shivam was produced before the AJCM court. He appeared unwell during the hearing and had an IV cannula attached to his hand. Police officers and relatives were seen assisting him, and a family doctor from Delhi was also present. Outside the court, Shivam reacted angrily to journalists recording videos, gesturing and questioning why they were filming him. Father’s defence and Political intervention Shivam’s father, tobacco businessman KK Mishra, had earlier denied that his son was driving the car at the time of the 8 February accident. Soon after the crash, he allegedly had his son removed from the scene. As the case gained attention, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed officials to take action. Subsequently, Kanpur Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal stated that investigations confirmed Shivam was driving the Lamborghini. The businessman, however, strongly objected to the commissioner’s statement, calling it false. Another man’s surrender rejected On Wednesday, a man named Mohan appeared before a Kanpur court claiming that he, not Shivam, was driving the Lamborghini at the time of the accident. However, the court rejected his plea and did not consider him an accused in the case. The investigation into the high-profile crash continues. What evidence and witnesses of the police the petition was dismissed 1. Accident Video Police included a video after the accident in their investigation. In this, after the accident, bouncers get out of another car following the Lamborghini. They break the Lamborghini's window with a brick to open the gate. Then they pull Shivam out from the driver's seat of the Lamborghini and take him to the hospital in another car. Police had claimed that Shivam could be clearly seen being pulled from the driver's seat. Watching the video makes it clear that there was no other person in the car. This is why they had to break the window with a brick. Only then could the car door be opened and Shivam could be pulled out. 2. Statements from more than 10 eyewitnesses The second biggest evidence in the police investigation report is the statements of eyewitnesses. Investigating officer Dinesh Singh recorded statements from more than 10 eyewitnesses. All of them stated that Shivam Mishra was driving the car. There was no other person present in the car. After the accident, Shivam was taken out of the bouncer car. All eyewitnesses dismissed claims about a driver operating the vehicle or presence of any other person in the car. Police recorded statements of all these eyewitnesses in their investigation report. 3. Shivam's mobile location was found at the accident site Police included Shivam's mobile location as electronic evidence in their investigation report. During the accident, Shivam's mobile location was also at the accident spot on VIP Road. 4. The entire incident was captured on CCTV Police included CCTV footage in the investigation report. The entire accident was captured in CCTV obtained from the municipal corporation. This footage also clearly shows that there was no driver in the car, only one person was present. 5. Complainant had identified Shivam Police had recorded the statement of Mo. Taufiq, a resident of Chamanganj Ghusiana who filed the FIR for the accident. He had stated that there was only one person in the driver's seat of the Lamborghini. After watching the video, he confirmed that Shivam Mishra was driving the car. The complainant's statement is considered most important in any case. Compromise application submitted in court, police unaware The most surprising thing in this case is that a compromise was reached between the complainant Mo. Taufiq of Chamanganj Ghusiana and Mohanlal. According to the compromise agreement presented in court by lawyer Dharmendra Singh, a settlement was reached between Taufiq and Mohan. On behalf of Taufiq, it was stated that he has been given expenses for treatment. Therefore, I am fully satisfied and do not want any further action in this case. This mutual compromise and settlement was not done under any pressure. DCP Central Atul Kumar Srivastava was contacted regarding this matter. He said- So far, the police have not received any kind of agreement. On February 10, complainant Mo. Taufiq had recorded his statement. During this time also, the complainant has not given any such information.
