stories.title: Wanted criminal fires several rounds at SP, killed in encounter:Amjad looted in police uniform; kept shooting in Muzaffarnagar till bullets run out
stories.summary: Police in Muzaffarnagar shot dead Amjad, a criminal carrying a reward of Rs 50,000, in an encounter. At around 3.30 am on Thursday, police received information that he was heading towards his village. Acting on the tip-off, police laid a cordon. The police team repeatedly warned him to surrender, but he began indiscriminate firing with a carbine and a pistol. A total of 20 rounds were fired from the accused’s side. SP Rural Aditya Bansal, CO Gajendra Singh and Station House Officer Subhash Atri narrowly escaped. Bullets struck their bulletproof jackets. Sub-Inspector Sandeep Chaudhary and Constable Ashfaq were shot in the hand. Police then retaliated with four rounds of fire. During the exchange, Amjad was hit by a bullet and fell to the ground. Police lifted him and took him to their vehicle, then rushed him to Budhana CHC, where he died during treatment. However, his accomplice managed to escape under the cover of darkness. The encounter took place in the Budhana police station area. The 40-year-old Amjad was a resident of Shahpur in Muzaffarnagar. Around 40 cases were registered against him in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Delhi and Uttarakhand. In 2021, he had looted 5 kg of gold from Muthoot Finance in Churu, Rajasthan. He often carried out crimes wearing a police uniform. He had recently committed a robbery in the Budhana police station area, and police were searching for him in connection with that case. Criminal kept firing until he ran out of bullets According to initial information, the encounter lasted around 20–25 minutes. The miscreant kept firing at police personnel until the bullets in both his pistol and carbine were exhausted. His bullets also struck vehicles at the scene, shattering their windows. Police personnel took cover behind a vehicle to save their lives and returned fire. The police recovered a carbine, a motorcycle and a pistol from the spot. Created terror in Muzaffarnagar and Ghaziabad Amjad was a wanted criminal not only in Uttar Pradesh but also in Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Bihar. A total of 40 cases were registered against him. He had particularly created terror in Muzaffarnagar and Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh. Of these, 21 cases were registered in Muzaffarnagar and nine in Ghaziabad. Apart from this, two cases were lodged in Bijnor, one in Meerut, one in Ghazipur, one in Bihar, one in Rajasthan, two in Delhi and one in Noida. Entered crime world in 2012, carried out robberies wearing police uniform Amjad stepped into the world of crime in 2012. Within just a year, he had created such fear that by 2013 he was booked under the Gangster Act at New Mandi police station in Muzaffarnagar and at Kotwali Gangnahar in Haridwar. He carried out robberies while wearing a police uniform and would open fire immediately if anyone resisted. In 2017, he came into the spotlight after shooting dead a youth during an attempted robbery. Besides this, four cases of attempt to murder are also registered against him. SSP Sanjay Kumar Verma said— Around 3 am, there was an encounter with the hardened criminal Amjad. The criminal, who carried a reward of Rs 50,000, was injured in police firing. He died during treatment at the Community Health Centre. A total of 40 cases are registered against him. Apart from Uttar Pradesh, he was also wanted in Haryana, Bihar, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand. 20 criminals killed in 130 days in UP CM had said – ‘If UP Police do not shoot, should they take the bullets instead?’ On February 3, during the inauguration of UP Pharma Conclave 1.0, Yogi said that more than 900 riots took place in Uttar Pradesh between 2012 and 2017. It was at such a time that he was given responsibility. “We decided on zero tolerance. Many times people comment on why the police fired. If the police do not fire, should they take the bullets instead? If that criminal has the freedom to shoot, we have also given pistols to the police.” ‘UP Police carrying out encounters for praise and promotion’ Last week, the Allahabad High Court expressed strong displeasure over the ‘half encounter’ method of the UP Police. The court observed that police officers were firing unnecessarily merely for appreciation, premature promotion and praise on social media. The High Court issued guidelines on six points. The bench of Justice Arun Kumar Deshwal clearly warned that if Supreme Court guidelines are not followed in encounter cases, the district SP, SSP and Police Commissioner will be held personally guilty of contempt of court. 259 criminals killed in encounters in eight years According to the state government, from March 2017 to October 2025, the UP Police have killed 259 criminals in encounters. During this period, more than 15,000 police encounters took place, in which over 31,000 criminals were arrested and more than 10,000 were shot.

stories.title: Female constable abducted hours before her wedding:Father alleges history-sheeter’s role; Meerut police recover her after 8 hours
stories.summary: Just hours before her wedding procession was due to arrive on Sunday evening, a woman constable went missing from her village, triggering panic among family members and a police hunt that ended within eight hours. The incident is from Akbarpur Sadan village in the Bahsuma police station area of Meerut district. The constable’s father lodged an FIR, alleging that a local history-sheeter, Ankit Thakur, had kidnapped his daughter. He told police that his daughter, posted at the Cyber Crime police station in Aligarh, was to be married on February 8, with the wedding procession expected from Khedki village in Mirapur. “Ankit has a criminal record. My daughter’s life is in danger,” the father said in his complaint. Police, however, claimed the woman left of her own free will. Now know the full matter... The female constable from Akbarpur Sadan was supposed to have her wedding procession on Sunday night. Before this, in the morning, a miscreant kidnapped the female constable. When family members received this information, there was an uproar. The female constable's father reached the police station and filed a complaint. He said - my daughter is posted at the Cyber Crime police station in Aligarh. Today, February 8, was her wedding day. The wedding procession was supposed to come from Khedki village in Mirapur. Before this, Ankit, a resident of Dhikoli, kidnapped my daughter. Ankit has a criminal record. My daughter's life is in danger. Called and said - I'm going by my own will According to police, shortly after the family reached the police station, they received a call from the woman constable on a home phone. She said that she was going by her own will. There is no need to worry about her. She also said that she is an adult and understands what's good and bad for her. However, the family is not confirming this. CO Pankaj Lawania said that a case has been registered based on the father's complaint. Ankit is a history-sheeter from Mawana police station Accused Ankit Thakur is a history-sheeter from Mawana police station. In May 2025, he and some accomplices robbed a liquor shop. Police had surrounded him. After an encounter, accused Ankit was arrested. During this, Ankit was also shot in one leg. He has recently been released from jail. Girl's father falls ill The family is in shock due to the daughter's kidnapping just hours before the wedding. It is being discussed that the constable's father has fallen ill. He was taken to the hospital due to complaints of chest pain. The person who had arranged this relationship has also reached the female constable's house. Meanwhile, continuous communication is happening over phone with the groom's side.

stories.title: Husband sells wife for ₹1,000, woman gang-raped:Victim in Badaun says he sent her with two men, told her, 'I will earn money from you'
stories.summary: In a shocking incident, a man in Uttar Pradesh’s Badaun allegedly sent his wife with two men after taking ₹1,000 from them, leading to her gang rape. Police have registered an FIR against three accused, including the husband, and launched a search operation. The incident took place in the Faizganj Behta police station area. According to the complaint, the woman was sent with the accused on the pretext of visiting a gas agency. Instead, she was taken to a jungle, where the two men allegedly raped her before fleeing. Sent with accused under false pretence The woman told police that on February 6, her husband claimed they were going to get gas-related documents prepared. On the way, they met two men — Pappu, a resident of Allahpur Khurd, and Balkishan from Takhora village. The husband allegedly took ₹1,000 from the two men. Soon after, the husband told his wife that he had some work elsewhere and asked her to go to the gas agency with the two men. Trusting her husband, the woman agreed and sat on their motorcycle. Instead of taking her to the agency, the accused drove her towards Balkanpur village and later diverted to a eucalyptus grove in a jungle. Threatened and assaulted in jungle The woman alleged that both men raped her in the jungle. When she raised an alarm, they covered her mouth and threatened to kill her if she resisted. The accused reportedly told her that they had paid her husband for the act and that he was fully aware of it. After committing the crime, the accused abandoned her in the jungle and fled. Husband admitted taking money, says victim The woman somehow managed to reach home, where her husband was present. When she confronted him, he allegedly admitted to taking money and told her that he would continue to earn from her in the same manner. The victim initially informed her brother-in-law, but due to his visual impairment, she could not approach the police immediately. The next day, she went to the police station and lodged a formal complaint. Police action underway Faizganj Behta Station House Officer Rajkumar Singh said an FIR has been registered against all three accused. “Search operations are underway to arrest the accused. The victim’s statement will be recorded and her medical examination will be conducted as per procedure,” he said.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:PM Modi in Malaysia says, ‘No double standards and no compromise on terror’; Ashes of Ajit Pawar immersed in Sangam Prayagraj More
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. ‘No double standards, no compromise,' PM Modi in Malaysia says, ‘India's message on terrorism is clear' PM Narendra Modi held talks with Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim. Modi emphasised that India and Malaysia will collaborate closely against terrorism, stating, “Our message on terrorism is very clear, no double standards, no compromise.” 2. Ajit Pawar’s ashes immersed at Sangam; family performs final rites in Prayagraj The ashes of former Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar were immersed at the Sangam here on Sunday, with his son Jai Pawar performing the final rites amid chanting of religious mantras. The Pawar family arrived in Prayagraj from Baramati by a chartered flight. Jai Pawar walked barefoot from the Prayagraj airport to the Sangam carrying his father’s ashes. 3. Ghaziabad sisters’ suicide: father was with third wife Police said the father was in a separate room with his third wife when three daughters jumped to their deaths in Ghaziabad. A diary found in their room is being treated as a suicide note and sent for forensic handwriting analysis. 4. Assam CM alleges Gaurav Gogoi’s wife has Pakistan links Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma claimed Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi’s wife, Elizabeth Colburn, has ties with Pakistan. Speaking on Sunday, he said the matter will be referred to the Home Ministry for investigation. The Assam government will also seek cancellation of her OCI/visa, calling her presence “detrimental to India.” 5. UP spends just over half of last budget so far Ahead of the February 11 Budget, an assessment shows the Uttar Pradesh government has released only 54.42% of last year’s allocation. While pension funds were fully released, health and infrastructure saw sharp cuts, despite reviews by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Finance Minister Suresh Khanna. 6. Sanjay Nishad flags lack of VIP protocol in Deoria UP cabinet minister Sanjay Nishad expressed anger after receiving no escort or VIP arrangements during his visit to Deoria. He said public programmes were affected. His office wrote to the DM and SP, seeking action against responsible officials. 7. PCB-ICC to hold talks on India-Pakistan clash; Bangladesh joins Pakistan had earlier refused to play the February 15 India match in Colombo, prompting ICC intervention. Talks are now underway between PCB and ICC. BCB President Aminul Islam Bulbul is in Lahore for discussions and will return Tuesday after deliberating on the fixture’s future. 8. ‘Rent a womb’ racket busted in Prayagraj Police uncovered an illegal egg-selling racket operating from an IVF centre in Prayagraj for eight years. Young girls were lured, including a minor shown as an adult using fake documents. Eggs were sold for ₹2–5 lakh per case. 9. Murshidabad mosque row: hoardings trigger alert Hoardings in Lucknow warn of a “New Babri” in Murshidabad ahead of a February 10 visit by Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad. The posters, naming Mamata Banerjee, prompted police to heighten security to prevent any law-and-order trouble. 10. Yash Raj Films denied using fake reports of 300 missing Delhi girls to promote Mardaani 3 Mardaani 3 landed in controversy after claims that reports of 800 people, including 300 girls, missing from Delhi were exaggerated as a publicity stunt. Social media accused Yash Raj Films of fuelling panic to promote the film. YRF denied all allegations, calling them baseless.

stories.title: Businessman’s son runs over 6 persons with Lamborghini in Kanpur:Bullet rider flung nearly 10-feet after high-speed crash
stories.summary: In Kanpur, a tobacco businessman’s son rammed a Lamborghini into more than six people. After hitting a Bullet motorcycle, the rider was flung nearly 10 feet into the air, following which the luxury car climbed onto the bike. After the accident, angry locals surrounded the car, forcing the driver to remain inside. His bouncers created a ruckus at the spot, pushing people aside. Police soon reached the scene and took the car to the police station. At the police station, the businessman’s bouncers allegedly misbehaved with the injured victims, triggering further chaos. The businessman’s son and other injured persons were later admitted to a private hospital. The incident took place in the Gwal Toli police station area. See 3 pictures Speeding car went out of control, hit people KK Mishra is a tobacco businessman. Around 3:15 PM, his son Shivam Mishra was speeding in his Lamborghini car on VIP Road. Near Rev-3, the car went out of control. The car hit more than 6 people including vehicle drivers parked on the roadside. A bullet rider was hit so hard that he was thrown and fell on the road. After this, the car climbed onto the front wheel of the bullet. As soon as this was known, Gwaltoli police reached the spot. The businessman's son was safely removed from the crowd. The injured and the industrialist's son were taken to the hospital. Police brought the car to the station. During this time, the crowd also reached the station. Due to it being a case involving an influential and prominent family, the car was kept safely inside the station. During this, the industrialist's bouncer misbehaved with people present there. This caused the crowd to create an uproar. 'We were standing by the roadside when they hit' Sonu Tripathi said - My uncle's son Vishal and I came on a Bullet motorcycle. Then we stopped at a shop by the roadside. Vishal was sitting on the Bullet. We were looking at T-shirts. That's when the Lamborghini car first hit an auto. After that, it crushed our Bullet. Vishal also fell far from the impact. There were 2 other boys who were also hit hard. They were thrown 10 feet in the air and fell on the footpath far away. Both have been sent to the hospital. In the accident, one youth was injured on his face. Blood was coming from his mouth. He has also been sent to the hospital. We have filed a complaint at the police station. Businessman's company was raided 2 years ago Tobacco businessman KK Mishra owns a company called Banshidhar Exports Private Limited. This company supplies tobacco to top gutka companies in Kanpur. About 2 years ago on February 28, the Income Tax Department raided the company's head office. At that time, cars worth more than 100 crores were found at KK Mishra's Delhi residence. These included luxury cars worth more than 60 crores. There was a Rolls-Royce Phantom car worth 16 crores, along with Lamborghini, Ferrari, and McLaren cars. The raid then uncovered tax evasion of more than 100 crores.

Uproar at Shahjahanpur medical college over patient’s death:Family vandalises hospital; police beat father and son, drag them to outpost
stories.summary: A 16-year-old student died after being hit by a Vande Bharat train in Shahjahanpur on Sunday. His family has accused doctors and hospital staff of negligence, alleging that no treatment was provided and the body was sent directly to the mortuary. Angry family members vandalised the trauma centre at the Government Medical College following the incident. Police forces from several stations were deployed outside the medical college to control the situation. Police initially claimed the student was making a reel when he was hit by the train. The family has denied this claim. Student injured after being hit by train, police cite reel-making The deceased, Ankit Singh (16), was a Class 12 student and a resident of Dhakiya Tiwari village under the Nigohi police station area. He studied at SP College in Shahjahanpur city. On Sunday, Ankit was seriously injured after being hit by a Vande Bharat train near Indranagar Colony. Railway Protection Force personnel informed the Sadar Bazaar police, who reached the spot and sent the injured student to the Government Medical College in an ambulance. Doctors later declared him dead. The body was kept in the mortuary as unidentified. Body kept in mortuary without treatment, alleges family Family members reached the medical college some time later and alleged that Ankit was still breathing when he was brought in but was not given any medical treatment. They claimed the body was placed directly in the mortuary without proper examination. The family said they took Ankit from the mortuary back to the trauma centre, but instead of treatment, doctors allegedly misbehaved with them. Family members vandalise trauma centre Following the alleged refusal of treatment, angry family members vandalised parts of the medical college. Furniture was damaged and files were thrown around inside the trauma centre. As the situation escalated, police personnel from Chauk Kotwali and Sadar Bazaar police stations reached the spot. Police assault father and cousin, alleges family The family alleged that police later assaulted Ankit’s father, Vimlesh Singh, and cousin, Vineet. A video that has surfaced shows police personnel dragging the two men into a police post and beating them. According to the family, the father was locked inside the post and released only after the situation calmed down. They also alleged that money was demanded for their release, a claim not officially confirmed. Demand for CCTV probe into hospital response The deceased’s cousin said the family accepts responsibility for the vandalism but wants clarity on whether doctors examined Ankit when he was brought to the medical college in an injured condition. They have demanded an investigation and examination of CCTV footage from the hospital premises. Family in shock; board exams were due Ankit’s father is a farmer. He is survived by his mother, Soni Devi, and younger sister, Siddhi. Family members said they are in deep shock and grief. Ankit’s Class 12 board examinations were scheduled to begin on February 18. He had come to Shahjahanpur to buy study materials when the incident occurred.

stories.title: 13-year-old student collapses while playing cricket in Mainpuri, dies:Heart attack suspected, family loses only son
stories.summary: A 13-year-old student died after collapsing while playing cricket in Mainpuri district on Sunday morning. The incident took place in the Bichwa police station area. Doctors have suspected a heart attack, though the exact cause of death could not be confirmed as the family did not opt for a post-mortem examination. The deceased, Virat Singh Chauhan, was a Class 6 student at Anara Education Academy in the Lahra area. He lived with his family in Sahara village. According to family members and friends, Virat had gone to a nearby ground close to his house on Sunday morning to play a cricket match with neighbourhood children. While bowling, he suddenly complained of severe pain in his hand. Now read the full news in sequence Somendra Singh’s son, Virat Singh, a resident of Sahara village, was a student of Anara Education Academy. On Sunday morning, he went to a ground near his house to play a cricket match with friends. As soon as he came on to bowl, he complained of severe pain in his hand. Moments later, he collapsed on the ground and began writhing in pain. The children tried to help him stand up, but he was unable to move. Frightened, they immediately informed Virat’s family. Friend recalls: first in pain, then unconscious A friend present at the ground said they were playing a match when Virat came on to bowl. After delivering one ball, he complained of pain in his hand. He bowled three more deliveries, but the pain intensified. Soon after, he lay down on the ground, writhing in pain, and within a short time, lost consciousness. Rushed to hospital, declared dead The friend said the family was informed immediately. Family members reached the ground and rushed Virat to the district hospital. Dr. Lalit, who was on duty in the emergency ward, examined him and declared him dead. Doctors said the child had already died on the way to the hospital. Cause of death unclear Chief Medical Superintendent Dr. Dharmendra Singh said the child was brought dead to the emergency ward. He added that the cause of death could not be determined. Only son, village in mourning Virat was the only son of his parents. His father, Somendra Singh Chauhan, is a farmer and was in Delhi for work at the time of the incident. After receiving the news, he immediately left for home. At the house, Virat’s mother Suniti and his younger sister Aradhya were inconsolable. Women from the neighbourhood gathered to console the family, as mourning spread across the village.

stories.title: 'If PM is unsafe in Parliament, he should resign':Imran Masood attacks Modi at Constitution dialogue rally in Varanasi; Pawan Khera invokes 'curse of Kashi'
stories.summary: Senior Congress leaders on Sunday launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at the party’s Samvidhan Samvad rally in Varanasi, alleging moral and political failure and accusing the government of betraying the civilisational ethos of Kashi. Addressing the gathering, Congress national spokesperson Pawan Khera said that the political challenges facing the Prime Minister in recent months had their roots in Kashi. Referring to the Manikarnika ghat and the Ganga, Mr. Khera alluded to the handling of bodies during the pandemic and said the “curse” of neglect and betrayal was returning to haunt the leadership. He alleged that the Prime Minister, who had invoked the name of the Ganga in his political narrative, had failed to uphold the dignity of the river and the city. Another Congress spokesperson, Supriya Shrinate, said Kashi was a “living civilisation” and criticised the government over the removal of statues, calling it deeply hurtful to public sentiment. She also referred to the 2024 Lok Sabha election results, claiming that the Prime Minister had faced repeated setbacks during the counting process in Varanasi, and thanked the electorate for what she described as a message of resistance. Congress MP Imran Masood raised concerns over security lapses, stating that if a Prime Minister’s life was under threat even within Parliament, it raised serious questions about governance and accountability. He argued that such circumstances warranted moral responsibility at the highest level. The rally was attended by Congress leaders and workers from several States and formed part of the party’s outreach campaign centred on constitutional values and democratic accountability. ‘Curse from Kashi’ Addressing the rally, Congress national spokesperson Pawan Khera alleged that the political troubles facing the Prime Minister in recent months stemmed from Kashi itself. Referring to Manikarnika Ghat and the Covid-19 period, Mr. Khera said the suffering witnessed along the Ganga had been ignored. He claimed that bodies floating in the river and the anguish of the people had gone unseen, and described this neglect as a “curse” emanating from the holy city. “If someone can betray Kashi and invoke Mother Ganga only for political gain, how will that person respect ordinary citizens?” he asked. Mr. Khera also questioned why Congress leaders continued to campaign despite difficult conditions, linking the struggle to what he described as an effort to safeguard constitutional values. He referred to Rahul Gandhi’s 5,000-km march as part of that effort. Statues, heritage and identity Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate accused the Centre and the Uttar Pradesh government of undermining Kashi’s heritage in the name of development. She said it was deeply disturbing that statues were being damaged under the watch of the Prime Minister and the State Chief Minister. “Kashi is mentioned in the Vedas and the Puranas. It is a living civilisation — the city of Shiva, devotion, values and faith,” she said, alleging that Sanatan traditions were being compromised in the name of infrastructure projects. Ms. Shrinate recalled the 2024 Lok Sabha results, saying she felt a sense of satisfaction as the Prime Minister trailed round after round in Varanasi. She thanked the people of Kashi for what she described as a message in defence of democracy and constitutional principles. Voting, Constitution and economy MP Imran Masood framed the political contest as a fight to protect the Constitution, urging citizens to take personal responsibility for voting. He argued that the Congress had weakened because sections of society had stopped voting, and warned that new laws would further erode citizens’ rights if public participation declined. Criticising the Union Budget, Mr. Masood questioned the emphasis on large infrastructure projects such as bullet trains. “If people do not have money in their pockets, who will travel on these trains?” he asked, alleging that big projects primarily benefited corporate interests. He also sparked controversy by saying that if the Prime Minister’s life was unsafe even inside Parliament, he should resign, adding that the real danger was to the Constitution and the soul of the nation. Allegations of insult to religious figures Prayagraj MP Ujjwal Raman Singh alleged that the insult to Ahilyabai and Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand amounted to an insult to the nation. He said Kashi would respond politically and warned that public anger would be reflected in future elections. Echoing this line, several speakers referred to incidents at Manikarnika Ghat and in Prayagraj as symbols of administrative insensitivity and erosion of respect for religious traditions. ‘People’s MP versus power’s MP’ Amethi MP Kishori Lal Sharma drew a contrast between what he called a “people’s MP” and an MP created by the machinery of power. He said there was no complaint against the people of Kashi, but alleged that the Prime Minister’s political rise was enabled by state power rather than popular mandate. Mr. Sharma also spoke of his own political journey, saying he contested elections at the insistence of the Gandhi family and with the backing of local voters. Documentary on ‘development’ A 15-minute documentary screened during the rally questioned development projects in Banaras, alleging that heritage, traditions and the city’s historical character were being compromised. The film also highlighted issues such as pollution of the Ganga, sewer overflows, traffic congestion and alleged administrative failures. Congress leaders said the rally was not merely a political event but an effort to defend Kashi’s identity, faith and constitutional values. They said issues raised at the gathering would be taken “from the streets to Parliament,” positioning Kashi as a moral and political centre of the larger democratic debate.

stories.title: Murshidabad Babri Mosque faces fresh threat:Hoardings in Lucknow claim demolition plan; warning of repeating Babri-style incident
stories.summary: The Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad has announced a visit to Murshidabad in West Bengal on February 10. The organisation has put up hoardings in Lucknow to promote the visit. The hoardings carry strong and provocative messages and also include an appeal asking people to go to Murshidabad on that day. One of the hoardings claims that there will be a decisive fight over what it calls a “New Babri” in Murshidabad. It also makes references to an “anti-Hindu government”. The posters include a photograph of West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. After the hoardings appeared in the city overnight, the police have gone on alert. Security agencies are closely monitoring the situation to prevent any disturbance to law and order. 5 hoardings put up from 1090 to Gomti Nagar 5 hoardings have been put up late Saturday night between Lucknow's 1090 Chauraha and Gomti Nagar. They mention the Babri Masjid under construction in Murshidabad. On one side, there is a picture of Lord Shri Ram and Gopal Rai, the president of Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad. On the other side, there is a picture of Mamata Banerjee and MLA Humayun Kabir. Humayun has been given the getup of Babar. Announcement to march to Murshidabad on February 10 Along with putting up the hoardings, Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad (VHRP) has also announced that its workers will go to Murshidabad on February 10. National President Gopal Rai said that the organization has decided on a program to go to Murshidabad on February 10. The hoardings convey a message regarding this program. Will also dig graves Gopal Rai said - West Bengal MLA Humayun Kabir has spoken about starting the construction of Babri Masjid in Murshidabad from February 11. Because of this, we should prepare to go from here to Murshidabad on February 10. We will leave from here on February 10. We will protest there on the morning of February 11. He said - If needed, we will also dig Humayun Kabir's grave there. The anti-Hindu government there also needs to be overthrown. Administration alert, keeping an eye on the situation After the hoardings were put up, the police-administration has become alert. The police have claimed to increase surveillance in sensitive areas. Now read the Murshidabad Babri Masjid dispute In Beldanga, Murshidabad district of West Bengal, TMC suspended MLA Humayun Kabir laid the foundation stone on December 6 for a mosque to be built on the lines of Ayodhya's Babri Masjid. During this, slogans of 'Nara-e-Takbir, Allahu Akbar' were raised. More than 2 lakh people had gathered at the event. Humayun Kabir had said on November 25 that he would lay the foundation stone of the Babri Masjid on December 6, marking 33 years since the demolition of the disputed structure in Ayodhya. TMC had suspended Humayun Kabir from the party on December 4. Now read the timeline of the Murshidabad Babri Masjid dispute November 28: Posters for the foundation stone laying ceremony of Babri Masjid were seen in several places in Beldanga, Murshidabad. It was written - The foundation stone laying ceremony of Babri Masjid will be held in Beldanga on December 6. Humayun Kabir was named as the organizer on the poster. Following this, the controversy escalated. BJP opposed it, while Congress leaders supported it. December 3: TMC distanced itself from the matter. The statement said - The party has no connection with Kabir's announcement. Another party leader said - Humayun Kabir has created this controversy so that he can get a ticket for the assembly elections from the Rethnagar seat. Humayun is currently an MLA from the Bharatpur seat of Murshidabad. December 4: Seeing the matter escalate, TMC suspended MLA Humayun Kabir. Kolkata Mayor Firhad Hakim said - the party does not believe in communal politics. On the party's action, Humayun said - I stand by my statement on Babri Masjid. I will also announce my new party on December 22. I will field candidates in 135 seats in the assembly elections. I will contest against both of them (TMC and BJP). Humayun had said - if 100 Muslims are martyred, they will take 500 Speaking to the media about building the Babri Masjid in Murshidabad, Humayun Kabir gave another controversial statement on November 28, 2025. He said, 'Anyone who tries to stop them will have to face serious consequences. If 100 Muslims are martyred, they will take 500 people with them.' Humayun Kabir has been in the news for controversial statements before. During the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, Humayun Kabir said at a public meeting in Shaktipur, Murshidabad, 'I will quit politics if I don't drown you (Hindus) in the Bhagirathi River within two hours. You are 30%, we are 70% (Muslims). I will not let you live in Shaktipur.' After this statement, the Election Commission had issued him a notice. Meanwhile, TMC had distanced itself from this statement. Mosque dispute is a year old The entire dispute began in November 2024. At that time, TMC MLA Humayun Kabir had talked about building a small replica of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya. When a controversy arose over the use of the name Babri, he said that Babri Masjid is an emotional issue for Muslims. After this, in December 2024, BJP talked about building a Ram temple in Murshidabad. However, even then, BJP leader Shankar Ghosh had said that the Ram temple should not be seen as a response to the mosque. The temple is part of culture, while the Babri Masjid has a bad history, how can it be built in Bengal?

stories.title: Inspector drags complainant by collar inside tehsil premises:Man made to sit for 4 hours in Kasganj Kotwali; released after Commissioner left
stories.summary: A man who reached a grievance redressal hearing to meet the commissioner in Kasganj was allegedly dragged and pushed out by the inspector of Kasganj Kotwali. The police personnel reportedly kept the complainant seated inside the police station for nearly four hours. He was released only after Aligarh Commissioner Sangeeta Singh left the tehsil premises. The incident took place on Saturday. The complainant, Santosh Gaud, had arrived to submit his complaint to the commissioner. A video of the entire episode has surfaced. The footage shows the station in-charge grabbing the complainant by his collar, pushing him out of the tehsil premises and then dragging him towards the police station. The victim said he was taken to the police station by force. He added that he had been hungry since morning, but was not allowed to leave. Now know the complete matter... Aligarh Division Commissioner Sangeeta Singh had arrived in Kasganj for a Samadhan Diwas public hearing. Santosh Gaud, a resident of Soron Gate area under Kotwali limits, had come to lodge a complaint regarding alleged illegal occupation of his 2.5 bigha land. It is alleged that Kotwali in-charge Pravesh Rana and his team did not allow him to meet the commissioner. The victim stated that inspector Pravesh Rana grabbed his collar inside the tehsil premises and forcibly dragged him out. He was then pushed and taken to the police station, where he was made to sit for four hours. He was released only after Commissioner Sangeeta Singh left Kasganj for Aligarh. During this period, a video of the alleged police misbehaviour also surfaced, clearly showing police personnel dragging Santosh Gaud by the collar while escorting him out of the tehsil. After the video surfaced, Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Santosh Gaud. Read the full conversation... Report: What had happened? Santosh: On Saturday, I went to meet Commissioner Sangeeta Singh during Samadhan Diwas. I had gone to complain about illegal occupation of my 2.5 bigha land. Inside the tehsil premises, the police misbehaved with me. When I protested, I was grabbed by the collar, dragged and taken to the police station, as if I were an accused in a serious criminal case. I was booked under preventive action Section 151. In the evening, my case was heard in the SDM court. I secured bail and was then released. Report: What complaint had you gone to raise? Santosh: My land in Paharpur Mafi, plot numbers 215 and 210, is being illegally occupied in collusion with BJP district panchayat chairman’s representative Bobby Kashyap and Sadar SDM Sanjeev Kumar. There was also an attempt to lay a road through my field. I had gone to raise this issue before the commissioner. Report: What happened at the tehsil? Santosh: I went to submit my written complaint. The police misbehaved with me there. I was holding my application and a poster alleging collusion between the SDM and a BJP leader in illegally occupying my land, where I plan to establish a Gurukul. I have submitted complaints through IGRS, the Chief Minister’s portal and public hearings, but false reports are filed every time. Report: How many times have you submitted petitions? Santosh:At least 250 to 300 times so far. I met the Chief Minister at a public hearing in Lucknow on January 12, 2025. I was assured that possession of my land would be restored, but nothing has happened till now. The complainant said he has been fighting a legal battle for the past three years to free his land from illegal encroachment, but justice has not been delivered despite repeated complaints. Legal battle continuing for three years Santosh Gaud said he has been pursuing legal remedies for the past three years. He has lodged more than 250 complaints with the Chief Minister’s office, district administration and through IGRS, but every time, incorrect reports are submitted. He intends to set up a Gurukul on his land. Victim's Family and Situation Santosh Gaud is a resident of Soron Gate in Kasganj and sells plastic goods for a living. His family includes his wife Geeta Gaud and three sons — Raghav (15), Madhav (13) and Keshav (12). His sons study at Gurukul Shri Sang Ved Sanskrit Vidyalaya in Narora, Bulandshahr. Warning of Protest in Lucknow for Justice Santosh Gaud said that after being stopped, dragged to the police station and allegedly mistreated, he is now planning to stage a protest in Lucknow. He said such treatment of citizens is condemnable and that he will continue his fight until justice is delivered. Who is Kotwal Pravesh Rana Inspector Pravesh Rana has been posted in Kasganj since August 8, 2025. Earlier, he was posted at Quarsi police station in Aligarh, where he was suspended on July 30, 2023. During his tenure there, AMU students had allegedly assaulted a dhaba owner and his friend, abducted them and beat them inside a hostel. In that case, Pravesh Rana was accused of negligence after releasing the accused under preventive sections. Following the video going viral and public outrage, senior police officials suspended him.

stories.title: Molestation accused beaten with shoes in public:Panchayat announces verdict, teenage victim slaps accused 5 times; complaint under probe
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh’s Sambhal, a village panchayat sentences a molestation accused to punishment by shoe beating. With the consent of the panchayat members, the teenage victim hits the accused five times with shoes. The incident takes place on Saturday in a village under the Chandausi area. The accused minor’s family objects to the panchayat’s decision. A video showing the public shoe beating in front of the full panchayat also surfaces. Meanwhile, the police say they have no information about the shoe-beating incident during the panchayat. However, they confirm that a molestation complaint has been received and is under investigation. Molested after finding her alone near village forest A 16-year-old boy living in a village under the Kudhfatehgarh police station area of Chandausi tehsil allegedly regularly harasses a 15-year-old girl living near his house. According to villagers, the distance between their houses is around 800 metres. The victim alleges that the teenager has been troubling her for a long time and repeatedly molesting her. On February 6, when the girl goes to a nearby forest to collect grass, the accused allegedly molests her after finding her alone. When the girl returns home, she narrates the entire incident to her mother. On Saturday afternoon, the victim’s mother reaches Kudhfatehgarh police station and informs the police about the matter. The police assure action and send them back. Panchayat lasted 4 hours, then announced verdict When the mother and daughter return to the village, the village head and other residents stop them. A village panchayat is convened, which continues for about four hours. The panchayat members hear all sides before deciding that the victim will hit the accused with shoes five times. Following the decision, in the presence of villagers and panchayat members, the girl hits the accused with shoes five times. During the punishment, the accused’s family continues to protest, while some villagers record the incident on their mobile phones. Accused side said - Will file complaint with police The elder brother of the accused minor says the panchayat’s decision was recorded on video, leading to public humiliation of the family. He says they will file a complaint with the police. Police unaware of events outside station Station in-charge Lokendra Tyagi says the minor girl came to the police station with her mother and accused a minor boy of harassment. The police asked for a written complaint, but no written statement was submitted.

stories.title: Unnao rape victim speaks out:Says daily court attendance difficult due to family responsibilities; regular hearing scheduled on Sengar’s petition
stories.summary: The Unnao rape victim expressed concerns over the daily hearings scheduled by the Delhi High Court from February 11 on Kuldeep Singh Sengar's petition. She said, "The High Court has set the 11th for daily hearings. Then there will be daily hearings. In such a situation, it will be very difficult for me to come to court every day." The victim said, "I am not backing down from justice, but I have the responsibility of my home, family, and small children. How will I be able to reach court every day in such a situation?" She also said that she is studying. "Attending court daily will affect both my studies and my future." The victim said she wants time to be given between hearings. "So that I can come to court, listen to the arguments of my case, ask questions, and present my views. My request is that the hearing dates be scheduled once a week, once every two weeks, or once a month." First, know the Unnao gangrape case in 5 points Now read what the victim said in the video The victim said- I want to tell all media channels that my hearing date was set in the High Court. During the arguments, they have scheduled the hearing for the 11th. This hearing is to be held every day. I want to clearly state that if the hearing is held daily, how will I be able to go to court every day? I also have work, my family, my home, and my children. It is not possible for me to go to court every day, leaving my children. Some people are filing applications for the case to be heard daily, but I will not be able to go to court regularly, because I am also studying and learning some courses. I need to do something for myself for my future. My request to the Honourable High Court, Supreme Court, and all concerned officials is that there should be an interval between hearings. So that I can be present in court, listen to the arguments of my case, ask questions, and present my views. I will not be able to go daily, so the hearing date should be scheduled once a week, once every two weeks, or once a month. Only then will I be able to fight my case. If daily hearings are mandatory, it would be better if my house were built in the High Court itself, so that I could wake up, bathe, wash, prepare food and water, and sit in court there. Because we have to take care of our family, children, and the case. Seeing all this, I am very sad that I am being tortured by being made to run around and harassed in this manner. stories.title: Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad angry over lack of VIP treatment:No escort received, no officer arrived in Deoria; letter written for action
stories.summary: Sanjay Nishad, a minister in the UP government, got angry when he did not receive VVIP treatment. Minister Nishad, who arrived in Deoria, was neither provided an escort vehicle nor VVIP arrangements at the Circuit House. No officer was present at the Circuit House either. The angry minister said, "Due to the lack of an escort, there was inconvenience in public hearings and other programs." The minister's PS, Ambika Prasad Srivastava, has sent a letter to the DM and SP, instructing them to take action against the concerned officers and employees and inform his office. The incident is from February 2. Minister Nishad had arrived in Deoria to attend a private program. The minister alleges that despite this pre-planned program, the district administration ignored the protocol. First, read what Minister Nishad said Minister Nishad said - Due to not getting an escort vehicle, I had to wander in the city for a long time. This caused a delay in reaching the event venue and affected government work. The minister called it a serious administrative lapse and stressed the need for action against the responsible officials. Minister's private secretary wrote a letter to the District Magistrate Minister Nishad's private secretary has written a letter to the DM and SP demanding action against the concerned officials. According to the letter, on February 2, at 10:30 AM, Fisheries Minister Dr. Sanjay Nishad visited Deoria district. But neither an escort vehicle was provided at the Gorakhpur-Deoria border, nor was any liaison officer present at the Circuit House. This protocol lapse came to light when the minister was scheduled to attend his programs and public hearings. Not following protocol during a minister-level arrival is an extremely serious matter. On the minister's instructions, immediate action has been ordered against the guilty officers and employees, and the office has been asked to be informed of the same. The letter has termed the serious negligence and indiscipline in protocol and has asked for clear instructions to be issued to prevent such a situation from recurring in the future. Officials said - unaware of the matter, haven't received the letter ADM Administration Prem Narayan Singh said- I do not have any information about this matter yet. No letter has been received either. According to the government order, the minister will be provided with full protocol. SP Sanjeev Suman said- So far, no letter has been received from the minister's private secretary. If there has been any negligence in providing facilities under protocol, it is a serious matter. An investigation will be conducted and action will be taken.

stories.title: Ajit Pawar’s ashes immersed at Sangam:Family performs final rites in Prayagraj
stories.summary: The ashes of former Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar were immersed at the Sangam here on Sunday, with his son Jai Pawar performing the final rites amid chanting of religious mantras. The Pawar family arrived in Prayagraj from Baramati by a chartered flight. Jai Pawar walked barefoot from the Prayagraj airport to the Sangam carrying his father’s ashes. The family reached the ghat in a long convoy, accompanied by several leaders from the BJP and the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP). Asthi Kalash yatra from Kashmir to Kanyakumari NCP youth wing president Dheeraj Sharma said the Asthi Kalash Yatra had traversed the length of the country before concluding at the Sangam. “The yatra began in Kashmir and ended at the Sangam today. It passed through 12 States. I personally joined the yatra from Haridwar to Telangana,” Mr. Sharma said, describing Ajit Pawar as a national political figure whose influence extended beyond Maharashtra. Earlier immersion in Kashi Earlier this week, ashes were also immersed in the Ganga at Kashi as part of the last rites, family sources said. Death in plane crash According to the information provided, Ajit Pawar died in a chartered aircraft crash at Baramati Airport on January 28. Five people, including two pilots, a female crew member and a security personnel, were killed in the accident. Following his death, his wife Sunetra Pawar took oath as Maharashtra’s first woman Deputy Chief Minister. See 2 pictures....

stories.title: Ghaziabad suicide- Father was with third wife when daughters jumped:2 other wives were present in the house; handwriting in diary notes under forensic analysis
stories.summary: After the death of three sisters in Ghaziabad, police have recorded statements from their father, Chetan, and his three wives. It emerged that at the time of the suicides, Chetan was in a separate room with his third wife, Tina, who is Muslim. However, after the incident, he had stated that he was sleeping in the same room with Sujata, Heena, Tina, and the children. Further investigation revealed that Chetan had also registered a court marriage with Tina. On the night the three sisters jumped from the balcony of the prayer room, Chetan was in a separate room with Tina. A pocket diary was recovered from the room shared by Nishika, Prachi, and Pakhi. The diary contained eight pages in which the girls had written their thoughts and complaints. Police are treating this as a suicide note, but it is not yet clear which of the three sisters wrote the entries. The pages are now being sent for forensic handwriting analysis. Police have also contacted the schools of the girls to obtain writing samples, which will help determine which sister authored the notes. On the evening of 7 February, State Women’s Commission Chairperson Babita Chauhan visited Bharat City Society and inspected flat number 907. In the presence of police, she examined whether the girls could have committed suicide from that window. During the visit, Babita Chauhan also spoke with the family members. Father Chetan Nishika was using mobile phone, I scolded her Chetan told police that he had scolded his eldest daughter, Nishika, for using her mobile phone excessively. On the night of 3 February, he was sleeping in a room with his third wife, Tina, along with his three-year-old daughter, Debu. His first wife, Sujata, and second wife, Heena, were sleeping in the adjacent room with the three daughters. His seven-year-old son was also in that room. In the evening, he had told Nishika that her education had already been stopped and that she would soon be married. He warned her that she could not use her mobile phone if she wanted to stay in the house. Chetan said that all three girls went to the temple room at night and locked the door from the inside. After that, they jumped from the balcony. Sujata woke him up, and he went downstairs with her. The bodies of all three daughters were lying there. Some other people and the building guard had also arrived. The door had been locked from inside and was only broken when police arrived. First Wife Sujata Daughters were on the bed, we were sleeping on mattresses Sujata told police that she was in the room with her sister Heena and the three daughters. Two mattresses were spread on the floor. Nishika (16), Prachi (14), and Pakhi (12) were on the bed along with the seven-year-old son. At night, Prachi was using her mobile phone, and Nishika had been scolded by Chetan. Suddenly, all three daughters woke up, kissed her on the cheek, and said they loved her. She assumed it was their way of showing affection. They then went to the temple room and locked the door from inside. Becoming suspicious, she woke her husband in the other room, but by then the girls had jumped. Second wife Heena Daughters locked the gate from inside Heena said that she and her elder sister Sujata had married Chetan willingly. Together, they had three daughters and one son. All three daughters committed suicide. She described that at around 2 AM, the middle daughter, Prachi, woke up while using her mobile phone, then woke Nishika and Pakhi, and went outside. They locked the gate of the adjacent room from inside. She said they stopped hearing the girls’ voices and later discovered that they had jumped. When they reached downstairs, they found all three covered in blood, and she lost consciousness. Third Wife Tina First Chetan told me I was unmarried, got a separate flat for me Tina, 22, told police that she had a court marriage with Chetan four years ago and is from Seelampur, Delhi. Initially, Chetan told her he was unmarried and kept her in another society. Nine months ago, she came to this flat but there were disputes, so she sometimes stayed in a separate room in the flat. She said Chetan often scolded the eldest and second daughters for using mobile phones. On the night of the suicides, she was sleeping with Chetan and their three-year-old child, and was not in the daughters’ room. Sister-in-law's fall will also be investigated DCP Trans Hindon, Nimish Patil, stated that about six years ago, Chetan had lived in Sahibabad, where his sister-in-law Anshika had also died from a fall. No post-mortem was conducted at that time. The case will now be investigated to determine the circumstances of her death. DCP Nimish Patil added that statements from family members and other witnesses have been recorded and so far all statements are matching. The handwriting from the diary pages is under analysis.

stories.title: UP govt spends 50% of last budget so far:100% funds released for pensions; health, and infrastructure see major cuts
stories.summary: Finance Minister Suresh Khanna will present the Uttar Pradesh Budget for the financial year 2026–27 in the Assembly on February 11. What relief or incentives the government offers in this election year will be known on budget day, but an assessment of the previous budget reveals important trends. More than 11 months after the last budget, the state government has released only Rs. 4,70,835.97 crore, just 54.42%, out of the approved budget of Rs. 8,65,079.46 crore. Due to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s regular review of budget expenditure, departments have spent Rs. 4,28,495.95 crore, which is 91% of the released amount. Here is a department-wise snapshot of allocations and spending. Budget for FY 2025–26 Finance Minister Suresh Khanna presented a budget of Rs. 8,08,736 crore on February 20, 2025. Two supplementary budgets—during the monsoon and winter sessions, expanded the total size to Rs. 8,65,079.46 crore. By February 6, the Finance Department had approved Rs. 5,17,168.91 crore (59.78%) for departments and released Rs. 4,70,835.97 crore (54.42%). Departments spent Rs. 4,17,305.32 crore (48.23%) by January 31 and Rs. 4,28,495.95 crore (49.53%) by February 6. Education gets priority The Finance Ministry has been generous to Basic, Secondary, Higher and Vocational Education departments. These departments have spent over 85% of their allocated budgets. No compromise on security Security spending remains a priority. Over 95% of the budget has been released to Police and Home Guards under the Home Department, which is headed by CM Yogi. More than 60% of the budget has also been released for prisons. Treasury open for food supply Around 74% of the budget has been released for food and logistics supply within 10 months. The Sugar Department has received 82.63% of its budget for sugarcane farmers. Tight spending on health The Finance Ministry showed restraint in Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak’s Family Welfare Department. In 11 months, Family Welfare received 59.75% of its budget, while Medical Education received 68.44%. The Medical and Health Department received 69.30% of its allocation. Transport department faces cuts Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh’s department has received only 42.60% of its approved budget so far. Sabka saath–sabka vikas Reflecting inclusive development, 91.31% of the budget has been released to the Muslim Waqf. Infrastructure focus, but limited funds Despite the government’s emphasis on infrastructure-led growth, allocations remain modest. The Energy Department received 69.27%, Urban Development 47.22%, PWD 60% for roads and 47.81% for bridges, Housing 52.33%, and Civil Aviation 61.88%. Under Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh, Namami Gange received only 39.11%, while the Irrigation Department got 45% of its budget. Social welfare spending Around 90% of the budget has been released for OBC and disability-related schemes, 70% for labour welfare, and 69.77% for the Women’s Welfare Department headed by Bebirani Maurya. Keshav and Rajbhar’s departments Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya’s Rural Development Department received 59.58% of its budget in 11 months. Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar’s department received 59.71%. Experts note that with Panchayat elections expected on time, low allocations to these departments could be concerning. Full payment of pensions The Finance Ministry has released and spent 100% of the budget for pensions and allowances, with no delay or cuts. Industrial development budget lags Despite strong focus on industrial growth, Industrial Development Minister Nand Gopal Gupta Nandi’s department received less than 45% of its budget. MSME Minister Rakesh Sachan’s department received over 60%. Disaster budget largely unused Only 22.99% of the budget for natural disaster management was spent, as no major calamities occurred. Revenue falling short Finance Department officials admit revenue collection is below target, affecting fund releases. By January, the state earned Rs. 1,78,556.43 crore—74.1% of the Rs. 2,40,980.67 crore tax revenue target. GST, VAT show no growth GST revenue in January 2026 stood at Rs. 7,161.95 crore, slightly lower than Rs. 7,167.29 crore in January 2025. VAT revenue was Rs. 2,816.47 crore in January 2026, marginally higher than Rs. 2,797.32 crore last year. Former UP Additional Chief Secretary (Finance) Sanjeev Mittal said governments often prepare large budgets based on political priorities, but actual spending depends on income. “When revenue does not match projections, full budget release is not possible,” he said.

stories.title: Ghaziabad suicide case takes new turn:Police re-examine suicide notes; father’s claims and sister-in-law’s death under scrutiny
stories.summary: The suicide of three young sisters in Ghaziabad, which initially appeared straightforward, has now become increasingly complex. At times, the father’s statements come under scrutiny, while the absence of both mothers from public view has further deepened suspicion. The spot from where the three girls allegedly jumped makes it physically difficult for all of them to leap together. One girl’s body was found barely one foot away from the apartment wall, raising further questions. Earlier, Chetan’s sister-in-law had also died after falling from an apartment where the family previously lived. At the time, the family termed it an accident. However, in light of the latest incident, people are now linking the two cases. The Dainik Bhaskar team continues to bring every aspect of the case to light. In this Sunday Big Story, we examine the questions surrounding the incident. Chetan married three times, allegedly neglected the children Chetan lived with his family in flat number 907 of Bharat City Society in Ghaziabad. He works in online share trading. He lived with three wives—Sujata, Hina and Tina. Sujata and Hina are real sisters. Another sister, Neha, frequently visited the house. According to family members, Chetan married Hina because he did not have children initially with Sujata. Later, both wives had children. Sujata has Nishika and Lavish, while Hina gave birth to Prachi and Pakhi. Tina has a four-year-old daughter named Debu. The same building from where the three girls fell Chetan’s father-in-law, Dilip Kumar, lives in Seelampur, Delhi. He earlier worked as a taxi driver but has been confined to home for the past two years due to a leg ailment. He said he has 14 children—11 daughters and three sons. Sujata, his eldest daughter, was married to Chetan. When Sujata did not conceive initially, Hina was also married to Chetan. Chetan earlier did small jobs, then entered property dealing, vehicle financing and house renovation for resale. During that phase, he earned well and used to travel in a Fortuner. Business losses, children pulled out of school Chetan earlier lived in a flat in Shalimar Garden’s Ekta Park in Delhi, later shifting to Rajendra Nagar in Sahibabad. Gradually, his business declined. Losses in online trading led to mounting debt. As a result, the daughters’ education was discontinued. Nikita studied up to Class 4, Prachi up to Class 3, and Pakhi up to Class 2. After that, the girls stayed home and spent most of their time watching Korean dramas and videos on mobile phones. Korean culture dominated their lives The girls occupied one room where they lived together. Korean culture deeply influenced them. They adopted similar looks, changed their names, and even began speaking in a similar style. Chetan stated that he had been negligent and failed to pay attention to his children. He claimed the girls were influenced by Korean personalities and urged the government to ban Korean videos, serials and games, saying they negatively affect children. Sold girls' mobile phone due to financial constraints The girls had two mobile phones. Due to financial hardship, Chetan sold one phone six months ago and sold the second one 15 days before the incident. This left the girls isolated. Investigations revealed that the girls occasionally used their mother Sujata’s phone. Some society residents said they heard abusive arguments from Chetan’s house on the night of February 3. Around 2 am, a loud sound was heard as the girls fell from the building. Both mothers rushed downstairs and sat near the bodies, crying uncontrollably. Sujata removed her clothes and placed them over the bodies, repeatedly hitting her chest with her slippers and shouting abuses. She reportedly said, “I will tell everything you did.” Police arrived shortly after and sent the bodies for post-mortem. Since then, both women have remained out of public view. Most questions are being answered only by the father, Chetan. Domestic conflict in the household Due to multiple marriages, frequent disputes took place at home. To avoid conflict, Chetan frequently changed residences. He had another flat in Bharat City where Tina reportedly lived. On February 6, when Chetan went there to recharge electricity, people recognised him. After the incident, Tina reportedly moved elsewhere. Sister-in-law also died from falling Chetan’s father-in-law Dilip said that around six to seven years ago, during Nishika’s birthday, his sixth daughter Anchal visited Chetan’s house in Shalimar Garden, Ekta Park. While removing clothes from the balcony, she slipped and fell, dying on the spot. She was around 16 years old. The family considered it an accident and did not file a police complaint. How did they jump from such a small window? The balcony area from where the girls allegedly jumped had barely enough space to stand. The window was about four feet above the room floor. A plastic stool was found near the spot. The window measured approximately 2.5 feet in height and 1.75 feet in width. All three girls could not have stood together at the window. One body was found just one foot from the building wall, while the other two were found eight and nine feet away. Police are trying to understand how this difference occurred. Suicide note under handwriting examination Police recovered a small diary from the room, containing an eight-page suicide note. The note refers to Korean culture and Korean dramas. At one point, it states, “Papa, sorry… I am unable to quit the game. Now you will realise how much we loved the game you wanted us to give up.” Police are examining the handwriting of the suicide letter. This is a page from the diary, which says that the reader should read it carefully as everything written in it is true. It ends with the words “Sorry Papa.” The suicide letter uses the word “I”; police say that if all three girls had written it together, the word “we” would have been used. Another point noted is that the letter mentions only the father and not the mother. The apology is also addressed only to the father. However, after the deaths, the women were seen crying loudly near the bodies, indicating that the mothers were deeply attached to their daughters. In contrast, Chetan stood silently at the spot, wore a mask the next day and did not speak to anyone. He has now locked the house and moved elsewhere. According to the post-mortem report, the fall from such a height caused all the girls’ ribs to break. Their internal organs, including the heart, liver, lungs and kidneys, were ruptured. The report also revealed that only 50 grams of food was found in Nishika’s stomach, while 200–300 grams of food was found in the stomachs of Prachi and Pakhi. This indicates that Nishika had not eaten anything after the afternoon, while the other two girls had eaten dinner. According to Chetan, Prachi was the leader among the three. The question now being raised is that if Prachi was the leader, then why did Nishika not eat food? Police also inspected the spot from where the girls fell to their deaths. At present, the police are trying to link all aspects of the case and are awaiting multiple investigation reports. DCP Trans Hindon Nimish Patil said the team is probing the case from several angles, and all emerging points are being included in the investigation. The crime scene inside the house has been recreated, revealing some facts. Mobile phones sold by Chetan are being traced so that data can be recovered and the complete picture can be established.

stories.title: 'Rent a womb' syndicate active in Prayagraj:Gang ran operations for 8 years, kept girl at dargah and lured her to donate eggs for lakhs
stories.summary: Prayagraj police exposed a shocking illegal racket involving the sale of human eggs for so-called “rent-a-womb” arrangements. During the investigation, police reached five suspects, including four women. The racket was operating from inside an IVF centre, where eggs were taken from young girls through minor surgeries and sold to wealthy childless women for large sums of money. According to police, the deals ranged between ₹2 lakh and ₹5 lakh per case. The operation was being run from an IVF centre located in the Civil Lines area of the city. The registered agent of the centre, Kalpana, was arrested. During questioning, police found that she had falsely shown a 15-year-old girl, Komal, as an adult by using fake Aadhaar cards and forged documents. Her associate, Himanshu, had allegedly helped in preparing these fake documents. Police were still trying to find out how many girls were exploited in the last eight years and to whom their eggs were sold. Investigators were also looking into claims that some girls were brainwashed and forced to convert to Islam. All five accused were being questioned. So far, the investigation has proceeded based on the statements of a 15-year-old girl, Komal (name changed). This girl's eggs were extracted. The price set was just 1 iPhone and 15 thousand rupees. The girl's mother, Shalini (name changed), reached the police. When the investigation began, 5 people were arrested one by one. It came to light that for about 8 years, these people used to prepare girls in Prayagraj to donate eggs for surrogacy. For this, they were given a fixed amount. People working in this syndicate were given 2 types of tasks. First - preparing girls to donate eggs. Second - brainwashing girls and instigating them to convert to Islam. Know who all were arrested, what tasks they received 19-year-old Palak is Rinki's daughter. She was mostly active on social media. She mostly befriended young girls. Then, while chatting, she would lure them with jobs as caterers, waiters, and agents. When she met the girls, she would take them to her mother Rinki. These people provided good mobile phones to many girls. They made girls under pressure donate ova at IVF centers in different districts. Rinky, a seemingly ordinary woman, was in the role of a leader in the syndicate. When Palak brought girls to her, she would tell them, "Okay, we will get you a job." Then, the concept of donating eggs for IVF was explained to them. Giving money after egg donation, and then gradually, once the girls gained trust, taking them to a Dargah this was part of their planning. Komal was also taken to a Dargah in Prayagraj for 6 days. Kalpana was a registered agent of the IVF Center. She handled the internal workings of the IVF Center. In Komal's case, she had used a fake Aadhaar card and affidavit to present a 15-year-old girl as a 22-year-old married woman. Kalpana used to contact wealthy childless women who came to the IVF Center. She would deal in millions of rupees. She would guarantee that they would have a child after the process. The biggest task for Seema was to find new girls. She was constantly searching for new girls in the field. So that, with the help of Rinki and Kalpana, they could be brought into the process of donating eggs. There was a commission of 30 to 35 thousand rupees on each girl. In the syndicate, Himanshu had the task of preparing fake documents. He would take the names, addresses, and pictures of girls and, with their help, create fake Aadhaar cards and affidavits. Not only that, he also did photo editing on the documents. He also made fake marriage certificates. With the help of these, the girls' eggs were donated. Girls were kept in the Dargah for 4-5 hours Police interrogated all five accused for a long time, and it came to light that Komal was brainwashed before her eggs were donated. She was made to understand that there is a very free environment in Islam. There is security in a burqa. Palak and Rinky also used to take Komal to a famous Dargah. She was taken there for 6 consecutive days and was also introduced to some Maulanas there. Komal was kept there for 4-5 hours. She was told about Muslim customs and traditions. Many times, Muslim dishes were also served to her. Palak often used to tell Komal, "Find a Muslim name of your choice with the help of Google. When you convert to Islam, your identity will also become new. You will also get the benefits available to minorities. First decide on a name, then we will ask the Maulana for its meaning in Arabic." First Prayagraj, then egg donation in the surrounding districts Komal was also assured that she would continue to receive a fixed amount after becoming a donor. First in Prayagraj, then in Kaushambi, Pratapgarh, Jaunpur, Bhadohi, Mirzapur, she would have to donate eggs at IVF centres. Not only this, it was also said that she would have to connect more girls like herself to this syndicate. The entire business is based on commission. The more girls there are, the more money will increase. Palak had told Komal that she had been a donor before. Because she is now married, there is no problem at all. Komal was told that once everything was set, they would get her married to a good Muslim boy. Even after marriage, she could continue the work of egg donation. Apprehension of IVF Center's complicity After the unearthing of this gang, the activities of the IVF center are also being investigated. So far, only the registered agent of the center has been sent to jail. In fact, the entire process of the IVF center is very tough. Along with documents, doctors' examinations and several forms are filled. In such a situation, how can just one agent run the entire system? Therefore, complicity of more people is also being suspected. Sindoor in Komal's hair parting, saree pallu When inquiries were made at the IVF center, they told the police that Priya was shown as married in the documents. Her registration was done under the name Priya Deepak. The same name was also registered on her Aadhaar. Whenever Priya was taken there, she was made to wear sindoor in her hair parting and a mangalsutra around her neck. The pallu of the saree or dupatta was draped in such a way that her face was not clearly visible. The getup was such that the girl looked completely married. 5 arrests made, investigation still ongoing DCP Kuldeep Singh Gunawat said - The first complaint was received from a woman. Tracing her, 5 people have been arrested. It has come to light that ova were donated at an IVF center. This was done with the help of some fake documents. The girl was 15 years old, but she was shown as married. We are currently investigating the matter.

stories.title: Jeweller’s son brutally attacked in Jhansi gym, video surfaces:Goons beat him after he refuses to vacate machine
stories.summary: A shocking incident of brutality surfaced in Jhansi, where a jeweller’s son was brutally assaulted by goons inside a gym. The attackers smashed his head with a dumbbell and repeatedly struck him with an iron rod. They also thrashed anyone who tried to intervene. After a struggle, people managed to rescue the youth and pull him out. Blood was flowing profusely from his head, and his clothes were drenched in blood. Actually, the young man was exercising in the gym as usual when the goon came with his friends. He said, ‘I want to work out. Vacate this machine.’ When he refused, the goon slapped him, and then his friends held the young man. The goon attacked him with a dumbbell. The attackers continued to brutally assault him with rods, kicks and punches. Bleeding heavily, the young man reached home, after which his father first took him to a police outpost. He was then sent to the hospital for medical examination. The incident took place at around 9 pm on February 6 at M-2 Gym on Filter Road, under the Kotwali police station area. CCTV footage of the assault surfaced the next day, Saturday. Police have registered a case against four unidentified youths. Three pictures Read the full case sequentially CCTV footage surfaces Two CCTV footages related to the incident have surfaced. In the first 4-minute 9-second video, a dispute is seen during exercise on a machine. Other people at the gym intervene and calm the matter. They separate Rohit and the 'Dabang' (bully/strongman). Meanwhile, the 'Dabang' youth approaches Rohit, saying something. When the argument escalates again, Rohit slaps him, and then the 'Dabang' and his companions brutally beat Rohit. The 'Dabang' is seen slapping Rohit and attacking him with dumbbells and rods. In the second CCTV, Rohit appears to be bleeding profusely. Identifying the accused from CCTV Kotwali Police Station in-charge Vidyasagar Singh said- Based on Rohit's complaint, a case has been registered on Saturday against 4 unknown youths under sections including assault and others. The accused are being identified based on CCTV footage. Details about the accused are also being taken from the gym owner. They will be arrested soon.

stories.title: Noida man shoots girlfriend on Valentine's Day:Then ends his own life; both bodies found inside car
stories.summary: On Valentine's Day, a lover shot and killed his girlfriend in a car, then committed suicide by shooting himself in Noida. Both bodies were found inside the car. People nearby arrived after hearing the gunshot. They called the police. When the Tata Altroz car door was opened, both bodies were found on the front seat. A pistol was lying beside them. Police took possession of both their mobile phones. The couple is said to be residents of Trilokpuri in Delhi. It is reported that a missing complaint for the girlfriend was filed on Friday at Sector 58 police station in Noida. Currently, police are questioning people in the area. The forensic team has also collected evidence. The incident occurred in the Sector-39 police station area.
