stories.title: AIMIM starts preparing for UP 2027 elections:SP and Congress challenge Owaisi to translate numbers into public rallies and advocate for the oppressed
stories.summary: In the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Asaduddin Owaisi’s party AIMIM has started mobilising. The All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen claims to have added over 10 lakh members in UP in the past two months. According to the party, over 86 lakh members are now registered across the state. AIMIM is steadily increasing its presence in UP and claims it will perform better in the 2027 Assembly elections, similar to its results in Bihar and Maharashtra. Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress have accused Owaisi of indulging in religion-based politics and benefiting the BJP. Read on for the full report… During a membership camp in Kanpur, AIMIM members were present. Congress leader speaks on AIMIM and Owaisi Former Congress city president Naushad Alam Mansoori said that AIMIM’s politics is religion-based and such an organisation can never manage the country. He alleged that the BJP government encourages such organisations, allowing them to grow. He added that if AIMIM truly has 87 lakh members, they should show courage and hold a rally in UP with at least 2 lakh people in attendance. He questioned that despite the atrocities in UP, Owaisi has only been seen giving speeches and has not been on the streets. SP’s comments on AIMIM and Owaisi SP leaders said AIMIM’s membership claims are a private matter. However, if there is any alternative to the BJP in UP, it is only the Samajwadi Party. They added that AIMIM is under a misconception that having so many members will automatically give them a major advantage. Yes, some of their corporators have won, but municipal elections are individual contests. SP leaders described Owaisi as a good speaker, saying that while he delivers good speeches in the house, he could secure better justice for the poor and oppressed by advocating for them in the Supreme Court. They also stated that celebrating just five corporator wins is not significant. If anyone has truly worked for Muslims in UP, it has been only Akhilesh Yadav and earlier Mulayam Singh Yadav. AIMIM leaders respond to SP-Congress Kanpur city vice-president Noor Alam said that Congress and SP accuse AIMIM of being the BJP’s ‘B-team’. He questioned why SP members secretly register for AIMIM membership while their own party is gradually becoming a “declining party.” He added that instead of making accusations, SP should focus on its own work. What AIMIM claims The party first entered UP in 2012. Party’s state general secretary (Central Zone) Azhar Alam said that the enthusiasm among party workers has increased following the party’s strong performance in Maharashtra municipal elections. He added that the party’s growing presence in Bihar has attracted large numbers of supporters nationwide. According to him, there are currently 87 lakh registered members in UP, with over 10 lakh added in the last 40 days of the membership campaign. In Kanpur, membership camps are held every two to three days. So far, 40,000 members have joined in the city. Along with camps, online membership drives are also being conducted. AIMIM claims that it is already strong in UP, holding five chairmen positions and 83 corporators. Both young and elderly citizens are joining the party in significant numbers.

stories.summary: In the Gida police station area of Gorakhpur, a young man was killed by having his throat slit on Saturday morning. After the murder, the blood-soaked body was dumped in a field. Farmers who discovered the body early on Saturday morning were shocked. They immediately informed the village head, Raju Nishad, and the local police. The police team reached the spot and sealed off the entire area. Investigations are underway. Local residents reported that a knife was stuck in the young man’s chest. Multiple wounds were also found on his stomach and other parts of his body. His clothes were soaked in blood. See 3 pictures... The incident took place in Pevanpur village of Siwan. An unidentified young man’s body was found. He had been murdered by having his throat slit, and a knife was also lodged in his chest. Upon receiving the information, the police reached the scene immediately. Villagers reported that the approximately 22-year-old youth’s body was discovered in the morning, which drew a crowd to the site. The body bore multiple stab wounds, and one knife remained embedded in his chest. Gida Inspector Ashwani Kumar Pandey and Nausad police station in-charge Kamlesh Pratap Singh, along with their teams, arrived at the scene. A forensic team was immediately called, which collected important evidence from the site. According to the police, the identity of the deceased has not yet been confirmed. Inspector Ashwani Kumar Pandey stated that the police are making efforts to identify the deceased and conduct a thorough investigation of the incident. The news is being updated.

stories.title: Window too narrow for three sisters to jump together:Police spend five hours recreating scene in Ghaziabad triple suicide case
stories.summary: As police continue to probe the triple suicide incident in Ghaziabad, investigators have concluded that it was technically impossible for two or three children to jump together from the same window of the flat. The finding emerged after police spent nearly five hours inside Flat No. 907, recreating the crime scene to determine the sequence of events. The girls had allegedly jumped from a window of the ninth-floor apartment in Bharat City Society. During the reconstruction, police opened the window from which the sisters fell and placed a plastic stool to assess whether more than one child could stand there simultaneously. The experiment showed that only one child could jump at a time. It is to be noted that on the night of February 3, at 2 AM, three girls died after falling from the 9th floor of Tower B-1 of Bharat City Society. From 8 pages of a pocket diary found in the room, it was revealed that the girls were fond of Korean culture. Their mobile phones had been snatched away, which made them upset. What new facts emerged in the 4-day police investigation? Read this in the report… Father questioned after contradictions in marriage claims Following this discovery, police conducted a prolonged interrogation of Chetan Kumar, the father of the deceased girls. Investigators found inconsistencies in the narrative he provided regarding his marriages. Chetan had earlier claimed that he married his second wife due to childlessness. However, police found that several facts related to this claim do not align, prompting further verification. Authorities are now examining whether false information was deliberately provided during the investigation. Incident occurred at 2 AM on February 3 The incident took place around 2 am on February 3, when three sisters—Nishika (16), Prachi (14), and Pakhi (12)—fell from the ninth floor of Tower B-1 in Bharat City Society, resulting in their deaths. An eight-page pocket diary recovered from the room revealed that the girls were deeply influenced by Korean culture. The notes suggested they were distressed after their mobile phones were taken away. Several new facts have emerged during four days of police investigation. CCTV footage and family’s location under scrutiny CCTV cameras installed in the society captured visuals at 2:03 am, showing Chetan Kumar, his wives Sujata and Hina, and sister-in-law Tina going downstairs. Police are also reconstructing who slept in which room that night. In the three-bedroom flat, Chetan was sleeping with his two wives and sister-in-law, along with his son and youngest daughter, Debu. Investigators are questioning how the adults failed to notice the girls’ actions in the adjacent room. Confusion over family relationships According to Chetan’s statement, he married Sujata in 2006. He claimed the families were acquainted as both fathers worked as taxi drivers. After a few months, the couple moved from Delhi to Ghaziabad. Chetan told police that due to childlessness until 2009, he married Sujata’s sister Hina with Sujata’s consent. However, police found contradictions regarding the identity of Tina and the parentage of the youngest child, Debu. Initially, Chetan stated that Debu was Hina’s daughter. Later, it emerged that he had legally married Tina through a court marriage, and Debu is Tina’s child. Police are now verifying these claims. Financial troubles: Trading losses and debt Police also examined Chetan’s financial background. He is one of four brothers; two live in Shalimar City and one in Delhi. His parents are deceased. The family owns two plots measuring 700 and 70 square yards in Delhi’s Khajuri area. When questioned about alleged Rs 2 crore losses in share trading, Chetan claimed that his actual loss was Rs 10 lakh, with another Rs 10 lakh borrowed to meet household expenses. Korean contacts and seized mobile phones The suicide note revealed that the sisters communicated with Korean friends through their youngest sister. Police are yet to determine the nature of these contacts or the social media platforms used. Chetan admitted to selling the girls’ mobile phones. One phone was sold three months ago, while the other was sold ten days before the incident. Nishika and Prachi each had a phone. The only phone found in the room belonged to their mother, Sujata. Police found no Korean apps, games, or data on this device, nor any evidence of connection to Korean online platforms. In the suicide note, one page of a diary and some writings on the walls were repeatedly crossed out. See its pictures Phones being traced through IMEI numbers Police are now using IMEI numbers to trace the sold phones. Once recovered, the devices will be sent for forensic examination to retrieve deleted data and identify any digital interactions. Post-mortem findings: Severe internal injuries According to post-mortem reports, the sisters fell from a height of approximately 80 feet, resulting in multiple fractures and severe internal organ damage, including ruptured heart, liver, lungs, and kidneys. Doctors stated that survival chances after such a fall are extremely low. No old injuries or signs of assault were found on the bodies. Food intake analysis revealed that Nishika had eaten only 50 grams of food two hours before the fall, while Prachi and Pakhi had consumed 250–300 grams, indicating they had dinner that night. Cause of death: Hemorrhage Medical expert Dr. Sanjeev stated that the sisters died due to excessive bleeding (hemorrhage) caused by extensive bodily injuries. The post-mortems were conducted by doctors from Christian Medical College. Police statement DCP Trans-Hindon Nimish Patil said police are investigating all angles. “The crime scene was recreated inside the flat, and several important facts have emerged. Efforts are underway to recover the mobile phones sold by Chetan so that the complete digital trail can be examined,” he said.

stories.title: Akhilesh aide seizes YouTuber’s phone in Kannauj:SP chief asks if questions are ‘coming from BJP’, supporters raise slogans
stories.summary: At a public interaction in Kannauj, an aide to Akhilesh Yadav, Ashish Yadav, briefly seized a YouTuber’s mobile phone after noticing that the questions being posed were appearing as written prompts on the device. According to those present, Ashish Yadav examined the WhatsApp messages on the phone, photographed the questions and showed them to Mr. Yadav. Responding to this, the Samajwadi Party president made a sarcastic remark, asking whether the questions were “coming from the BJP,” before breaking into laughter. Mr. Yadav then asked journalists present to identify themselves by name, remarking that such information helped determine whether the questioners were adequately informed. The exchange prompted slogans from party supporters gathered at the venue. Later, Mr. Yadav inaugurated a local cricket tournament, participating briefly in both batting and bowling. Addressing broader political issues, he accused the Bharatiya Janata Party of diverting the attention of the younger generation through campaigns such as ‘Ghuskhoor Pandit’ and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. He said the government was doing so because it had failed to generate jobs or employment opportunities and was apprehensive of an increasingly discontented youth population. Akhilesh Yadav’s key remarks 1. On the OTT film controversy Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav said people needed to be cautious of the Bharatiya Janata Party, arguing that the same authorities that cleared a controversial film for release on OTT platforms were now allowing cases to be filed over it. He alleged that citizens were being deliberately “entangled”, noting that individuals could face trouble regardless of whether they supported or opposed the film. He further claimed that the funding for such OTT content was likely to have come from individuals linked to the BJP. 2. On U.S. tariffs and ‘Swadeshi’ Referring to reports of the United States reducing tariffs, Mr. Yadav remarked sarcastically that Indians would now “eat American food, wear American clothes and praise America”. He questioned the silence of BJP leaders who, he said, had earlier been vocal proponents of Swadeshi, asking where those voices had gone. 3. On youth, jobs and SIR Mr. Yadav alleged that the BJP was fearful of the younger generation as it had failed to provide adequate jobs and employment opportunities. He claimed that young voters were instead being drawn into the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. Citing an example from Lucknow, he alleged that Muslim votes had been deleted using forged signatures under Hindu names such as Dasharath and Nandlal Kashyap. According to him, an inquiry revealed that one of the named individuals did not know how to sign and used only a thumb impression. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav attended a series of programmes in Kannauj on Friday, paying condolences to bereaved families and participating in a private function. Mr. Yadav first visited Tirwa, where he reached the residence of late Parmanand Tiwari and paid tribute by offering flowers to his portrait. He also met family members and expressed his condolences. He later paid homage to Pratham Pandey, the son of women’s wing leader Sangeet Pandey, who died recently. He subsequently visited the Abantibai Nagar locality, where he met the family of Jaikaran Yadav and offered condolences on the death of his son. Mr. Yadav also went to the residence of Samajwadi Party leader Anshul Yadav to pay tribute following the death of his father. During the course of the visit, Mr. Yadav expressed condolences to the families of Anand Katheria and Abeer Ali as well. The tour concluded at Hotel BK Grand, where Mr. Yadav attended the wedding ceremony of Vishal Dixit, son of perfume businessman Ram Dixit, and extended his blessings to the newly married couple.

stories.title: Over 12 ministers may be replaced in UP:Second cabinet expansion likely soon; BJP plans Gujarat model reshuffle ahead of key elections
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief minister Yogi Adityanath-led government is preparing for its second cabinet expansion, which is expected to take place soon. Keeping the 2027 Assembly polls and this year’s Panchayat elections in sight, the ruling Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) is reportedly considering a major reshuffle on the lines of the Gujarat model, potentially dropping more than half of the current ministers. According to party sources, over 12 ministers are likely to be replaced, while around 15 MLAs and party office-bearers could be inducted to create new social and political equations. What is the Saffron Party's strategy? Which new faces can get a place in the cabinet? What is the Gujarat model? Why is there a need to adopt it here? Read the special news… Current strength of the Yogi cabinet At present, the Yogi government includes 21 cabinet ministers, 14 ministers of state with independent charge, and 19 ministers of state, apart from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak—taking the total strength to 54 ministers. The maximum permissible size of the cabinet is 60, leaving room for six additional inductions. The first cabinet expansion of Yogi Government 2.0 took place on March 5, 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, when Om Prakash Rajbhar (SBSP), Anil Kumar (RLD), Sunil Sharma and Dara Singh Chauhan were inducted. With Pankaj Chaudhary becoming the BJP’s Uttar Pradesh president in December 2025 and Nitin Nabin recently taking charge as national president, political circles believe the cabinet expansion is now imminent. Why is a cabinet overhaul being considered? 1. Making space for new faces and leadership According to party sources, a section of the central leadership favors a major cabinet reset, removing up to 50% of the existing ministers and replacing them with fresh faces from the party organization and legislature. The proposal suggests sending outgoing ministers into the field for at least a year to focus on election strategy and ground-level mobilization. The move is expected to correct social equations, energize governance, and address internal dissatisfaction among party workers and legislators. However, another faction within the party advises caution, arguing that major changes in an election year could be risky. They recommend minor reshuffles or portfolio changes instead, warning that dropped ministers may defect to rival parties like the Samajwadi Party. 2. Addressing public discontent Multiple complaints against ministers have reportedly reached both state and central leadership through MLAs, RSS functionaries and party workers. Feedback from RSS coordination meetings has also flagged dissatisfaction over the performance of several ministers. What is the Gujarat model and why Uttar Pradesh needs it Ahead of the 2022 Gujarat Assembly elections, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel accepted the resignations of 16 ministers and formed a new cabinet after consultations with the central leadership. Out of 26 ministers, 19 were fresh faces. The strategy proved successful, as the BJP won 156 of 182 seats, its biggest-ever mandate in Gujarat. Political experts view this approach as a political reset, aimed at balancing caste, regional and social equations while neutralizing public anger against incumbent ministers. Analysts believe a similar strategy in Uttar Pradesh—inducting new faces while sidelining underperformers—could help the BJP regain momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Political analyst and journalist Virendra Nath Bhatt said that ministers facing dissatisfaction among the public, party workers, government and RSS could be removed, while new inductions would send a clear message that performance matters. Samajwadi Party rebels may also find a place Some of the seven MLAs who rebelled against the Samajwadi Party and joined the BJP may be rewarded with ministerial berths. Names doing the rounds include Manoj Pandey (Unchahar) and Rakesh Pratap Singh (Gauriganj). An audio clip allegedly featuring Manoj Pandey’s son claiming his father would soon become a minister recently went viral. There is also speculation that Pooja Pal could be inducted to project a strong female face against the SP, though senior leaders downplay this possibility. When could the cabinet expansion happen? Political observers see two possible timelines: Senior journalist Yogesh Mishra, however, downplays the likelihood of a major reshuffle. He believes the cabinet expansion will occur between February and March, with only the five to six vacant positions being filled by a mix of old and new faces. According to him, the BJP is not in a position to risk a large-scale purge of ministers, as such a move could destabilize the leadership structure. However, a cabinet expansion is inevitable. Even without major changes, Jat and Brahmin representation likely Political analysts agree that even if sweeping changes are avoided, the cabinet is likely to include one Jat and one Brahmin minister. A Jat ministerial berth has remained vacant since former BJP state president Bhupendra Chaudhary resigned from the cabinet in 2022. Despite the BJP’s alliance with the RLD, there is currently no core-cadre Jat leader in the cabinet, making Bhupendra Chaudhary a frontrunner. Similarly, a Brahmin slot has remained vacant since Jitin Prasada joined the Union cabinet. Potential contenders include Shrikant Sharma, Shalabh Mani Tripathi, Govind Narayan Shukla, and Vijay Bahadur Pathak. Analysts note that Brahmin discontent was openly raised in a meeting of Brahmin MLAs in December, prompting intervention from the party leadership. To contain the fallout, the induction of a Brahmin MLA or MLC is considered almost certain. At present, the cabinet includes seven ministers, each from the Brahmin and Kshatriya communities.

stories.title: Ghaziabad triple suicide case:Girls’ aunt died the same way; grandfather blames son-in-law’s debt woes
stories.summary: The mystery surrounding the suicide case of three young sisters in Ghaziabad has deepened after their grandfather revealed that another girl from the same family had died earlier after falling from the same building. Dilip Kumar, the maternal grandfather of the three deceased girls—Nishika, Prachi and Pakhi—said that around six to seven years ago, one of his daughters had also died after falling from his son-in-law’s flat. At that time, the family had treated it as an accident. Under what circumstances did Dilip marry both his daughters to Chetan? What was Chetan's situation at that time? What did he do? We spoke in detail with his father-in-law, Dilip, on questions like how the situation deteriorated. Read on... “My son-in-Law Once Lived Well, Later Fell Into Debt” Speaking to reporters, Dilip Kumar said his son-in-law Chetan, was once financially stable. “Chetan had a lot of money. He owned a Fortuner car. He worked in vehicle financing and used to buy old houses, renovate them and sell them,” he said. According to him, Chetan lived in Shalimar Garden near Ekta Park in Delhi and later shifted to Ghaziabad. Over time, however, his financial condition deteriorated. “I don’t know what went wrong. He kept sinking into debt. Even the car was sold,” Dilip added. Three sisters died after jumping from ninth floor Chetan lived in Bharat City Society, Ghaziabad, with two of his wives—who are sisters—and their five children. On the night of February 3, the three girls died after falling from the ninth floor of the building. Post-mortem reports revealed that most of their body parts were badly damaged due to the fall. Initially, Chetan claimed the girls had taken their lives after playing a “Korean game,” but police investigations found no evidence supporting this theory. Soon after the incident, the family locked the flat and left. Another daughter died earlier after falling from balcony Dilip Kumar revealed that around six to seven years ago, his daughter, Anchal, aged 16–17, died after falling from the third floor of the same building where the family lived in Shalimar Garden. “She had gone there for my granddaughter Nishika’s birthday. Clothes were drying on the balcony. She slipped while removing them and fell,” he said. The family had then accepted it as an accident and did not pursue any legal action. Two sisters married to the same man Dilip Kumar said he married his eldest daughter Sujata to Chetan around 18 years ago. When Sujata could not conceive initially, the family later married their second daughter Heena to him as well. He said the children were once well cared for and attended school when the family was financially stable. However, as conditions worsened, the girls stopped going to school. “If the parents had made the girls sleep with them, this might not have happened,” he said, questioning why the children slept in a separate room. Sister-in-law falls to death from Chetan's flat About 6-7 years ago, when Chetan lived in Shalimar Garden, his sister-in-law Anchal had gone there. She died after falling from the third floor of the building. Dilip says, 'It was my granddaughter Nishika's birthday, and Anchal had gone there for that. Clothes were put out to dry on the balcony, Anchal was standing on the railing to take down the clothes, her foot slipped and she died on the spot.' Anchal was Dilip's sixth daughter, and was about 16-17 years old. At that time, the family considered it an accident and did not take any action. Limited contact with maternal family The grandfather said that over time, Chetan reduced contact between the girls and their maternal family. Festivals visits stopped, and communication became minimal. One of the sisters, Tanya, said off-camera that the girls slowly became withdrawn and stopped speaking to relatives. “Chetan was in heavy debt. He avoided people, wore masks outside and stopped talking to anyone,” she said. Police continue investigation Police officials are continuing to record statements and investigate unanswered questions. Chetan has not spoken to the media and is reportedly not allowing others to speak either. The case remains under investigation, with authorities trying to piece together the circumstances that led to the deaths of the three sisters.

stories.title: 6 killed on Yamuna Expressway in Mathura:Noida–Farrukhabad bus stops mid-route, container crushes passengers standing roadside
stories.summary: On the Yamuna Expressway in Mathura, six passengers were crushed to death by a speeding container after stepping out of a sleeper bus. One person was critically injured, while two others also sustained injuries. The accident occurred early Saturday morning at around 2:45 am. According to reports, the Agnihotri Travels sleeper bus (UP 75 BT 3907) had left Nangloi, Delhi, around midnight. The bus was packed with passengers and was heading via Noida to Farrukhabad and Rasoolabad in Kanpur Dehat. During the journey, some passengers requested the driver to stop so they could use the bathroom. Instead of stopping at a designated green zone, the driver halted the bus on the expressway itself. Several passengers got down and stood by the roadside. At that moment, a high-speed container (DL 1GE 4418) coming from behind first hit the bus and then ran over the passengers standing on the road. The container driver fled the scene immediately. After the crash, there was chaos at the site, and traffic was blocked for a considerable time. Passersby alerted the police, who rushed ambulances to take the injured to the nearest hospital. The bodies were sent for post-mortem examination. The accident took place near Milestone 88 in the Surir police station area. Victims identified Mohammad Arif, a resident of Etawah, said he was travelling to Katra on the bus. Some passengers asked to stop for the toilet, and the driver pulled over on the roadside. At that moment, the speeding container struck and crushed the passengers. Six people died on the spot, while three others were injured. Arif said his son-in-law Aslam, who worked as a tailor, was among the deceased. The deceased include Sonu, a resident of Sarwa Katra in Auraiya; Devesh from Alewal in Basti; Aslam from Ganesh Ka Purwa in Kannauj; and Santosh from Prem Nagar in Delhi. The identities of two other deceased passengers are yet to be confirmed. Amar Dubey, a resident of Bela in Auraiya, was critically injured and is receiving treatment at a hospital. Surir Station House Officer Ajay Kumar said traffic was disrupted temporarily after the accident, but movement was restored following relief and rescue operations. The police are investigating the case further. Recall of a major Expressway accident Earlier, on December 16 last year, dense fog caused a collision of eight buses and three cars on the Yamuna Expressway. The impact caused fire, killing 19 people including a BJP leader and injuring over 70 others. Police had recovered the bodies in polythene bags, and DNA tests were used to confirm their identities Surir Station House Officer Ajay Kumar said Traffic was disrupted for some time after the accident, but movement was normalized after relief and rescue operations. Police are conducting further investigation into the case. The news is being continuously updated...

stories.title: Shankaracharya asks Yogi to choose one post:Avimukteshwaranand calls dual authority un-Hindu, compares model to caliph system
stories.summary: After leaving the Magh Mela in Prayagraj, Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand is currently in Varanasi. In an interaction with the media, he spoke at length about Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, raising questions over the compatibility of religious renunciation and political office. Dainik Bhaskar had a special conversation with Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand. Read the full conversation Shankaracharya… Q: You have called CM Yogi a “fake Hindu.” What do you mean by that? Shankaracharya: We have not declared him a fake Hindu. We have raised a question mark over whether he is a true Hindu in conduct. We gave the government 40 days to prove its commitment to Sanatan Dharma. Ten days have passed. Based on our review so far, we do not see sufficient seriousness in proving adherence to Hindu principles. Q: Some say this is a political stand by you. Is it? Shankaracharya: This is not politics. We are not members of any political party, nor are we aligned against any. We act according to Dharma, not party lines. Anyone may accuse us of politics, but we are guided by scripture. Q: You have questioned the Chief Minister’s salary. Why? Shankaracharya: In our scriptures, a renunciant — a Vairagi or Sanyasi — cannot be salaried. In the Nath sect’s foundational texts, wage-based work is described as condemnable, even likened to poison. If someone has taken vows of renunciation, how can they accept a salary? Shouldn’t they follow the standards of Sanatan Dharma? Q: You also raised the issue of “Saffron versus Pink.” What does that mean? Shankaracharya: Saffron robes symbolize renunciation and non-violence. They represent a vow not to harm even a single living being. But the Chief Minister’s office promotes policies where animals are slaughtered in large numbers for revenue. Can someone wearing saffron support the meat trade? That is the contradiction we are highlighting. Q: Why did you compare the Chief Minister to a “Caliph”? Shankaracharya: In Islam, a Caliph is both the political ruler and religious head. In Hindu tradition, the king and the guru are separate. Combining both roles is not our system. Here, one person is both the Mahant of a monastery and the Chief Minister of a state. That resembles the Caliph model, which is not a Hindu tradition. Q: What is your demand, then? Shankaracharya: He must choose one position. Either remain Chief Minister and give up the Mahant’s seat, wearing simple clothes, or remain Mahant and leave the Chief Minister’s post. Both seats cannot be held together. That is not the tradition of Hindu dharma. Q: You also objected to recent government statements on animal slaughter? Shankaracharya: Yes, a minister publicly acknowledged the slaughter of buffaloes, goats, and pigs in the state. This hurts Hindu sentiments. Moreover, the Union Budget 2026 has given concessions to meat exporters. That promotes violence against living beings. It shows that revenue is being prioritised over religion. Q: You cited figures about meat production. What is your concern? Shankaracharya: Before 2017, meat production in Uttar Pradesh was around 7.5 lakh tonnes. It has now reportedly crossed 13 lakh tonnes — nearly a 60% increase. Slaughterhouses are being granted industrial status and subsidies. Meanwhile, farmers struggle for fertilisers and seeds. Is taxpayer money meant to support such activities? Q: What are your next steps? Shankaracharya: We have announced nationwide scriptural debates (Shastrarth) on February 19. On March 1, there will be an All-India gathering of saints and scholars in Varanasi. On March 11, we will present the final conclusion of our campaign in Lucknow. The issues of “Salary versus Renunciation” and “Religion versus Governance” will be publicly addressed.

stories.title: Girl flees from home after keeping snake skin in bed:Family thought she turned into ‘nagin’; investigation revealed she didn’t want to get married
stories.summary: A bizarre incident surfaced in Uttar Pradesh’s Auraiya district, where a 25-year-old woman staged a dramatic disappearance by leaving behind a 5-foot-long snake skin on her bed, triggering panic and rumours in the village. The incident took place in Singanpur village under the Fafund police station area. The woman, identified as Reena, daughter of Rakesh Valmiki, allegedly placed the snake skin along with her ring, neck thread, and bangles on her bed before leaving home around 3 am on Sunday. On Monday morning, when family members went to wake her, they found the snake skin in the room. Soon, rumours spread in the village that the woman had “turned into a snake woman”, leading to a large crowd gathering outside the house. Villagers later informed the police about her sudden disappearance. Police reached the spot and began an investigation, which revealed that the woman was in a relationship with a young man from the village, while her family was arranging her marriage elsewhere. To avoid being traced immediately and to create confusion, she allegedly planned the drama before running away. Villagers told police that the woman had been seen searching in isolated fields for the past two days, possibly looking for the snake skin used in the act. Locals also said the family was aware of her relationship and had objected to it. Station House Officer Ajay Kumar said the incident appeared to be a “fully planned drama”. He added that the woman’s mobile phone has been put under surveillance and efforts are on to trace her. Police said she is likely to be recovered soon.

stories.title: Only son dies in Prayagraj car accident before joining CRPF:Two vehicles carrying wedding guests plunge into canal; 8 people rescued, 2 bodies recovered
stories.summary: Two cars filled with wedding guests fell into a canal in Prayagraj. All 10 people in the vehicles drowned in the water. 2 people died in the accident, while 8 were rescued. Seeing both cars fall into the canal, wedding guests coming from behind ran to save them, but stopped due to high water levels in the canal. Police arrived on information and rescued 8 people safely from the water with help from local divers. After about 8 hours of overnight rescue operations, 2 bodies were recovered on Monday morning. The deceased were identified as Pradeep Kushwaha alias Pintu (30) from Banda and Anish Singh (20) from Ballia. Anish's father was in the CRPF and had died 10 years ago. Anish was about to join the CRPF in his father's position. Anish was the only son of the family. Lalji Shukla lives in Naini. His son Shubham Shukla's wedding procession was going from Naini to Vijay Kumar Pandey's house in Ghugha village of Koraon police station area. Shubham's friends were also going in the wedding procession. Around 10:30 PM on Sunday night, their car fell into the Belan main canal in the Koraon police station area. After the accident, villagers immediately started relief work. Police reached the spot after receiving information. After this, the SDRF and Fire Brigade teams arrived. Two cranes and a JCB were called to remove the cars from the canal. Water police and SDRF personnel, along with divers, safely rescued 8 members of the wedding party from the water. Two were missing. Divers continued searching for them by boat. The rescue operation continued in the canal until 4 AM, but two people were not found. The rescue resumed again at 6 AM. After this, both bodies were recovered. 22 people from government departments were involved in the rescue. Shubham Shukla, Saurabh Gautam (Rewa), Sandeep Kumar (Azamgarh), and Vishal Maurya (Jaunpur) were first removed from the Kia Seltos car. Pradeep Kushwaha, Anoop Kumar, Wasim, Anshu (Ghazipur), and Rohit Kumar (Ballia) were removed from the second i10 car. Anees was the only child of the family Anees's uncle, Virendra Kumar, said - Anees was the only one among two siblings. He was pursuing BSc. His father was in the CRPF. He died 10 years ago. The son was about to join under compassionate grounds. Pradeep got married on February 24, 2024. He had completed BSc. He was preparing for competitive exams. Father is SI in CRPF. Posted in Srinagar. February 24 was his wedding anniversary. His wife is pregnant. He used to live in the CRPF camp in Srinagar.

stories.title: Speeding trailer runs over UP woman in Udaipur:Body torn apart on highway, daughter clings to mother; driver escapes
stories.summary: A woman from Uttar Pradesh died in Rajasthan while on a family trip to Udaipur. On Monday afternoon, a speeding trailer hit her while she was crossing the road. She got stuck in the front part of the vehicle and was dragged along the road. Her body was torn apart, and pieces of flesh were scattered over a stretch of nearly 50 metres. Police reached the spot after being alerted by passers-by. The body parts were collected in polythene bags and sent for post-mortem examination. Station House Officer Kitab Devi said the deceased was Anita Yadav, wife of Brij Mohan Yadav, a resident of Patta Mohalla under the Sadar Bazar police station area in Meerut. She was travelling by bus with her younger daughter, Nidhi Yadav, to visit Khatu Shyam. After the accident, the trailer driver fled the scene. Trailer dragged the mother, body kept getting torn into pieces Daughter Nidhi Yadav said - They had come to visit Shrinathji in Ghasiyar. People from the group were getting out of the taxi one by one. My mother got down from the driver's side and would have walked only 5-7 steps. She was just 15 feet away from me. During this time, the trailer hit my mother. It kept dragging her from the front part. Her body kept getting torn into pieces. After the accident, the trailer driver stopped, and, about a minute later, fled from the scene. Police examining CCTV footage Station Officer Kitab Devi said - Upon receiving information, the Badgaon police station team immediately reached the spot. The body was removed from the road and kept in the MB Hospital mortuary. Post-mortem was conducted with the family's consent. Police have registered the case. CCTV footage installed on the highway is being examined to trace the absconding trailer. The trailer was orange in color with a Gujarat registration number and was loaded with coal. The woman had come to Udaipur 3 days ago with her daughter and a group.

stories.title: Keshav says, 'SP's PDA means Family Development Agency':'If they abandon goons’ support, party will collapse'; Congress born out of corruption, adds Maurya
stories.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya on Monday said that there is no possibility of the Samajwadi Party coming to power in Uttar Pradesh, or the Congress returning to power at the Centre, till 2047. He said making Uttar Pradesh and the country developed by 2047 is beyond the vision and capability of both parties. Addressing a BJP traders’ conference on the Union Budget in Lucknow, Maurya said the Samajwadi Party and Congress only talk about PDA. “Their PDA does not stand for social justice; it stands for ‘Parivar Development Agency’ (Family Development Agency),” he said. He added that if SP loses the support of criminals, the party would collapse immediately. Targeting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, the Deputy CM questioned the quality of opposition leadership. He said that Rahul Gandhi’s statements in Parliament do not reflect the dignity expected from the Leader of Opposition in the world’s largest democracy. “They target the Prime Minister and disrupt Parliament. The same behaviour is seen in the UP Assembly under SP,” he added. Maurya contrasted this with the conduct of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee during his time as LoP. He said BJP leaders had always maintained parliamentary decorum, even while sitting in opposition, unlike SP and Congress. He accused SP of being “born out of anarchy” and Congress of thriving on “corruption and appeasement”. The Deputy CM was speaking as the chief guest at the traders’ conference held at PWD’s Vishveshvaraya Hall. BJP state vice-president and Noida MLA Pankaj Singh also addressed the gathering. A large number of traders were present at the event. 5 Major points by Keshav Prasad Maurya 1- We are providing ration even to those who didn't vote for us, and we are also providing free treatment under Ayushman Card to them. 2- In 2027, we have to break our own record in Uttar Pradesh by making lotus bloom on all seats in Lucknow. 3- Akhilesh Yadav should go to Saifai. He is not needed in Lucknow. 4- If anyone says that we will end the constitution and remove reservations, let me tell you that the BJP worships the constitution and supports reservations. 5- After our victory in Delhi, Maharashtra and Bihar, Akhilesh Yadav is agitated. Since, he is related to Tejashwi Yadav, he will be completely wiped out here as well in 2027 You people have more vision than us The Deputy CM said - As a political worker, whatever vision we all have, you people have a better vision than that. That's why you people know a lot of things that have come in the central budget. If traders are not secure, how can they do business? When the Samajwadi Party was in government, traders were afraid. They used to say how we will do business when our money and even our lives are not safe? Our Uttar Pradesh government is a guarantee of security for the 25 crore people of Uttar Pradesh. Have continuously seen our central government's budget since 2014. When people gave Prime Minister Modi the right to form the government, at that time, a goal was set to make the country's economy 5 trillion dollars. If there is no goal, how will we know what we need to do? We are trading with the most powerful countries We have come very close to achieving the goal of becoming a $5 trillion economy. Today, India is the fourth-largest economy in the world. The whole world is stunned and cannot believe that India will make such economic progress. Today, we are trading with the most powerful countries. If they have technology and good production, India is not behind anyone today. If we have made open trade deals, you have seen that in these deals the American market and the European market have opened up for us. Industrial revolution has come to Uttar Pradesh An industrial revolution has also come to Uttar Pradesh. The country's largest state will have a share in such a big market. If goods made in Lucknow do not go to Europe and America, this open trade deal will not be properly utilised. Therefore, prepare for this. We don't have time. There is an effect of moving forward quickly. When you take more steps, the double-engine government stands with you. You all know that earlier traders were harassed in the name of VAT. When GST came after VAT, the tax was very high, but now it has been reduced. UP receives more tourists than the entire country More tourists come to Uttar Pradesh than visit the entire country. They want to buy and take something with them. Last year, 100 crore people came to Uttar Pradesh. 66 crore came for Kumbh, we're not even talking about other places yet. stories.title: Minister’s son’s Fortuner runs over man, dies:Family creates uproar, mother unconscious; demands ₹50 lakh compensation and arrest
stories.summary: A young man injured by the Fortuner of State Minister Manohar Lal Panth 'Mannu Kori's son has died in Lalitpur. Family members became enraged. They have blocked the Lalitpur-Jakhlaun road near the Howrah Bridge. People are protesting by placing the body on the road. The family members have put forward three demands. First- arrest of the minister's son. Second- financial assistance of Rs 50 lakh. Third- employment for one family member. People have placed a large electricity pole on the road. Family members are sitting under a tent. During this time, the young man's mother fainted. Bhim Army District In-charge Harpal Singh, District President Ramakant Chaudhary, and SP District President Nepal Yadav have also reached the spot. Police officers have been trying to convince the family members for 7 hours. But without action, the family members are not ready to move. The young man had been fighting for life and death in the hospital for 13 days. Another young man has already died in the accident. People allege that the minister's son and 4 other people were in the car at the time of the accident. All were heavily intoxicated. The car's speed was over 100. The collision was so severe that the car dragged on for about 300 meters. Hit the bike, threatened people when they arrived The incident is from Barkhera village in the Jakhlaun police station area. On January 26, around 1 AM, Anuj Yadav (21) was returning home on a bike with his cousin Shivendra Yadav (18) and Shankar (45) from a Sundarkand Path program. During this time, State Minister Manohar Lal Mannu Kori's son Naresh Panth was traveling with his companions from Jakhlaun towards Lalitpur. The Fortuner's speed was over 100. The car hit the bike near the Howrah Bridge. The collision was so severe that the Fortuner's airbags deployed. All four doors got locked. After this, all the people in the car broke the back window and came out. When people protested, the minister's son threatened them by showing a gun. Taking advantage of the night, all the people fled. In this accident, all three youths on the bike were seriously injured. Meanwhile, the villagers informed the families of the injured and the police about the incident. Police admitted all three injured brothers to the hospital, where Shivendra Yadav died during treatment at night. While treatment continued for Anuj and Shankar. Later, due to their critical condition, both were referred to Jhansi Medical College. Second brother also dies after 13 days Anuj Yadav was treated at Jhansi Medical College for 13 days, but breathed his last on Sunday evening. Anuj was the younger of two brothers and worked at a petrol pump. The Fortuner car is registered in the name of the State Minister's wife, Kasturi Devi. Minister's son surrendered and got bail Family members had filed a complaint against the minister's son, Naresh Panth, on January 27. On February 3, the minister's son, Naresh Panth, surrendered in court, then got bail the same day. Accusing the police of negligence, Anuj's family members blocked the Lalitpur-Jakhlaun road by placing a pole on Monday morning. After that, they started protesting by placing the body. When there was no hearing even after 3-4 hours of sit-in, the family members set up a tent right in the middle of the road. Anuj's mother is also sitting in the protest. She fainted during the sit-in. Protesting by setting up tent More than 200 people are sitting in the protest. Now, Bhim Army District In-charge Harpal Singh, District President Ramakant Chaudhary, and SP District President Nepal Yadav have also reached the spot. Police officers are continuously trying to convince the family members. Shivendra's father, Rajendra Singh Yadav, said that Minister Manohar Lal Pant's son Naresh Panth had hit three people, including my son, with his Fortuner on the 26th. In this incident, my son Shivendra Pratap Singh Yadav died during treatment. The second injured, Anuj, who was my nephew, was admitted first to a private hospital and then to Jhansi Medical College for 14 days. Later, with the minister's intervention, he was shifted to a government hospital, but he also died due to a lack of proper treatment. The third injured, Shankar Nanna, is still struggling between life and death, and his condition is extremely critical. Compensation, jobs should be given, and Minister's son should be arrested Rajendra Singh Yadav said - Financial assistance of 50-50 lakh rupees should be given to the families of Shivendra and Anuj, and at least 30 lakh rupees should be given for the treatment of injured Shankar Nanna. We demand from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath that one government job each should be given for the sustenance of the affected families. Jobs should be given to Anuj's elder brother, our elder son, and Shankar Nanna's elder son, so that they can support their families. We also demand that Minister Manohar Lal Pant's son, Manohar Naresh, should be arrested immediately, and the sections applied in the case should be changed to serious sections. In this regard, we appeal for justice from the Chief Minister, Police Administration, SP, DM, and all senior officials of Jhansi.

stories.title: Trader set his own shop on fire in Varanasi:Pours petrol on himself, buldozer action begins; people kept pleading
stories.summary: The administration's bulldozer has started demolishing houses for road widening in Dalmandi, Varanasi. Today, 21 of the dilapidated houses identified by the Municipal Corporation will be razed. This is the biggest operation in Dalmandi in a single day so far. Local shopkeepers are continuously protesting. They are requesting a 10-day grace period from administration officials. However, the officials are not listening to anyone. During the administration's operation, the owner of house number 40/71 threw petrol and set it on fire. He threatened to burn himself. Meanwhile, the angry shopkeepers said while crying - What is our fault? Will you kill us? If you want to widen the road, will you destroy people's lives? The government is destroying us. They have taken away our livelihood. The administration didn't give any notice. The administration has tightened its grip on this. Forces from all four police stations are deployed vigilantly. 500 police personnel, including female staff, are present. Everyone is present at the scene. This is also being monitored by drones. Earlier, 8 houses were demolished together on January 21. Barricading has been done on the road leading to Dalmandi ACP Dashashwamedh Dr. Atul Anjan said - Houses are continuously being demolished for widening work in Dalmandi. This is a major operation today. The police force is deployed vigilantly. Barricading has been done on the roads leading to Dalmandi. So that there is no movement of any kind, and work is not hindered. 23 houses declared dilapidated Municipal Corporation has issued notices to 23 houses on January 31, 2026. The houses that have been served notices by the Municipal Corporation are all over 100 years old and in dilapidated condition. However, people are living in these houses, risking their lives. In this situation, house numbers CK 40/68, CK 40/70, CK 40/69, CK 67/25-A, CK 43/113-A, CK 39/9, CK 39/3,4, CK 70/79, CK 40/71, CK 43/158, CK 43/152, CK 42/106, 107, 108, CK 42/100,101, CK 42/96-A, CK 69/1, CK 69/2, CK 69/31-A, CK 69/29, CK 42/4, CK 42/5,6, CK 42/88, CK 69/24-A and CK 69/24 have been asked to be vacated within three days.

stories.title: Kuldeep Sengar gets setback from Supreme Court:Bail hearing denied, CJI says, 'High Court might hear the case'
stories.summary: BJP's former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar has not received any relief from the Supreme Court. The apex court refused to hear the bail plea in the case on Monday, related to the custodial death of the victim's father. However, the Supreme Court has requested the Delhi High Court to complete the hearing on Sengar's appeal within three months. The bench led by Chief Justice Suryakant said - This case deserves consideration in the High Court and the pending appeal should be disposed of promptly. The court clearly stated, “We consider this an appropriate case where the High Court is requested to complete the hearing of the appeal as soon as possible, but without delay exceeding three months.” Upon hearing this, the Supreme Court said, "We will not pass any interim order at this stage." The jurisdiction to decide this appeal lies with the Delhi High Court, and the final decision will be made there. The judge said that they will request the High Court to complete the hearing within the stipulated time frame. It is noteworthy that Kuldeep Singh Sengar is a former MLA from Unnao, Uttar Pradesh. He has been convicted of a rape case. The death of the victim's father is also connected to this case, which had generated widespread discussion and outrage across the country. Former MLA Kuldeep Singh had approached the Delhi High Court seeking bail before moving the Supreme Court. On January 19, 2026, the High Court rejected his bail plea, stating that no leniency can be shown in a case involving the custodial death of a family’s sole breadwinner. When was the victim's father attacked? The Unnao rape victim's father was arrested and sent to jail in 2018 on charges of possessing weapons. His condition deteriorated in jail, and he later died. The victim's family had alleged that this was not a natural death, but a custodial death carried out under conspiracy. It was alleged that the victim's father was persecuted under Sengar's influence and pressure. October 30, 2017- A defamation case was filed against the victim and her family at Makhi police station on behalf of the MLA. 03 April 2018- The accused MLA's brother, Atul Singh Sengar, along with his associates, physically assaulted and made a life-threatening attack on the victim's father. 04 April 2018- In the assault case, a report was filed against the victim's father under serious sections, and he was sent to jail. 09 April 2018- The victim's father's condition in jail deteriorated day by day, and finally, he breathed his last in jail.

stories.title: 58-year-old principal accused of bad touch in Varanasi:Around 200 people surround school with shoes and slippers; police escort him out wearing helmet, probe on
stories.summary: A 58-year-old principal of a primary school in Varanasi has been accused of inappropriate physical conduct with four girl students. The incident triggered massive outrage, with nearly 200 villagers surrounding the school campus in protest. According to the families, the accused principal allegedly threatened the girls with death when they resisted. As news of the alleged misconduct reached parents, they rushed to the school carrying shoes and slippers in anger, demanding action against the accused. The incident took place in the Shivpur police station area. Principal locked himself inside room As tensions escalated, villagers began searching for the accused inside the school premises. Fearing for his safety, the principal reportedly locked himself inside a room. Police officials, including the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) along with forces from three police stations, reached the spot to control the situation. Amid heavy protest and sloganeering, police escorted the accused out of the school premises, making him wear a helmet to prevent possible assault by the angry crowd. He was taken into custody. Allegations of luring students with sweets One of the victim’s fathers alleged that the principal, identified as Padbhakar Singh, would call girls to his chamber by offering toffees, snacks, and chocolates. “He would touch them inappropriately. He even followed them into the bathroom. This had been happening for the past 10 to 15 days,” the father said. He further alleged that two days ago, the principal forcibly assaulted one of the girls, causing her pain. The child informed her family, after which other girls also began sharing similar experiences. “After that, things went beyond tolerance, and we reached the school,” he added. Parents claimed that their daughters, studying in Classes 4 and 5, had been facing inappropriate behavior from the teacher for several days. “When teachers behave like this with students, where should we send our children to study?” one villager said. See 4 images... Police detain accused, inquiry ordered The accused principal has been taken into custody. The matter is being investigated by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Sadar and the Basic Education Officer (BEO). Police spent nearly two hours pacifying the agitated villagers. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Varuna Zone), Pramod Kumar, said: “A large number of villagers were protesting at the primary school in Shivpur. The principal was accused of misconduct with girl students. We are taking a written complaint from the villagers, and further legal action will follow.” Principal was relieved 15 days ago Officials revealed that the accused principal had been formally relieved from the school 15 days ago, but was unwilling to leave the post. According to the Basic Education Officer, the school has 12 female and three male teachers. A female and a male teacher had recently been transferred to another school. The accused, who is 58 years old, is reportedly due to retire in two years.

stories.title: Basti SSI’s body recovered in Ayodhya Saryu River:CCTV shows him riding with worker; brother says police failed, demands suspension of entire station
stories.summary: The body of senior sub-inspector (SSI) Ajay Gaur was recovered from the Saryu River in Ayodhya. He had gone missing four days earlier while on duty. The last CCTV footage shows him riding a bike with a sanitation worker. Three days ago, police found his bike near the Kuano River, and the last mobile location was also recorded there. After the bike was found, his wife reported a suspicion of murder and filed a missing person complaint. According to her, Ajay Gaur had left home in the morning for duty but did not return. On Sunday evening, a body was spotted near Tighura Majha village along the Sarayu River in Ayodhya. Ayodhya police recovered the body, identified it, and informed Basti police. The deceased officer, Ajay Gaur, was posted at Parshurampur police station in Basti. His younger brother and ADM Arun Kumar questioned police action, stating that the police did not do their job properly, and demanded the suspension of the entire station, including action against the CO. Ajay Gaur lived in Basti with his wife and two children. He was originally from Mudadiha village in Deoria Kotwali area. Wife had said... She last spoke to her husband around 3 PM on February 5. After this, she tried to contact again between 8 to 9 PM, but the phone was switched off. When the phone was still switched off on the morning of February 6, she contacted other staff at the police station, after which details of the case came to light. Meanwhile, Ajay's younger brother ADM Arun Kumar said... The police did not do their job properly and we found this body. No senior officer has come to Ayodhya Ghat in Ayodhya to talk to our family yet. We don't consider this a suicide. This is a planned murder. Our request is that there should be an impartial investigation. Now know the complete matter... Ajay Gaur, a 2016 batch officer, hailed from Mudadiha village, Deoria. He lived in rented accommodation in Mishraulia Mohalla, Basti, with his wife Ranjita and two children. Their elder son studies in Kanpur. According to Ranjita, Ajay left home for duty on 5 February after breakfast. After the Parshurampur station in-charge Vishw Mohan Rai went on leave, SSI Ajay Gaur took charge of the station. He spoke to his wife once in the afternoon. Around 3:30 pm, Ranjita had her last conversation with him. According to station staff, Ajay left the station around 5 pm on a bike with a sanitation worker. A video captures him leaving the station. Between 8–9 pm, calls from Ranjita to his number went unanswered. Bike found 50 km away from police station near Kuano river According to Ranjita’s complaint, she contacted the station the next morning and was informed that Ajay had been missing since the previous evening. Despite inquiries, there was no trace. On 6 February, his bike was found 50 km away at Amhat Ghat along the Kuano River, along with the last mobile location. Ranjita filed a missing person report. She said that during a prior posting at Dubaulia police station, Ajay had received threats over the death of a minor. She demanded that this angle be investigated. Wife believes bike was planted to mislead police My name is Ranjita. I am the wife of SI Ajay Kumar Gaur, who was posted at Parshurampur police station and went missing between 4 to 5 PM on February 5th. I believe that his bike which was found at Amhat Ghat was placed there to mislead the police. I suspect that my husband was held captive and he was in or around the police station area, because he hadn't gone anywhere else.In this area, a trusted person betrayed them. The saddest thing is that I was not informed about their disappearance by the police station. The next morning around 9 to 10 when I called them as usual, I found out that they had been missing since the previous evening. When I asked the police station staff why their location or call details were not traced, I did not get any satisfactory answer. Three-day search along Kuano River yields no clues Police, along with the SDRF team from Gorakhpur, conducted a continuous three-day search along the Kuano River, from Amhat Ghat to Bhadreshwarnath, covering 2 km with motorboats. The search ended around 4 pm on Sunday with no results. News came from Ayodhya after three hours About three hours after the search ended, around 7 pm, information came that a body was spotted in the Sarayu River near Tighura Majha village, under Darshan Nagar police. Ayodhya police recovered the body, which was identified as Ajay Gaur. Younger brother ADM Arun Kumar said... I want to make it clear to you that I am not a police officer. I have no complaint against any magistrate because I myself am a magistrate and go to the scene even at 12 midnight. I have served as SDM and am currently ADM, but despite this I did not receive any cooperation. My demand is that the entire police station should be suspended, murder charges (Section 302) should be filed against four people, and action should be taken against the CO of Harraiya. The way the CO spoke to me and tried to frame my brother, I will not tolerate it. If needed, I will go up to the Chief Minister, please note this. It is being said that they are sleeping with their phones switched off, but I don't want to talk to the Captain. I will only speak when the DIG sir comes and will present my demands. Until the demands are met, I will not leave from here and the body will remain here. My brother has died, not yoursI am in pain, a lot of pain, and this can be understood by looking at our faces. Inspector's father said - Murder happened after kidnapping Ajay Gaur’s father, retired senior inspector Ramchandra Prasad, said the incident occurred on 5 February around 6 pm. His wife Ranjita informed them at 10 am on 6 February. It is unclear what police action has been taken. “We suspect he was kidnapped on the way from Parshurampur station to home and murdered. The police department, CO, and SP were all in contact. On 8 February evening, his body was found near Sarayu River in Ayodhya.” Many questions still unresolved The discovery of the inspector's body has caused grief and sensation throughout the police department. The biggest question is why he went alone on a bike despite being the station in-charge, where is his service revolver and mobile phone, and how did the body reach the Saryu river instead of Kuano. SP says - Postmortem report will reveal the mystery Basti SP Yashveer Singh said that the inspector's body has been recovered. The cause of death will be confirmed based on the postmortem report. A thorough investigation of the case is being conducted, and further action will be taken based on whatever facts come to light.

stories.title: Gangster abducts woman constable before wedding:Cops rescue her after 8 hrs, father’s health deteriorates when wedding ceremony fails to start
stories.summary: In Meerut, just hours before her wedding, a a woman constable was reportedly kidnapped by a history-sheeter. The wedding was scheduled for Sunday evening, but she went missing earlier that morning. Her father filed an FIR against the accused. Police, however, claimed that the woman went voluntarily. Four police teams were deployed for the rescue operation. Officers retrieved call records from both the constable and the accused, Ankit Thakur, which contained evidence of communication between them. The woman constable was recovered within eight hours. On Sunday evening, police brought her to Mavana police station, where SP Dehat questioned her. It remains unclear where exactly the woman constable was found. The whereabouts of the history-sheeter remain unknown. SP Dehat Abhijeet Kumar stated that the woman would undergo a medical examination on Monday, followed by recording her statement in court. Further action will follow. The groom’s family refused to bring the wedding procession today. The incident occurred in the Bahsuma police jurisdiction, in the village of Akbarpur Sadan. At Mavana police station, SP Dehat conducted questioning of the woman constable. She was to remain in police custody overnight and will be produced in court the following day. Full details of the case… The woman constable, a resident of Akbarpur Sadan, was expecting her wedding on Sunday night. Earlier that morning, she was reportedly abducted by a criminal, prompting panic among her family. Her father approached the police to file a complaint. He said: “My daughter is posted at the Cyber Crime police station in Aligarh. Her wedding was scheduled for 8 February. The procession was supposed to arrive from Khedki village in Mirapur. Earlier, a man named Ankit from Dhikoli kidnapped my daughter. He has a criminal record, and my daughter’s life is in danger.” Calls father to say she went voluntarily According to police, shortly after the family arrived at the station, the woman constable made a call from a home phone. She said she had gone voluntarily and there was no need for concern. She also stated that she is an adult and understands right from wrong. However, her family has not confirmed this claim. CO Pankaj Lavania said the FIR was filed based on the father’s complaint. Accused is a known history-sheeter recently released from jail The accused, Ankit Thakur, is a known history-sheeter from Mavana. He had recently been released from jail. In May 2025, he and some accomplices carried out a robbery at a liquor shop. The police had laid a siege and Ankit was arrested after a shootout, during which he sustained a gunshot wound to one leg. Father’s health deteriorates The abduction hours before the wedding left the family in shock. Reports suggest the woman constable’s father’s health worsened, and he was taken to hospital with chest pain. The person who arranged the marriage also arrived at the family’s house, and communication with the groom’s side has been ongoing by phone.

stories.title: 'Go back’ slogans raised against Governor in UP Assembly:Governor asks MLAs to calm down, says throat will get sore
stories.summary: The budget session of the Uttar Pradesh Legislature has begun. At 11 am, Governor Anandiben Patel started her address. Soon after, Samajwadi Party MLAs raised slogans and rushed into the well of the House. They shouted slogans over inflation, unemployment, SIR, UGC and other issues. As the noise increased, the Governor stopped her speech and asked the SP MLAs to calm down. She said otherwise their throat would give way. Pallavi Patel was not part of the protest. She remained seated at her place. Eighty four year old Anandiben Patel completed her address in 30 minutes. She spoke in praise of the government’s policies. Earlier, SP MLAs held a strong protest in the Assembly campus. SP MLC Ashutosh Sinha reached the Assembly on a bicycle. The bicycle had a picture of Ahilyabai on it. He said that under the BJP government, temples in Varanasi were being demolished continuously. Key points related to the Budget session The session is proposed for a total of 10 days. The sittings will continue till 20 February. The Budget will be presented in the Assembly on 11 February. There is a possibility that the Budget will focus on fulfilling pending promises, along with new announcements for women, farmers, youth and rural areas. After the Budget is presented, discussion on the motion of thanks on the Governor’s address will begin. This discussion will take place on 12 and 13 February. A detailed discussion on the Budget will be held from 16 to 18 February. From 19 February, department-wise budgets will be passed, and voting on the entire Budget will take place on 20 February.

stories.title: MLA blocks drain, water floods 20,000 homes in Lucknow:Locals claim severe waterlogging, visible structural damage to tiles and homes
stories.summary: In Lucknow’s Khargapur area, blocking of a drain is causing water to accumulate in empty plots. Nearby houses are developing dampness, and tiles are coming loose. To protect their homes, residents are dumping concrete debris against the outer walls to strengthen the foundations. Homeowners opposing this are being threatened with demolition. Repeated complaints were made to Mayor Sushma Kharkwal, MLA Yogesh Shukla, Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar, and councillor Mamta Rawat, but no solution has been found. To understand the residents’ problems, Dainik Bhaskar visited the ground zero. Locals accused Subhaspa MLA Bedi Ram of blocking the drain, while MLA Bedi Ram has outright denied the allegations. Encroachment on drain land In Khargapur, near Bharwara Malhaur Ward, on the road from Amity University towards the STP, the MLA has extended about 6 feet to build a boundary wall on the drain land. This has narrowed the drain, preventing wastewater from flowing out. As a result, dirty water is filling nearby empty plots and colonies. During the monsoon, the situation becomes severe. This is the drain that is supposed to be constructed. MLA Bedi Ram is accused of encroaching on it. Here’s what the locals said… Reena said – 20,000 homes affected Reena said that water from this drain goes to 20,000 homes, but the MLA has blocked the drain by occupying its land. Because of this, water is entering their houses. Even when municipal trucks came to take action, the MLA did not allow any work. Ranju said – Water and drainage problems Ranju said that the water and drainage issues are severe. Bathroom and house tiles are coming loose. During rains, water enters homes. Drain water is flowing into houses, and people are falling ill. Vibha Singh said – Drain blocked, no relief Vibha Singh said that there is no outlet for water. Residents are struggling with illnesses. The drain has been blocked ahead. From the Mayor to the MLA, assurances were given, but no one is listening. Men and women in Khargapur are distressed due to the situation. Demolition threats for homes Ram Vijay said that the drain has been closed for the past year. Water is entering plots and houses in the colony. Residents have been unable to sleep for over a year. Some try to open it, some close it. Fights are breaking out among locals. They meet the Mayor and municipal officials every week. They are being threatened that the entire colony is illegal and homes will be demolished. Until one and a half years ago, the drain went straight from the STP to the river. Water from over 2,000 homes used to flow through it. Now, sewage water is entering homes. Mayor and then Municipal Commissioner Indrajeet Singh also visited the site, but nothing changed. MLA says – Thousands facing difficulties Local BKT MLA Yogesh Shukla inspected the site on Saturday, accompanied by municipal officers. The MLA said the drain will eventually be dug. Locals are facing problems. He added that water used to flow freely before, and no one could stop it. As elected representatives, responsibilities increase, but now the entire population is suffering from waterlogging. At the site, councillor Mamta Rawat and her supporters accused revenue officer Kaushal of malpractice. Mayor says – Encroachment will be acted upon Mayor Sushma Kharkwal said that anyone occupying government land, regardless of position, will face action. About a year ago, she visited the site after complaints, when residents reported that 30,000–40,000 people were affected due to one person. She asked the MLA to show legal papers for the encroached land, but nothing has been done so far. About a year ago, Mayor Kharkwal had visited the site to inspect the encroachment after residents’ complaints. MLA says – Drain land will be measured MLA Bedi Ram rejected the allegations entirely, saying that the drain land will be properly measured and only lawful actions will follow. He explained that he owns a marriage lawn, and revenue officers repeatedly visit taking money. He also raised the issue in the assembly and demanded answers. He added that he will talk to the Mayor and Municipal Commissioner, as municipal officers and revenue officials are not working according to government directives. “We have not used any abusive language,” he said.

stories.title: Lucknow goldsmith absconds with nearly 1-kg gold:Gold from Bahraich jeweller was sent from Aminabad to Chowk; police register FIR
stories.summary: In Lucknow’s Chowk area, a craftsman absconded with 967 grams of gold entrusted to him by a jeweller from Bahraich. The accused’s mobile has been switched off since the incident. The victim filed a case at Chowk police station. Manthan Patil (32), a gold and silver trader from Kajipura North in Bahraich, said that on February 6 he sent jewellery craftsman Afzal Ahmed to Lucknow along with his employee Shivaji Bhosle. Afzal was instructed to collect gold from a jeweller in Aminabad and deliver it directly to Shani Verma, operator of New Balaji Ornament, in Chowk Sarafa Market. Alone in Aminabad According to Manthan Patil, Afzal Ahmed deliberately left Shivaji Bhosle waiting in the Chowk Sarafa Market and went alone to Aminabad. There, he collected 967 grams of fine gold and sent only a photo of the gold to the trader on WhatsApp to create an illusion. After this, Afzal reached Chowk but intentionally avoided going to the shop, heading instead towards the parking area. He then switched off his mobile and fled with the gold. After waiting for a long time without any trace, the suspicion of theft intensified. Chowk police have registered a case based on the complaint. The authorities stated that CCTV footage is being examined and a search for the accused is ongoing.

stories.title: Lucknow man duped of ₹7.12 lakh in trading scam:Cyber scammers displayed fake ₹1 crore IPO profit and wanted ₹20 lakh deposit to withdraw funds
stories.summary: Cyber fraudsters in Lucknow tricked a young man into investing in share trading and IPOs by promising huge profits, swindling him of several lakh rupees. Following the victim’s complaint, a case has been registered at Gudamba police station, and an investigation is underway. According to Mayank Srivastava, a resident of Shyam Enclave, Janakipuram, he received a call on 8–9 December inviting him to join a WhatsApp group related to trading. After joining the group, the fraudsters helped him open a trading account and initially made him deposit ₹5,000. The next day, a profit was shown in the account, which gained their trust. Victim asked to deposit ₹20 lakh to withdraw funds Subsequently, the victim was persuaded to deposit a total of ₹7,12,500 in installments across different bank accounts. The scammers promised investment in an IPO and displayed a fake profit of ₹1 crore in his account. When he asked to withdraw the money, they demanded an additional ₹20 lakh deposit. Suspecting fraud, the victim contacted SEBI, which confirmed that he had been cheated. He then filed a complaint on the 1930 Cyber Helpline, resulting in ₹3,47,000 being frozen across the bank accounts used by the fraudsters. The victim stated that the WhatsApp group was called “Steady Hain Group,” administered by a person named Kavya Godbole. Account manager Raghavan Narayanan handled communications. Full details of the bank accounts used in the scam have been handed over to the police. Gudamba police confirmed that a case has been registered based on the complaint, and the cyber cell is identifying the accounts and suspects. Action against the accused will follow soon.

The incident occurred around 9 pm after the train departed Govindpuri station and approached Bhimsen. Following the incident, the coach attendant removed the broken glass. Bhimsen GRP station in-charge confirmed that an FIR has been registered against unknown individuals, and investigations are ongoing to trace the suspects.
