stories.title: Bomb threats to 5 courts including Lucknow and Varanasi:Campuses evacuated; judges step out as ATS and STF launch investigation
stories.summary: Courts in Lucknow, Varanasi, Ayodhya, Meerut and Mirzapur received bomb threats on official government email IDs, triggering panic and immediate security action on Friday. Following the threat emails, police evacuated all five court campuses. Court proceedings were suspended as a precautionary measure. Campuses cleared, thousands evacuated In Varanasi alone, more than 3,000 lawyers and around 5,000 litigants hurriedly vacated the premises. The District Judge and other judicial officers also stepped out of the campus. Police teams, along with dog squads and bomb disposal squads, conducted thorough searches of every corner of the court complexes. However, nothing suspicious had been found at the time of reporting. Similar email pattern, probe underway According to police officials, the threat emails received at different locations follow a similar pattern. Authorities are yet to determine who sent the emails and from where. Investigators are examining why the emails were sent simultaneously and whether there is a larger conspiracy behind the threats. Senior officials in Lucknow are closely monitoring the situation. The cyber cell and other security agencies have joined the investigation. Past attack raises alarm The threat has been taken extremely seriously, especially in light of the November 23, 2007, bomb blast at the Varanasi court, in which nine people — including three lawyers — were killed and around 50 others were injured. Given the history, Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Special Task Force (STF) teams have also been deployed to assist in the investigation. Authorities continue to maintain heightened security across all five court complexes.

stories.title: Durgam cheruvu: A glittering view, a gasping lake
stories.summary: The gem-like appearance of Durgam Cheruvu hides a sinister, calculated assault. As evening lights and rooftop views sell the lake as a tourist spot, a multi-agency process seems to be killing it softly. One civic body lowers the water level to free up land, another lays a 10-metre-wide walking track on the exposed lake bed and yet another releases organically loaded effluents that fuel decay. Once a source of drinking water and part of Golconda Fort’s hydrological system, the lake is now trapped in a bureaucratic tic-tac-toe, writes Serish Nanisetti

stories.title: Former Congressman Naseemuddin to join SP:Left Congress 20 days ago; vowed to defeat communal forces
stories.summary: UP Congress heavyweight Muslim leader Nasimuddin Siddiqui, who resigned on January 24, will now join SP. On Friday after prayers, he will meet with his supporters and then announce joining SP. For 20 days, there were various discussions about his political move. Finally, after touring different districts and having long discussions with his supporters, he has made this decision. In an interview given to Dainik Bhaskar, he had also indicated that he would either join a party with a similar ideology to defeat communal forces or form a new party. Siddiqui, who started his politics from BSP, wielded considerable power as a cabinet minister in Mayawati's government. He is considered to have a strong political influence in western UP. Nasimuddin sent his resignation to Congress National President Mallikarjun Kharge and other senior leaders on January 24. At that time, 73 other leaders also left the Congress party with him. This included several former MLAs. Nasimuddin's resignation was seen as a major loss for Congress in UP. However, even after leaving the party, he maintained a soft stance towards Congress. Nasimuddin said - I came to Congress to fight casteism Nasimuddin Siddiqui was also the Provincial President of Western Uttar Pradesh Congress. He is considered to have a strong hold on the Muslim vote bank in districts around Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar. In his resignation, Siddiqui wrote - 'I came to Congress to fight against casteism. Could not work on the ground for 8 years. I was getting rusty.' I respect Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Sonia Gandhi, and will continue to do so. But there was no work for me in the party. I joined Congress so that I could fight against communalism. But now that was not possible.' Did not get attention in Lok Sabha elections There was dissatisfaction regarding Nasimuddin's role and influence in Congress. He did not receive attention in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections either. With the 2027 assembly elections approaching, Nasimuddin was worried about his future in Congress. The stature of Congress MP Imran Masood from Saharanpur has risen rapidly. He is counted among Priyanka's special lieutenants. Siddiqui was quite troubled by this, too. Recently, while receiving Rahul Gandhi at Amausi airport, he was not given entry ahead of other leaders, including Pramod Tiwari and Aradhana Mishra. Mayawati had expelled from BSP Nasimuddin's resignation is being considered a big loss for Congress before the 2027 assembly elections. Siddiqui was earlier in BSP, from where Mayawati expelled him in 2017. After that, he joined Congress in 2018, and the party promoted him as a Muslim face. According to sources, after the resignation, Congress state president Ajay Rai is trying to persuade him, but for now Siddiqui has clearly refused to change his decision. Now all eyes were fixed on Siddiqui's next move. There were speculations about whether he would join a new party or do independent politics? There was also a discussion that he might join Chandrashekhar's Azad Samaj Party, but Siddiqui has decided to join SP, putting an end to all speculations. Dainik Bhaskar In conversation with, Nasimuddin Siddiqui had said - 73 leaders from Delhi, Uttarakhand, Ghaziabad, including western UP have left the party with me. This includes former MLAs and other senior people. We will take a decision after discussing with everyone. Career started as a railway contractor Nasimuddin Siddiqui's name has long been prominent in Uttar Pradesh politics. His journey, which began as a railway contractor, reached its peak when he became one of Mayawati's closest associates in BSP. After being expelled from BSP, he formed a new party. Shortly after, he joined Congress along with his wife and son. Now, one year before the assembly elections, he has bid farewell to Congress as well. Nasimuddin Siddiqui was born on June 4, 1959. There was no political background in the family. After leaving his army job due to his mother's illness, he became active in railway contracting. Around 1990, Nasimuddin came in contact with BSP founder Kanshi Ram. The beginning was with the Palika (municipality) election. In 1991, he contested from the BSP from the Banda Sadar assembly seat and won. After this, he remained active in the West.

stories.title: 12th-grade student arrested in hit and run case:Accused was returning from a party with girlfriend; 6-yr-old dies, 5 seriously hurt
stories.summary: A Class 12 student has been arrested in Lucknow for mowing down 6 people while ramming vehicles with a Swift Dzire car. CCTV footage of the hit-and-run has surfaced. A six-year-old boy died on the spot, while five others remain in critical condition. The deceased child has been identified as Dikshant, son of Sadhana from Unnao. He had come to the market with his grandmother for the first time. When his mother reached the hospital, and the shroud was removed from his body, she screamed in grief. The accused fled the scene after the accident but was arrested within an hour. During questioning, he said he was returning from a farewell party. A female classmate was also in the car but got out immediately after the accident. Locals caught her and handed her over to the police. Accident near Hanuman temple The incident took place around 7 pm on Thursday near Hanuman Temple on Kanpur Road in the Banthra police station area. As the car stopped, the girl got down while the student sped away. According to ACP Krishna Nagar Rajneesh Verma, police traced the car and arrested the accused, Gaurav Singh, and seized the vehicle. He is a Class 12 student at Avadh Collegiate. He and his classmate were returning from a farewell party on Mohan Road when the accident occurred. Sequence of the incident Pramod Kumar of Sahijanpur had parked his bike by the roadside and was buying items from a shop when a speeding car travelling from Lucknow to Kanpur hit his bike. When people ran to catch the driver, he accelerated and hit 12-year-old Armaan, son of Pape alias Pauwa of Banthra, who had come to the market. About 100 metres ahead, the car struck Sadhana Patel (35), her mother Meena Devi (60), and her son Dikshant (6) from Atwa Khurd in Unnao. The driver also ran over e-rickshaw driver Avadh Bihari (42) from Pathraha village in Sohramau, Unnao, and then crashed into a stationary auto. He fled with the car before people could catch him. Injured and eyewitness accounts Pramod Kumar suffered serious head and facial injuries and is undergoing treatment at Sarojini Nagar CHC. Avadh Bihari said he was waiting for passengers near Banthra crossing when a vehicle rammed into his auto from behind, throwing him out. His wife, Shiv Devi, said she was informed by police that her husband had met with an accident. He has a head injury and is not fully conscious. Accused borrowed car; father is businessman According to information, the accused student’s father runs a cement and iron business. The student had borrowed someone else’s car to attend the party. The child’s mother, Sadhana, has filed a written complaint with the police based on the car number. Police continue to investigate the incident.

stories.title: Man kills family, calls priest:Dies by electrocution, ashes found inside Mathura home; black magic suspected
stories.summary: The mystery surrounding the deaths of 5 members of a family in Mathura has led police to a temple located about 2 km from their home. Before the incident, Manish reportedly made a call to the son of temple priest Karua Baba. Police have detained the priest and are trying to determine what was discussed in that final conversation. Matter being investigated from all angles Investigators are also examining Manish’s relationship with his wife, Seema, and questioning relatives about possible disputes or any suspected affair. Locals said Manish had given up alcohol in recent years, turned to worship, and began offering spiritual advice and sacred ash to people. After the bodies were discovered, police suspected that Manish killed his wife and three children before dying by electrocution. Forensic findings indicate no one else entered the house. Despite the incident occurring on the night of 10 February, an FIR has not yet been registered. Police interrogated Manish Baba in closed room Manish immersed himself in worship, gave people packets of sacred ash Police held a closed-door questioning session with Manish, the son of temple priest Karua Baba. They asked whether Manish used to spend time at the temple. The priest replied that he would visit every Tuesday and Saturday, help with cleaning, and gradually people began approaching him with their problems. He would perform prayers for them and distribute packets of sacred ash. When police asked if this was linked to black magic, the priest said he could not say that. He maintained that people came voluntarily for worship, shared their concerns, and Manish performed rituals on their request, adding that there was nothing wrong with that. Learn about the evidence found at Manish's house in Khapparpur village that supports this theory... Herbal prescription on fridge, worship materials found Police spoke to people from more than 20 villages. They acknowledged that Manish used to drink alcohol before, but in the past few years, he had given up everything. He spent most of his time in the temple. He started visiting nearby villages for worship. Childless couples also started coming to meet Manish. Large quantities of worship materials (nutmeg, coconut, and havan materials) were found in his room. Ayurvedic herbs were found on top of the fridge. A prescription was found that had names of herbs like Kankar, Manesil, Saffron, Tagar, and Kut written on it. Peacock feathers were found in various places. During the investigation, police found 2 red pouches kept in the temple inside Manish's house. Police considered this as part of the investigation; these red pouches were exactly like those that hang with strings in the temple 2 km away from Manish's house. Most people tie these red pouches while making wishes. The villagers say that about 3 months ago, Manish got typhoid. At that time, he would not leave the house, but would regularly go to the temple, where he would chant the Gayatri mantra. Manish's name was found written in the list of vows at this temple. Manish had also asked for some vow from the temple goddess; whether it was fulfilled or not, this could not be determined. Cause of death not mentioned, only financial accounts written in note Suicide notes were found in 4 places in Manish's house. First- House wall. Second- Manish's diary. Third- Two slips. Fourth- VIDEO in mobile. The notes found did not mention the reason for killing the wife and children before embracing death. Only details about selling land and money transactions were written. Manish's uncle Bhagwan Singh said - Manish has changed a lot. Now he rarely meets with family members. He spent most of his time in the temple. He had started doing worship and prayers. Brother Sudhir said - 5 years ago in the division, Manish got 6 bigha land. He sold 4.5 bigha of land in 2 installments. There was a tubewell in the field, which they used to sell water for irrigation. Then the tubewell was also shut down. Now he wasn't even going to the field anymore. Killed wife and children, then made a VIDEO Police found a VIDEO in Manish's mobile on February 10. In this, he was saying - we are dying by our own will, no one is at fault for this. Initially, police believed that Manish made this VIDEO before the murder-suicide. However, the doctor who conducted the postmortem gave a new theory. According to them, his wife and three children were killed between 3 and 4 o'clock. His wife, Seema, was struck on the head with a pestle. She had an open wound on her head. While the three children were killed by strangulation. Manish was alive until this time; his video was recorded at 4:25 in the morning. The video was recorded in the bathroom, and then suicide notes were written on the wall. Police theory is that if Manish himself murdered his family, he made this video after doing everything. Manish found next to fridge, others on bed The body of 5-year-old daughter Honey was lying on a cot in the room. The bodies of wife, son, and daughter were on a nearby bed. Manish's body was next to the fridge. There were exposed wires near Manish's body. Manish, who lived in Khapparpur village of Mahavan area, was married 8 years ago to Seema from Madhnai village in Hathras district. They had 3 children - 5-year-old Honey, 4-year-old Priyanshi, and two-and-a-half-year-old Pankaj. They had returned from their in-laws' house at 8 PM on Monday night. When there was no movement in the house on Tuesday morning, elder brother Sudhir looked through the window by removing the cardboard covering. That's when he saw the family members unconscious. Police broke open the door to enter and found a blood-stained iron rod near the bed in the room. Seema had serious injuries on her head. A piece of nylon rope was also found lying there. The forensic team has submitted its report to SSP Shlok Kumar after examining the crime scene. SP said - FIR not filed, but investigation is ongoing SP Rural Suresh Chandra Rawat said we have received the suicide note and video. After the post-mortem report, it has become clear how everyone died. We have some facts based on which we are investigating. The priest is also being questioned. Since the person who committed the killings is also dead, no FIR has been filed in this case yet. Our investigation is ongoing. We will take action according to any new facts that emerge.

stories.title: Man who eloped with mother-in-law, claims her affair with brother-in-law:Woman walks away with ₹2 lakh after dispute with daughter's husband
stories.summary: The man who eloped with his mother-in-law now says he regrets his decision in Aligarh. He claims that falling in love with her was the biggest mistake of his life. Within nine months, she allegedly developed an affair with his brother-in-law. She began speaking to him secretly and eventually ran away. He says, “If only I had married the daughter, I would have lived a happy life. Now only the police can deliver justice for me.” Rahul, who ran away with his 38-year-old mother-in-law Anita Devi on April 6, 2025, the day they both ran away was the same day Rahul was supposed to bring his wedding procession to marry Anita Devi's daughter. After both suddenly disappeared, this case made headlines. After almost 9 months, both appeared again. But this time affair wasn't the reason. Rather, they reached Aligarh due to separation. Meanwhile, Anita Devi, who reached Aligarh police station, said- False allegations have been made against me. Rahul himself trades girls. I have no connection with my brother-in-law. Now I will live my life on my own terms. This case is from Machharia Nagla of Dado police station area in Aligarh. Daughter was to be married on April 18, but they eloped 12 days before Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Rahul to understand the entire matter. He says - Anita's daughter was to be married on April 18, 2025. Before this, on April 6, Anita and I left Aligarh. We first went to Uttarakhand for some work, then came to the Bela area of Sitamarhi district in Bihar. Here, we rented a room. Got married in the temple. Rahul says - Sapna's family members started putting pressure on the police, then both of us went to the Aligarh police station ourselves. People from both sides sat in one room, and after long discussions, it was agreed that the family would not trouble us anymore. We will live together. Sold clothes in Sitamarhi, fights started after 3 months We asked - When you people left home, there was talk that Anita was pregnant. To this, Rahul says - After our marriage, Anita was never pregnant; this is all just a rumor. We asked - What did you do to run the household? Rahul says - We fell in love, got married too. We didn't know anyone there, so I started selling clothes door to door. Some money started coming in at home, and everything was going well. We asked - So, when did the relationship turn sour? Rahul says - After 2-3 months, Anita started talking secretly with her brother-in-law. Gradually, her behavior also started changing. She started fighting with me over small things. I was troubled because I couldn't understand the reason. Money sent to sister's account, then she 'disappeared' We asked - Then what happened before dropping Anita home? Rahul says - About 5 days ago, Sapna asked to send 1500 rupees to her sister. I said I don't have money. After this, there was a fight. After this, I first transferred 500 rupees, then 1 thousand rupees to her sister's account. Then everything was fine, but 5 days later, Anita suddenly went 'missing' from home. We asked - Anita says you were harassing her? Rahul says - This is completely false. She was troubling me. You should understand that before leaving home, she took 2 lakh rupees and jewelry with her. Son-in-law said - Mother-in-law deceived, read the exact complaint Son-in-law Rahul filed a complaint at the Dado police station on Wednesday. In this, Rahul said - I work selling clothes by roaming on streets in Bihar. 15 days ago, my wife Anita contacted her brother-in-law. I have heard the audio recording of their phone conversation. In the audio, both were talking about living together. Both had planned to poison me and run away together. On February 6, my wife Anita (previously mother-in-law) deceived me and left with her brother-in-law. She also took 2 lakh rupees in cash and jewelry with her. Therefore, my wife should be caught. Woman said - My decision turned out to be wrong After the matter came to light in the media, Anita reached the police station on Thursday. She told the police - I left my children and went with my son-in-law. I deeply regret this now. My decision turned out to be wrong. Rahul (son-in-law) threatens and harasses me. He is involved in trafficking women. Now, I want to work hard and live separately from Rahul. I want to live with my children, but Rahul has forbidden me from going to my children. Rahul beat me up, took away my jewelry and money. That's why I left him. The story of eloping with son-in-law from one year ago 1- Ran away with son-in-law 10 days before daughter's wedding Anita's first husband is Jitendra Kumar, and their daughter Shivani lives in the village Manoharpur Kayasth in the Madrak police station area. Jitendra had fixed his daughter's marriage on April 16, 2025, with Rahul, a resident of Riya Nagla village in Dado police station area. Rahul was a supervisor in a private company in Rudrapur, Uttarakhand. 10 days before the wedding, on April 6, 2025, Shivani's mother, Anita, suddenly disappeared from home. On the other hand, the groom-to-be, Rahul, also left his house, saying he was going to buy clothes, but did not return. As soon as they left Aligarh, both turned off their mobile phones. 2- After FIR was filed, surrendered at police station with son-in-law Family members searched extensively, but neither could be found. Five days later, Rahul called his father and said not to try to find him; he would not return. After this, Rahul's family learned that his mother-in-law to be was also missing. The family filed a complaint with the police. After this, the police conducted raids and search operations in several states, including Bihar. On April 18, both reached the police station and surrendered. Police took both into custody and interrogated them. 3- Refused to go to police station with husband, then started living with son-in-law During interrogation, it was revealed that over 10 days, both traveled about 2,826 kilometers while on the run. They kept hiding in UP, Nepal, Delhi, and Bihar. Both also underwent counselling for 4 hours. Police advised the woman and asked her to go with her husband, but she clearly refused. Anita said that she had been suppressing her desires for 20 years. She was mistreated over small matters. She could not tolerate all this anymore, so she left home. She said that she does not want to go with her husband now. After this, the police let both of them go. The woman had been living with her son-in-law since then. First husband remarried, daughter's marriage not yet arranged Anita's first husband, Jeetu, had remarried a month ago. However, her daughter's marriage has not been arranged yet. The daughter says that they have completely forgotten Anita. They don't want to know anything about her anymore.

stories.title: 20K positions to be outsourced in UP:Budget increased by ₹426 cr, minimum salary to be ₹16K; know about other benefits also
stories.summary: Before the election, the Yogi government of UP had prepared to fill more than 20 thousand positions through outsourcing. Indications of this have come from the increased budget of this department. The government has released ₹2223.84 crore this time by increasing the budget by ₹426 crore. Applicants who will be recruited through outsourcing will get most of the facilities available to government employees, along with a reservation. A minimum honorarium of ₹16K will be given. Lakhs of outsourced employees are working in various departments in the state. Currently, their appointments are being made by different agencies on a contract basis. They were being heavily exploited. They were neither getting a salary on time nor were they given a fixed honorarium. Like other government employees, they were not eligible for any kind of facilities. Looking at these problems of outsourced workers, the government recently formed UP Outsource Service Corporation (UPCOS). Now in the state, all vacant outsourced positions will be filled transparently through the Outsource Corporation. These employees will get several new facilities. Additionally, reservation provisions have been made for Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), Other Backward Classes (OBC), and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). Large increase in outsourcing corporation's budget Budget figures clearly show that there is a continuous increase in expenses on outsourced recruitment and related arrangements. Considering this, the government has increased this corporation's budget by more than ₹426 crore this time. According to corporate sources, this budget can accommodate at least 20,000 positions through outsourcing. The more than 3-fold increase in the outsourcing corporation's budget over 8 years also indicates this trend. These figures show that the government is focusing on increasing the number of outsourced employees and their facilities. The budget has increased more than 3 times from 2019-20 to 2026-27. This increase is not only for new recruitments but also covers improvements in service conditions of existing employees, salary increases, and expenses related to corporation formation. The upcoming budget is expected to have more provisions for this corporation. Particularly, there is discussion about more than 20-50 thousand new recruitments. Corporation formation and management responsibility determined After cabinet approval, the corporation has been registered under the Companies Act. It will function as a non-profit organisation. Senior IAS officer Amrita Soni of the 2003 batch has been appointed as its Managing Director (MD). Amrita Soni is working as the Principal Staff Officer to the Chief Secretary. Now, she is handling the command of the corporation in-additional charge. The corporation office is being prepared in the Pickup Building. Details of vacant outsourcing positions have been sought from all departments by the corporation. The corporation is preparing to start the recruitment process for these vacant positions soon. Clear provision for reservation in outsourced recruitments The opposition often attacked the ruling party regarding outsourced recruitments. The opposition alleged that reservation provisions were not being followed in outsourced recruitments. SP often attacks the government, calling it a robbery of PDA's rights. To counter this, the government has implemented reservations in recruitments for outsourced positions as well. Now in recruitments done through outsource corporation, Scheduled Castes (SC) will get 21%, Scheduled Tribes (ST) will get 2%, Other Backward Classes (OBC) will get 27% and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) will get 10% reservation. Employees will get these facilities Employees recruited under the outsource corporation will get several benefits, like those available to government employees, which were not available earlier through agencies. Why was this Corporation necessary? Previously, agencies would take contracts from departments and recruit employees. This often led to complaints of salary deductions, delayed payments, and exploitation. Employee organisations demanded that the government take direct control. The formation of the corporation will solve this problem. Recruitment will be done through the GeM portal, which is completely transparent. The corporation will not only recruit but will also take responsibility for salary, service conditions, and grievance redressal. Youth can now get jobs directly in government departments through the corporation. With reservation provisions in place, youth from backward classes will especially benefit.

stories.title: Heat rises early across Uttar Pradesh:Summer 2026 could have record temperatures, say experts
stories.summary: Half of February has not yet passed, yet summer is already beginning to make its presence felt in Uttar Pradesh. While mornings and evenings still carry a slight chill, the afternoon sun has grown noticeably sharper. During the recent winter season, cold conditions affected much of Uttar Pradesh and North India. Now, there are indications that just as winter was intense, summer this year could also set records. Early signs of rising temperatures are already visible. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), 2025 was the country’s eighth warmest year. Before that, 2024 was recorded as the warmest year on record. In this context, projections emerging for 2026 are raising concern. This leads to key questions: how severe will the heat be this time? Could 2026 surpass the record set in 2024? And how cold was the recent winter? Winter conditions this year Mahesh Palawat, Vice-President (Meteorology and Climate Change) at Noida-based Skymet Weather, explained that Uttar Pradesh experienced milder winter conditions compared with the previous two years. In December and January, both average maximum and minimum temperatures remained above normal. Typically, winter maximum temperatures in North India range between 20°C and 22°C, while minimum temperatures range between 10°C and 15°C. According to Palawat, both parameters were higher than average this season, and extreme cold was not observed. He attributed the milder winter to the absence of La Niña conditions. Mohammed Danish, a scientist at the Lucknow Meteorological Centre, also confirmed that this winter was less severe than last year. What is La Niña? La Niña is a global climate pattern in which ocean waters become cooler than usual. When this cooler water evaporates, cloud formation increases, influencing rainfall patterns. In India, whether rainfall will be deficient or abundant, and whether temperatures will trend colder or hotter, is significantly influenced by La Niña. Before winter 2025 began, the IMD had estimated that La Niña might develop, potentially intensifying cold conditions in North India. However, La Niña did not materialise in the Pacific Ocean, and therefore, a sharp increase in cold was not observed. At the beginning of the season, the United States weather agency NOAA had estimated a 60 per cent probability of La Niña becoming active during winter, with possible effects lasting until March. This scenario did not occur. Reduced western disturbances and rainfall deficit Meteorologist Mohammed Danish noted that the activity of Western Disturbances over Uttar Pradesh was also limited during the winter season. As a result, rainfall during the cold months remained below normal. Extended periods of cloud cover and fog typically intensify cold conditions, but such patterns were largely absent this year. In most districts, sunshine prevailed during the day. According to IMD data, Uttar Pradesh recorded a 36 per cent rainfall deficit between 1 January and 11 February. February trends and short-term outlook Professor Manoj Kumar Srivastava, a meteorologist from Banaras Hindu University’s Geophysics Department, stated that the region is currently experiencing spring conditions. Over the next two to three weeks, significant changes are unlikely. Mornings and nights will remain slightly cool, while afternoons will feel warmer. Mahesh Palawat indicated that light drizzle may occur around 18 February in districts including Hathras, Mathura, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Banda, Lalitpur and Jhansi. Experts agree that winter is now in its final phase and temperatures will gradually increase. Record temperatures in early 2025 For the first time since temperature records began in 1901, the average minimum temperature in February 2025 remained above 15°C. January 2025 was also recorded as the third-warmest January since 1901. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) confirmed that 2024 was the warmest year on record globally, with Earth’s temperature rising by 1.55°C that year. Outlook for Summer 2026 According to Professor Srivastava, weather conditions in Uttar Pradesh will change markedly from the first week of March, marking the onset of summer. Both daytime and night-time temperatures are expected to rise rapidly. By the last week of March, maximum temperatures in many districts could reach 35°C to 38°C. In April, temperatures are likely to hover around 40°C. He further indicated that maximum temperatures could climb to 42°C to 45°C in several districts. Relief from heat may be limited even at night, with humidity persisting. However, he cautioned that precise predictions depend largely on the El Niño situation. If El Niño persists or strengthens, summer conditions could intensify further, increasing the number and duration of heatwave days. Climate change and urban heat Dhruvsen Singh, Head of the Department of Earth Sciences at Lucknow University, highlighted structural factors contributing to rising heat. Rapid deforestation, disappearance of natural water bodies, expanding urban concrete infrastructure and increased vehicular traffic are collectively driving temperatures upward. Urban areas may face heightened severity due to the Urban Heat Island effect. Experts assess that 2026 could see above-normal heat in Uttar Pradesh, with more frequent and prolonged heatwaves. National and global projections IMD projects that maximum and minimum temperatures across India will remain above normal from March to May. In March, both are expected to exceed normal levels nationwide, and heatwave days are likely to be higher than usual. Only Northeast India and certain peninsular states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, are expected to experience normal heatwave frequency. El Niño, like La Niña, originates in the Pacific Ocean. When El Niño occurs, India’s monsoon weakens, often leading to drought in several states. Meteorologists currently express concern that if El Niño develops, severe heat could follow. Impact on Agriculture Professor P.K. Singh of BHU’s Agriculture Department warned that March could prove challenging for farmers. Rapid temperature increases during the grain-filling stage of wheat could reduce yield. Excessive heat prevents proper grain development. Hot winds and moisture deficiency may also damage mustard, gram and peas. Rising temperatures dry soils quickly, increasing irrigation costs and crop stress. Global heat concerns A report by Environment and Climate Data UK suggests that 2026 could rank among the four hottest years globally. Rising greenhouse gas concentrations and natural factors such as El Niño continue to elevate global temperatures. Projections indicate that average global temperatures in 2026 may be 1.4°C to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. Such warming could undermine Paris Agreement goals, increasing the likelihood of extreme heat, droughts, floods and abrupt weather events, directly affecting health, agriculture and daily life.

‘European pride’: Kallas responds to boos for JD Vance during Winter Olympics opening ceremony in Italy
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance was booed at the Winter Olympics opening ceremony in Milan, with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas attributing the reaction to "European pride" amid growing transatlantic tensions. Kallas cited recent US criticism of the EU, including Vance's questioning of shared democratic visions and comments on disinformation.

stories.title: Nancy Guthrie kidnapping case: Third ransom letter sent to TMZ demands 1 Bitcoin to reveal ‘name of individual involved’
stories.summary: A new letter reportedly sent to TMZ demands one bitcoin, valued at $66,000, for the identity of Savannah Guthrie's mother's kidnapper. This is the third alleged note since Nancy Guthrie's disappearance on January 31. The letter includes a working bitcoin address and emphasizes the urgency of the situation.

stories.title: 1 in 3 faculty posts vacant across AIIMS; over 17,000 Non-Faculty Posts Also Unfilled
stories.summary: Nearly one-third of faculty positions across India's AIIMS are vacant, with both older and newer institutes facing significant staffing gaps. Non-faculty positions are also severely understaffed, raising concerns about the pace of recruitment matching infrastructure and patient demand growth.

stories.title: Indian-origin man jailed in US over false kidnapping charges files lawsuit: 'Biggest headache'
Delhi CM disburses education aid to 15,700 workers' children
stories.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta disbursed financial aid to 15,700 construction workers' children, totaling Rs 12.40 crore, to support their education. This initiative, marking the BJP government's first anniversary, offers monthly assistance ranging from Rs 500 to Rs 10,000 based on educational levels. The government also highlighted other welfare schemes and development projects.

stories.title: Delhi HC grants bail in MCOCA case over 24-hour production violation
stories.summary: The appellant, Harsh Pal Singh alias Rubal, was allegedly involved in an organized crime syndicate and faced charges under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the Arms Act. Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha delivered the judgment on February 10, 2026, setting aside a previous trial court order that had denied him bail. The core of the legal dispute centered on the timeline of the appellant's arrest and subsequent production in court. Singh was detained at Amritsar Airport on the night of September 25, 2025, while attempting to travel to Bangkok.

stories.title: 'Why was Puri seeking advice from Epstein?' Congress ups the ante, poses 6 questions
stories.summary: Congress has intensified its criticism of Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri regarding his alleged connections with financier Jeffrey Epstein. Party leader Pawan Khera questioned Puri's interactions, citing an email exchange suggesting Epstein facilitated a meeting with Reid Hoffman. Khera also condemned Puri's remarks on Epstein's conviction, accusing him of trivializing child sexual exploitation and demanding moral clarity from public officials.

stories.title: Kerala poll jitters: CPM scrambles to pacify Satchidanandan after backlash
stories.summary: After the meeting, Khader and Charuvil sought to underplay the row. According to them, Satchidanandan clarified that he was making a general observation and wasn’t referring specifically to the situation in Kerala. They said Satchidanandan also alleged that media had distorted some of his remarks. Satchidanandan said he stood by his statement on the dangers of returning a party to power repeatedly.

Witnesses and activists described a worsening climate of fear and institutional breakdown, urging U.S. policymakers to condemn the violence and impose sanctions on Chief Advisor Muhammad Yunus.

13-year-old suspect shouted ‘Allahu Akbar’ while stabbing student in the neck in UK; eyewitness says children were 'shouting and screaming'

Police are investigating the incident as potentially ideologically motivated, with counter-terrorism officers leading the probe. The suspect was apprehended nearby shortly after fleeing the scene.

stories.title: Indian diaspora among UK's most successful groups: Report links migration to post-war recovery, tech growth
stories.summary: Indian migration to the UK, spanning four distinct waves since 1947, has profoundly shaped the nation's economy. From filling post-war labor gaps and revitalizing local economies through entrepreneurship, to contributing significantly to the tech sector and addressing critical skills shortages today, the diaspora's economic impact is undeniable and continues to be strategically vital.

stories.title: Tumbler Ridge student describes chaos during Canada school shooting: 'We were formulating an escape plan'
stories.summary: A devastating mass shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia has claimed nine lives and injured 25. A Grade 12 student recounted the terrifying hours spent barricaded in a classroom as alarms blared. Police found the suspect deceased at the scene. This incident marks one of Canada's worst shootings, leaving a community in shock and grief.

'Let us do it together': Rahul Gandhi cuts in as minister Ashwini Vaishnaw speaks - watch
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of "selling out Bharat Mata" and compromising India's energy security and farmers' interests through an interim trade deal with the US. He alleged the deal amounted to a "wholesale surrender," with the US dictating India's oil purchases and monitoring its finances. Gandhi's claims were met with objections from treasury bench MPs.

stories.title: 'I barely know what he’s saying': AOC fires back at Trump after he calls Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl halftime show ‘worst ever’
stories.summary: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez responded to Donald Trump's criticism of Bad Bunny's Super Bowl halftime show. Trump called the performance "terrible" and nonsensical, stating "nobody understands a word this guy is saying." AOC retorted that she "barely knows what Trump is saying half the time, so… I feel him."

stories.title: Indian trucker Sukhwinder Sidhu pleads guilty in 2023 crash killing Olympian skater in Ontario, was driving for 26 hours
stories.summary: Sukhwinder Sidhu, an Indian-origin truck driver, has entered a guilty plea in connection with the fatal chain of events that led to the death of Olympic figure skater Alexandra Paul in 2023. Evidence showed that Sidhu was driving at perilous speeds through a construction zone—almost twice the legal limit—after being on the road for a grueling 26 hours.

stories.title: 'Didn’t really like the way she talked': How a phone call from Swiss leader led Trump to raise tariffs to 39%
stories.summary: President Trump revealed a phone call with Swiss leader Karin Keller-Sutter, whom he mistakenly called Prime Minister, prompted a tariff hike on Swiss imports. Despite her arguments about Switzerland's small size, Trump increased tariffs to 39% due to a $42 billion trade deficit, believing Switzerland had been "ripping us off."

stories.summary: An Indian family in Dubai experienced a moment of panic when the gold they owned, worth AED 50,000 was accidentally thrown away. A diligent waste worker found the valuables. Dubai Police swiftly traced the gold back to the family. The precious items were returned within three days, showcasing civic efficiency and honesty.

stories.title: 'Met Epstein 3-4 times': Harpdeep Puri sets record straight after Rahul Gandhi's charge in Lok Sabha

I just want to share some information... I want to clarify that these facts are all public," Puri said at a press conference. Puri said the meetings took place before he joined the Union Cabinet in 2017 and are already in the public domain.

stories.title: American Youtuber Alex Stein mocks Hindus with cow urine slurs at event; angry Indian-Americans walk out
stories.summary: During a recent Plano City Council meeting, comedian Alex Stein caused a stir by mocking Hindu customs, specifically cow veneration along with the traditional uses of cow dung and urine. Clad in Indian garb, his satirical commentary prompted several Indian-American attendees to walk out in protest.

stories.title: Jynxzi accuses Supercell of ignoring streamers in Clash Royale “historic year” recap
stories.summary: Twitch star Jynxzi slammed Supercell after its 2025 Clash Royale recap credited internal updates for massive growth while overlooking streamers. He argued that creators drove the game’s renewed popularity and accused the company of taking full credit. During a fiery livestream, Jynxzi criticized leadership and predicted 2026 could be Clash Royale’s worst year without major changes.

stories.title: Beyond Silicon Valley: India and UAE are building a new AI model
stories.summary: India and the UAE are forging a powerful AI alliance in 2026, prioritising human-centric development for social welfare and equitable growth. The strategic partnership focuses on shared values. It aims to leverage AI for societal benefit through joint infrastructure, workforce development and ethical governance frameworks to set a global precedent.

stories.title: “Erika should be dragged into a police”: Candace Owens faces outrage over Erika Kirk jail remark and conspiracy claims
stories.summary: Candace Owens' recent commentary, suggesting Erika Kirk should be jailed and calling her statements a "full-blown conspiracy," has ignited a fierce online debate. Critics condemn her language as dangerous and defamatory, while supporters argue she's raising valid questions. The controversy highlights the rapid escalation of online discourse and the impact of public figures' words.

stories.summary: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta made the submission before a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and PB Varale in response to the Supreme Court’s earlier query, asking the authorities to consider Wangchuk’s release on medical grounds over his deteriorating health issue. stories.title: DM Tehri reviews Lake Festival preparations; Master Chef, kite show, fashion show among events

stories.summary: The Supreme Court reduced a "faulty haircut" compensation from Rs 2 crore to Rs 25 lakh, stating damages require material evidence, not just claims. The court emphasized that consumer dispute compensation cannot be based on whims or presumptions, especially for large sums. While "deficiency in service" was established, the woman failed to provide sufficient proof of her claimed losses.

stories.title: 'Over 50% polling stations centres': How Bangladesh is preparing for first election since Hasina ouster
stories.summary: Bangladesh is holding parliamentary elections amidst unprecedented security following the ouster of former PM Sheikh Hasina. Over half of polling centres are deemed risk-prone, prompting a massive deployment of nearly 9.58 lakh security personnel. For the first time, drones and body-worn cameras will monitor the process, aiming for a peaceful transition after the Hasina era.

stories.title: UAE visa rejection reasons: Top mistakes Indians make and how to avoid them
stories.summary: Indian citizens seeking UAE visas in 2026 face increased scrutiny, with common rejections stemming from minor errors. Wonder what the key pitfalls include? Read on as we spill the beans on incomplete applications, passport issues, incorrect visa categories, weak financial proof and insufficient ties that could be the reason behind visa rejection. Careful documentation and adherence to guidelines are crucial for a smooth approval process.

stories.title: UAE grocery prices set to drop as retailers permanently slash prices on 10,000 essentials
stories.summary: Choithrams is implementing a permanent price reduction on thousands of everyday essentials across the UAE, aiming for "everyday lower pricing" rather than temporary promotions. This strategic move, affecting around 10,000 products with average cuts of 15%, seeks to provide predictable savings for consumers, especially ahead of Ramadan.

These reforms aim to make services faster for Overseas Filipino Workers, including those in the UAE. The goal is to cut down waiting times and simplify procedures. Digital passes and streamlined travel clearances will be key. This modernisation will improve support and protection for millions of vital overseas workers.

stories.title: Who is Hind Al-Owais? UAE human rights diplomat named in 469 Jeffrey Epstein emails

The files are unverified, and Al-Owais remains in her role.

stories.title: UAE drops corporate tax for sports bodies under new law: Here’s who qualifies
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates Ministry of Finance has introduced a new corporate tax exemption for non-commercial sports organisations. This policy aims to boost the UAE's sports sector and strengthen its global standing. Qualifying entities must be officially recognised and strictly non-commercial. The move is expected to encourage investment and growth within the sports ecosystem, supporting talent development and international partnerships.

stories.title: Kuwait extends two-day public holiday for 65th National Day, Liberation Day celebrations
stories.summary: Kuwait's Cabinet has declared February 25th and 26th, 2026, as public holidays to celebrate National Day and Liberation Day. This announcement grants public sector employees a four-day break, including the weekend, with work resuming on March 1st. The holidays commemorate significant historical events and foster national pride through various public celebrations.

stories.title: ‘Mini Pakistan’ reference in Rajya Sabha kicks up a row

stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor criticized the India-US interim trade deal, calling it a "pre-committed purchase agreement" that lacks reciprocity. Tharoor also described the Union Budget as an "underwhelming" and "squandered opportunity."

stories.summary: Opposition's bid to remove the Speaker failed, exposing internal rifts as pragmatic voices pushed for legislative business. The government emerged stronger, refusing Congress's demands, while regional parties' desire for discussions on their concerns helped end the impasse. The Speaker stepped aside until the notice is addressed.

stories.title: Joblessness among those aged 15 and above falls in rural, urban areas in Oct-Dec: PLFS
stories.summary: India's unemployment rate for those 15 and above in rural areas dropped to 4% in Oct-Dec 2025, down from 4.4% in the previous quarter. The overall Labour Force Participation Rate also saw a marginal increase to 55.8%, with female participation rising to 34.9%.

Ensure marginalised groups’ representation in MP legal team: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has urged Madhya Pradesh's advocate general to ensure representation of marginalized communities and women as government lawyers. Justices M M Sundresh and N Kotiswar Singh highlighted the lack of ST advocates and low representation of SCs and OBCs, questioning how these communities can emerge without opportunity.

stories.title: Centre proposes spl NIA courts in 17 states, SC seeks their reply
stories.summary: Responding to Supreme Court's push, the Centre will establish at least one special court in 17 states for NIA terror cases. Each state will receive ₹1 crore for costs, with existing courts to be designated for these trials. This move aims to expedite justice for serious crimes, preventing prolonged detentions due to overloaded dockets.

stories.title: “I want to honor God”: Erika Kirk addresses backlash as Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl LX show outshines TPUSA’s halftime show
stories.summary: Erika Kirk spoke out after Turning Point USA aired its alternative Super Bowl LX halftime show honoring her late husband, Charlie Kirk. The broadcast featured a tribute montage and patriotic performances, claiming millions of viewers despite streaming restrictions. While Bad Bunny headlined the official NFL show, the rival event blended politics, grief, and culture into a deeply emotional night.

stories.title: Niti Aayog seeks diesel vehicle phase-out, focus on cleaner tech
stories.summary: Niti Aayog has proposed a roadmap for India's transport sector to achieve net zero emissions by 2070. The strategy involves phasing out diesel vehicles and promoting cleaner technologies like CNG, hybrids, and electric vehicles. Stricter Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency (CAFE) norms will also be implemented to support this transition.

stories.title: SC puts on hold drive against encroachers in Assam forests
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has halted Assam's anti-encroachment drive in reserved forests, emphasizing that environmental protection and rule of law must coexist. Alleged encroachers will now have a chance to submit documents, and action will only be taken after a thorough review and a formal notice to vacate.

stories.title: Kelly Refuses To Condemn Owens: Faces backlash over Israel row; cites free speech stance
stories.summary: Megyn Kelly defended her decision not to condemn Candace Owens despite public pressure over controversial online claims involving Charlie Kirk. Kelly said the demands were political and rooted in Israel-related debates. She stressed about Charlie Kirk theories and that refusing to condemn someone does not mean agreement, adding she will not speak just to satisfy critics.

stories.summary: The Delhi High Court urged the family of late industrialist Sunjay Kapur to pursue mediation to resolve their disputes, advising them not to let wealth become a curse. stories.title: CPI, CPM move SC for FIR against Himanta over 'target-shooting' video

stories.title: Online evaluation for CBSE Class XII, Class X to be manual
stories.summary: CBSE will implement on-screen marking for Class XII evaluations while Class X will continue with manual marking. This shift aims for faster, error-free assessments, though principals express concerns about the short preparation time. Schools are being equipped with necessary infrastructure and training for the new system.

stories.title: 3-hr takedown, AI labels: Govt cracks down on deepfakes
stories.summary: India has significantly tightened digital rules to combat deepfakes, mandating clear labelling and traceability for AI-generated content. Social media platforms now face stricter compliance, with reduced timelines for takedown of unlawful material and direct responsibility placed on senior officers. These new regulations aim to enhance user safety and accountability in the digital space.

stories.title: Twitch introduces new ads for paused streams, sparks viewer backlash
stories.summary: Twitch is rolling out "pause-screen ads" starting February 10, 2026, a move met with criticism from viewers and streamers. While intended to boost streamer earnings, users fear these ads will disrupt viewing habits and potentially lead to site abandonment. The platform maintains the ads aim to increase revenue without fully interrupting the stream.

stories.title: SC's gender handbook is too 'Harvard-oriented': CJI
stories.summary: Chief Justice Surya Kant criticized the Supreme Court's gender stereotype handbook as overly technical and inaccessible to common people and rape survivors. He emphasized the need for practical training for High Court judges on handling sexual assault cases. The bench set aside an insensitive Allahabad High Court ruling on an attempted rape case.

stories.title: Opposition, barring TMC, submits notice for removal of Speaker
stories.summary: Opposition parties, excluding TMC, have submitted a notice to remove Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, accusing him of "blatant partisanship." The move follows repeated denials of permission for Rahul Gandhi to speak, escalating tensions. Birla will abstain from proceedings until the resolution is addressed, likely on March 9.

The White House's exclusion of key Democratic leaders goes against the NGA's tradition of bipartisan gatherings.

stories.summary: Team USA curler Rich Ruohonen used an Olympic press conference to voice concerns about immigration enforcement actions in his home state of Minnesota. Ruohonen also commended Minnesotans for their compassion during this challenging time.

The extended service aims to boost tourism by making journeys more comfortable and visually captivating.

stories.title: 'From 150 members to 12': Uttarakhand gym owner counts cost of becoming 'Mohammad Deepak'

Security has been increased amid threats of further action.
