Some raised slogans supporting Syed Hassan Nasrallah, Palestine, and Hezbollah.

stories.title: UK considers targeting Russia’s ‘shadow fleet’ in new escalation against Moscow
stories.summary: Britain is exploring military options to seize Russia-linked shadow fleet tankers, potentially opening a new front against Moscow as its oil revenues decline. This comes after the US seized a similar vessel. While international law allows for challenging stateless ships, escalatory risks have so far prevented action, despite Royal Marines expressing readiness.

stories.title: Eyewitness recalls horrific moment as skier dies on expert run at popular California mountain resort
‘Never seen an Indian…’: US political influencer defends Asian students amid exam cheating claims
Three-storeyed building collapses in Rajasthan's Kota; 2 killed, several feared trapped
stories.summary: A three-storey building housing a restaurant collapsed in Kota, Rajasthan, killing at least two people and leaving several others feared trapped. Rescue operations are underway, with five individuals already rescued and hospitalized. The incident occurred in the Talwandi area, and authorities are working to ascertain the full extent of casualties.

stories.title: About 37,000 players without diet allowance for 10 months in Haryana, claims AAP's Dhanda
stories.summary: Haryana's BJP government faces sharp criticism for allegedly withholding diet allowances for 37,000 players for ten months. Senior AAP leader Anurag Dhanda also highlighted the denial of pensions to over 75,000 elderly citizens, citing "absurd" income criteria. This has left athletes and seniors struggling, questioning the government's commitment to their welfare.

stories.title: The Art of the Deal, drawn in ink: Trump’s map makes India the anchor
Sri Lankan influencer arrested in Canada for creepy public filming of women; charged with harassment
After 44 Years, BJP returns to Mumbai mayor’s office: Ritu Tawde set to be elected unopposed; end of Thackeray era in BMC
Epstein acquaintance Jeffrey Leeds accuses wife of affair, misuse of marital funds in divorce filing
stories.summary: A high-profile divorce between private equity executive Jeffrey Leeds and his wife, Elizabeth, has erupted with accusations of affairs, financial misconduct, and harassment. The legal battle spans multiple states and involves a significant real estate portfolio. Allegations include claims of infidelity with a Miami businessman and misuse of marital funds for personal gain.

stories.title: Nancy Guthrie's kidnapping case: Trump says 'feds have strong clues and answers coming up soon'
stories.summary: Federal authorities are reportedly close to identifying a suspect in the apparent abduction of Nancy Guthrie, mother of NBC anchor Savannah Guthrie. President Trump stated on Air Force One that strong clues are emerging and answers could be forthcoming soon.

stories.title: Delhi biker death: CM Gupta issues 8-point safety framework, seeks list of excavation sites
IShowSpeed announces streaming break after YouTube income drops to $800K a month
stories.summary: Popular streamer IShowSpeed is taking a break, citing a drop in his monthly YouTube income to approximately $800,000. He expressed frustration over his perceived lack of value despite consistent effort, highlighting the unpredictable nature of online earnings. This move underscores the immense pressure top influencers face and the volatility of their income, even at substantial levels.

stories.title: Fairground ride collapses in Haryana's Surajkund Mela: One dead, several injured
stories.summary: Tragedy struck the Surajkund Mela in Faridabad Saturday evening when a swing ride collapsed, killing a police inspector and injuring thirteen others. The brave officer lost his life attempting to rescue people as the ride tilted. Authorities have vowed swift action against the operator, with an FIR to be registered.

stories.title: Private Bill seeks diversity in judicial appointments, SC’s regional benches
Oil-smuggling syndicate exposed at sea: Coast Guard intercepts 3 vessels near Mumbai
'Only complaining when it’s Indians': Row over Dinesh D’Souza calling Trump’s ‘racist’ AI video on Obama ‘harmless’
'Sangh does not seek popularity or power': RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated the organization wasn't formed in opposition to any group and doesn't seek power or popularity. He highlighted over 1.3 lakh service projects by volunteers nationwide, funded by their own resources. Bhagwat also touched upon the challenging early life of RSS founder K.B. Hedgewar and his involvement in revolutionary activities during India's freedom struggle.

stories.title: The GOAT job: Texas hires 300 goats to clear invasive shrubs in a unique ecological move
stories.summary: Dallas deployed 300 goats to clear invasive shrubs near White Rock Lake, utilizing controlled grazing over 11 acres. This unconventional method reduced soil disturbance and avoided fuel-powered equipment, proving effective against stubborn vegetation. The goats' natural browsing habits and ability to access difficult terrain offer an eco-friendly alternative to machinery for land management.

stories.title: 'Rahul became violent': Ravneet Singh Bittu on 'traitor' face-off, says LoP came towards him after 'losing his temper'
'Shree Ram Mandir Mayur Vihar': Mayur Vihar Pocket 1 metro station gets new name
Unemployed Indian-origin woman fined over Rs 2 lakh for feeding pigeons in Singapore
MCD commissioner's financial powers enhanced from Rs 5 crore to Rs 50 crore: Delhi govt
stories.summary: In an ambitious push for development, Delhi's municipal commissioner now wields expanded financial authority, increasing from Rs 5 crore to a hefty Rs 50 crore. This significant change, spearheaded by the Delhi government, aims to cut through bureaucratic red tape, ensuring that essential projects for roads, sanitation, and civic amenities are launched and completed swiftly.

stories.title: Enthusiasm of tourists from across India to visit J&K has not diminished: Amit Shah
When music turns into prayer: Inside the world of 'bhajan concerts'
stories.summary: Devotional music concerts are experiencing a surge in popularity, attracting younger audiences with their blend of spiritual chants and contemporary arrangements. These gatherings offer a unique, immersive experience, fostering community and emotional grounding amidst urban life. Prime Minister Modi even highlighted this growing trend, calling it 'bhajan-clubbing,' as traditional practices find new relevance.

stories.title: You didn’t go to school: Bill Maher slams Billie Eilish’s anti-ICE Grammy speech
Slipped on ice and got paid? Indian influencer claims icy driveway falls in Canada can bring $40,000 — is it true?
stories.summary: A viral video suggests Canadian homeowners face hefty lawsuits for icy driveway slips, with potential payouts of $20,000-$40,000. While homeowners do have a duty to maintain safe conditions, liability hinges on negligence. Cases are assessed individually, often involving insurance, and depend on reasonable steps taken to prevent hazards.

stories.title: Ajit Pawar plane crash probe: NCP (SP) leader Rohit Pawar to present details on Feb 10 as doubts persist
Prince Andrew’s ex Lady Victoria Hervey says Epstein is alive, mocks those not in files: “You were a loser”
How Shashi Tharoor-Congress 'Hum Saath Saath Hai' moment gives UDF a timely lift before Kerala polls
Evening news wrap: PM Modi in Malaysia for 2-day visit; key details of India-US trade pact revealed & more
“His third eye…”: Candace Owens claims Charlie Kirk believed he was psychic and a time traveller
stories.summary: Candace Owens claims Charlie Kirk spoke privately about having psychic abilities, including a “third eye,” astral projection, and unusual childhood experiences. She also alleged he believed he might die young and referenced a CIA program called “Project Looking Glass.” The unverified remarks have sparked backlash, with critics questioning her claims and their impact on Kirk’s legacy.

stories.title: ‘Keeping Indian wife happy’: Row over Republican saying Texans go to malls and ‘feel like they’re in Pakistan’
Russia oil to keep flowing? India reiterates stance on energy sourcing
“Islam is a religion built on migration”: NYC Mayor Mamdani invokes Prophet Muhammad’s hijrah while speaking on immigration
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani sparked debate by referencing Islamic history, specifically the Hijrah, to advocate for compassionate US immigration policies. He highlighted Prophet Muhammad's journey as a lesson in welcoming strangers, linking it to NYC's sanctuary status and shared moral values across faiths.

stories.title: Sheikh Mohammed to honour sixth Arab Hope Makers winners with Dh1 million prize on February 15
stories.summary: Dubai will host the Arab Hope Makers closing ceremony on February 15. His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum will attend. The event will honour humanitarian efforts from across the Arab world. A winner will receive a one million Dirham award. This initiative celebrates individuals and organisations dedicated to improving lives through voluntary work.

stories.title: ‘Khejri Bachao Andolan': Why Rajasthan is rallying to protect its ‘Kalpavriksha’? Explained
stories.summary: A significant protest is under way in Rajasthan over the felling of the khejri tree. Communities are demanding stronger protection for the state tree, alleging that it is being cut to make way for solar power projects. Political leaders across parties have joined the movement, drawing attention to the tree’s cultural and ecological significance. In an arid landscape where survival is closely tied to ecology, the debate in western Rajasthan now extends beyond development to questions of history, identity and survival.

stories.title: Could MrBeast’s $100 million gamble transform East Carolina into college football’s next powerhouse?
stories.summary: MrBeast has hinted at a potential $100 million investment to help East Carolina chase a national championship. The idea gained traction after an AI image sparked online buzz. In today’s NIL-driven era, such funding could instantly elevate the program’s recruiting power and roster strength. While questions remain, the proposal could reshape college football’s competitive landscape.

stories.title: ‘Tamil is India’s link to the world’: PM Modi addresses Indian diaspora in Malaysia; highlights cultural ties
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the strong cultural and emotional ties between India and Malaysia during his interaction with the Indian diaspora in Kuala Lumpur. He praised the community for preserving traditions and acknowledged Malaysia's significant Indian-origin population as a "living bridge." Modi also emphasised the global importance of the Tamil language and culture.

stories.title: 'Blow to stomachs of Indian farmers': Opposition slams India-US trade framework — who said what
stories.summary: Opposition leaders are raising concerns over the India-US Interim Trade Agreement. They claim the government has compromised national interests. Worries are focused on the impact on farmers, tariffs, and oil imports. Leaders suggest the deal could lead to unrest as its full implications become clear. The agreement is part of broader trade negotiations.

stories.title: 'Frivolous and politically motivated': Sonia Gandhi opposes plea over 1980 voter list entry
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi has opposed a criminal revision petition against her, labelling it politically motivated and an abuse of law. She argued that citizenship and electoral roll matters, dating back four decades, cannot be criminalised. Her response, filed in court, asserts the complainant's accusations are based on speculation, not authentic records, and urges dismissal of the plea.

stories.title: North Korea executes teens for watching Squid Game and listening to K-Pop
stories.summary: Shocking testimony reveals North Koreans, including students, face execution for watching South Korean shows like Squid Game and listening to K-pop. Amnesty International reports severe punishments, including death, for consuming foreign media. New laws mandate harsh penalties, with executions serving as 'ideological education' to deter citizens from foreign cultural influences.

stories.title: UAE launches new public security reporting service SSD: what it is and how it works, explained
stories.summary: The UAE State Security Department has launched the "SSD" service, a confidential reporting channel for residents to alert authorities to potential threats. This initiative aims to enhance preventive security, foster community partnership, and reinforce national security by encouraging public participation in maintaining a safe society. The service accepts reports on various security concerns and ensures strict confidentiality for all reporters.

stories.title: UAE warns citizens in Spain as storm Leonardo triggers floods and evacuations
stories.summary: The UAE Embassy in Madrid has issued a critical safety advisory for Emirati citizens in Spain due to Storm Leonardo, which has caused severe flooding and evacuations. Citizens are urged to remain vigilant, avoid affected areas, and follow official guidance. The embassy also advises registration on the 'Tawajudi' service for emergency assistance.

stories.title: UAE education reform 2026: English mandatory for mathematics and science in private schools
stories.summary: The UAE's Ministry of Education has mandated that advanced mathematics and science subjects will be taught in English across private schools, starting with Grade 9 in the 2026-2027 academic year. This phased implementation, extending to Grade 12 by 2029-2030, aims to equip students with global competencies for higher education and STEM careers where English is prevalent.

stories.title: Message to Pakistan? Amid trade pact, India's map shared by US trade representative grabs attention
stories.summary: A US trade representative's map, released alongside an interim trade agreement framework, correctly depicts the entirety of Jammu and Kashmir and Aksai Chin as part of India. This marks a departure from previous US maps and aligns with India's stance, potentially signaling a shift in US policy towards Pakistan and China.

stories.title: UAE makes historic Winter Olympics debut at Milan-Cortina 2026
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates made history at the Milan Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics, marking its first-ever senior team debut. Alpine skiers Alexander Astridge and Piera Hudson proudly carried the UAE flag, showcasing the nation's growing commitment to winter sports. This milestone underscores a strategic, long-term vision for developing a sustainable winter sports ecosystem beyond traditional snowbound nations.

stories.title: Ola, Uber and other app-based taxi drivers to hold day-long strike – all you need to know
stories.summary: App-based transport workers nationwide protested on February 7, demanding fair incomes and protection against exploitation. Unions cited falling earnings and rising costs, urging governments to implement minimum base fares as mandated by 2025 guidelines. The strike highlighted concerns over unilateral pricing by platforms and financial burdens from device changes, with workers seeking statutory protections.

stories.title: 'Dost dost na raha': Congress takes filmy jibe at India-US trade deal; poses 5 questions
stories.summary: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh criticized the recent India-US trade framework, alleging it benefits American farmers at India's expense and includes a commitment to stop Russian oil imports. He questioned the value of "photo-ops" given the perceived lack of substantial benefits for India in the deal.

stories.title: 'Many can be CM': Ahead of civic polls, Siddaramaiah's son quashes CM-change buzz
'Aim to deepen defence, security ties': PM Modi embarks on two-day visit to Malaysia
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is on a significant two-day visit to Malaysia to bolster defense, security, and economic ties. This trip aims to deepen the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, with discussions focusing on defense cooperation, innovation, and new collaborative areas. PM Modi will also engage with the vibrant Indian diaspora in Kuala Lumpur.

stories.title: 14 of 15 WB IAS officers attend EC’s observers briefing; 1 officer exempted by EC
IFS/IAS appointees can’t reappear for 2026 Civil Services exam; IPS can’t choose IPS again
stories.summary: New rules for the Civil Services Examination will regulate repeated attempts. Candidates appointed to IAS or IFS from CSE 2026 will not be allowed to reappear. Those appointed to IPS or Group A services can get one improvement attempt. The Union Public Service Commission is also adding more examination centres and prioritizing candidates with benchmark disabilities.

stories.title: 'Consequences are very steep': Trump gives update on US-Iran talks; follows it with stark warning
stories.summary: President Trump has signed an executive order allowing tariffs on countries trading with Iran, citing a 25% example. This move comes as Trump described ongoing US-Iran talks as "very good" and expressed optimism about a potential deal, while also warning of "steep consequences" if negotiations fail. The administration aims to hold Iran accountable for its nuclear program and regional destabilization.

stories.title: UAE weather forecast: Morning mist, humidity and rain expected this week
stories.summary: UAE residents should prepare for humid mornings and increasing cloud cover this week. Rain is possible, particularly over islands and coastal areas from Saturday night into Sunday, with another chance on Tuesday. Temperatures will rise until Monday before a slight dip. Light to moderate winds are expected, with occasional rough seas.

stories.title: ‘Harvard is woke, we are not’: US to cut ties, end military training and fellowships with Ivy League giant
stories.summary: The US Pentagon will stop all military training and fellowship programs with Harvard University starting in the 2026-27 academic year. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated Harvard no longer meets the needs of the War Department. This action is part of a broader campaign by the Trump administration against the university.

stories.title: Strengthens ‘Make in India’: PM Modi hails India-US trade deal; thanks Trump
'Didn't make a mistake': Trump refuses to apologise for video depicting Obamas as monkeys
stories.summary: President Trump refused to apologise for a racist video depicting the Obamas as apes, which he posted and then deleted. He claimed he hadn't seen the offensive content and blamed a staffer, despite acknowledging he watched part of it. The White House initially defended the post before stating a staffer made an error.

stories.title: Violent anti-govt protests return to Dhaka, this time against Yunus
Propaganda against Manmohan insult to Sikh faith: Kharge
Amit Shah calls for tech-driven solutions to border challenges, holds high-level review meet on J&K security
Studies vs gaming: Strike a balance, PM Modi tells students
stories.summary: PM Modi, at Pariksha Pe Charcha 2026, urged students to find balance between academics and skills, emphasizing life and professional skills are intertwined. He encouraged pursuing gaming as a skill, drawing from Indian stories, but warned against gambling. Collaborative learning and prioritizing Class XII exams were also highlighted, with a call for parents to trust their children's individual growth.

stories.title: 3rd extension in UP SIR: 1 more month for filing claims
stories.summary: The Election Commission has granted a one-month extension for filing claims and objections on Uttar Pradesh's draft electoral rolls, now allowing submissions until March 6. This marks the third extension for the state's voter list revision, with the final rolls to be published on April 10.

stories.title: Suicide blast at Islamabad mosque kills 31, MEA snubs Pak claim of Indian hand
stories.summary: A devastating suicide bombing at a Shia mosque in Islamabad on Friday claimed at least 31 lives and injured over 170, marking the capital's deadliest attack since 2008. The bomber detonated himself at the mosque's entrance after Friday prayers. Pakistan's Defence Minister alleged Indian sponsorship, a claim India vehemently rejected as baseless and a diversion from domestic issues.

stories.title: Epstein’s deathbed will: Who stood to inherit multimillion-dollar fortune, and what about the victims?
stories.summary: Newly released Justice Department records reveal how Jeffrey Epstein sought to distribute his fortune through a trust signed two days before his death in 2019. While the document named dozens of beneficiaries, including his girlfriend, lawyer and accountant, it made no provision for victims. Years of litigation and compensation payments have since dramatically reduced the estate’s value.

stories.title: 'When told I'm 75, I said 25 yrs left': PM Modi tells students to focus on future
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi advised students at 'Pariksha Pe Charcha' that education is for life, not just exams, emphasizing character and temperament over grades. He encouraged focusing on future goals rather than dwelling on past achievements, urging them to live in the present and plan for what lies ahead.

stories.title: US accuses China of secret N-tests in 2020
'I don't know what will happen to me': Pappu Yadav after arrest in 1995 case
stories.summary: Purnea MP Pappu Yadav was arrested by Patna Police in connection with a 1995 case, expressing fears for his safety and demanding to be taken directly to court. He questioned the police's methods and the timing of the arrest. The MP was later admitted to hospital due to health concerns.

stories.title: Norway's Crown Princess apologises for Epstein link, says she did not understand who he was; husband backs her
Chicago woman shooting: Judge allows release of video, Border Patrol agent’s texts who shot her five times
VHP flags Netflix film title as 'offensive'
stories.summary: The Vishwa Hindu Parishad has strongly objected to the Netflix film 'Ghooskhor Pandat', deeming its title offensive and an attack on a respected community. The VHP has demanded government intervention, while sources indicate Netflix voluntarily removed the film's teaser and promotional content from social media. The organization warned of protests if an apology isn't issued.

stories.title: 'Can't be compelled': SC allows termination of minor's 30-wk fetus
stories.summary: The Supreme Court permitted a minor's pregnancy termination, acknowledging her right to reproductive autonomy and the lifelong trauma of an illegitimate child. Despite the Maharashtra government's concerns about a 30-week fetus's viability and the suggestion of an orphanage, the court prioritized the girl's mental well-being, directing the procedure with medical safeguards.

stories.title: Exports to China up 37% in Apr-Dec: Minister
stories.summary: India's exports to China surged 37% to $14.2 billion in April-December, with December shipments jumping 67%. Imports, however, rose 13.5% to nearly $96 billion during the same period. The government highlighted that most Chinese imports are capital and intermediate goods, crucial for India's expanding electronics, pharma, and telecom sectors.

stories.title: H-1B visa fee is here to stay: Immigration attorney says employees should hire through L-1 visa to bypass $100K
Iran backs Chabahar port, ready to expand ties with India
stories.summary: Iran reaffirms its commitment to the Chabahar port and cooperation with India, despite US sanctions uncertainty. While a recent budget showed no allocation, India has fulfilled its $120 million commitment and maintains a $250 million credit line for future development. Iran's ambassador highlighted the port's strategic importance for regional access and expressed confidence in India's management of the situation.

stories.title: Winter Olympics Team GB skier uses urine to write an anti-ICE message on snow
Can't misuse judiciary after poll drubbing: Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court sternly criticized the Jan Suraaj Party for challenging Bihar's assembly elections, questioning their motive after a significant electoral defeat. Justices noted the party's failure to win any seats and suggested their petition aimed at gaining popularity. The court emphasized that economic policy issues are for voters to address, not judicial annulment of elections.

stories.title: Top Jaish, LeT men call for jihad, threaten to strike Delhi, Agra
stories.summary: Top commanders from Pakistan-based terror groups JeM and LeT have issued direct threats against India and global powers during rallies coinciding with 'Kashmir Solidarity Day'. Speeches incited violence, calling for jihad and targeting major Indian cities like Delhi and Agra. Intelligence agencies are on high alert for potential cross-border attacks.

stories.title: In a 1st, resolution professional held by ED for colluding with promoters of bankrupt co
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Arvind Kumar, a former resolution professional for Richa Industries Ltd., on charges of collusion, asset siphoning, and money laundering during insolvency proceedings. This marks the first such arrest of an RP by an enforcement agency. The ED's investigation revealed unexplained cash deposits and illicit fund transfers linked to the company's original bank fraud.

stories.title: Lowering age of consent will undermine child safety: Govt
stories.summary: The Union government has rejected the Supreme Court's suggestion to introduce a "Romeo-Juliet" clause for "genuine adolescent relationships" under the Pocso Act. Citing child safety concerns, the government stated that diluting the age of consent would increase exploitation risks and undermine child protection efforts.

stories.title: Supreme Court to examine HP decision to withdraw cases against 65 netas
stories.summary: Himachal Pradesh government has approached the Supreme Court. They are challenging a High Court ruling. The ruling prevented the withdrawal of 65 cases against politicians. These cases involve non-serious offenses. The government believes withdrawing these cases serves public interest. The Supreme Court has issued a notice and will hear the matter further.

stories.title: 'You failed medicine, humanity': Indian-origin doctor blasts at gynecologists who treated Epstein's victims
Pvt, more than govt, colleges gain from NEET PG cut-off drop
stories.summary: NEET PG cut-off reduction to zero in 2023 disproportionately benefited private medical colleges, especially for clinical specialties. General category candidates saw the largest gains, with a significant portion of these seats going to them. The analysis highlights admissions with extremely low scores, raising questions about data completeness.

stories.title: Toll on partially opened e-ways like Delhi-Mumbai to be same as that of other NHs
stories.summary: Commuters using partially operational expressways like Delhi-Mumbai will now pay the same toll as normal national highways. This relief, effective for one year or until full operationalization, addresses concerns that higher tolls deterred usage of incomplete stretches. The decision aims to boost traffic on these corridors.

stories.title: 50 lakh bought FASTag Annual Pass; 50% rise in short trips
stories.summary: Over 50 lakh highway car users have embraced the FASTag Annual Pass in six months, facilitating 26.5 crore toll payments. This scheme has spurred a 50% surge in trips for frequent travelers, with 28% of car transactions now utilizing the pass. Chandigarh, Tamil Nadu, and Delhi lead in adoption, paving the way for barrier-less toll collection.

stories.title: Pahalgam shadow on Omar’s budget: Special hospitals for shelling-prone zones
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah presented a Rs 1.27-lakh crore budget for 2026-27, addressing challenges from recent attacks and floods. The budget includes provisions for emergency hospitals, bullet-proof ambulances, fee waivers for economically weaker students, and support for orphans and disabled individuals. Opposition leaders criticized the budget, calling it uninspiring and a repackaging of central schemes.

stories.title: Why the Netherlands is building homes on water: A global climate solution no one expected
Fake outrage over internet meme: White House responds to Donald Trump's racist Obama video, deleted now
‘Processed food kills’: Mike Tyson’s Super Bowl message sounds alarm on US obesity crisis; Watch
‘They’re trying to take him again’: DHS moves to fast-track deportation in case of 5-year-old Liam Ramos
stories.summary: The federal government is seeking to end asylum claims for a 5-year-old boy and his father, who were recently detained and then released. The Department of Homeland Security has filed a motion to expedite deportation proceedings, which the family's lawyer calls "retaliatory" and a politician condemns as an attempt to break the child's spirit.

stories.title: Jewish billionaire Robert Kraft’s $15 million Super Bowl ad on antisemitism ignites online fury
89 Indians named by US as 'worst of the worst' criminals arrested by ICE
‘I’ve learned Italian since the last time I saw you’: JD Vance jokes with Italy’s Meloni during meeting
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance, attending the Winter Olympics in Italy, engaged in a lighthearted exchange with Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Vance, on a diplomatic visit, jested about his Italian language skills during their meeting. The encounter occurred amidst evolving US-Europe relations, with Vance also attending the figure skating competition.

stories.title: ‘No limits, no transparency, no controls’: US accuses China of covert nuclear tests
stories.summary: The US has accused China of secretly conducting nuclear tests, urging Beijing to join arms control talks as the New START treaty expires. While Russia and the US acknowledge the need for urgent negotiations, China rejects the claims and refuses to participate, citing its smaller arsenal. This raises fears of a new nuclear arms race.

stories.title: Epstein brought models to US on H-1B visa; personally sponsored Ghislaine Maxwell's entry in 1992
‘People are vile and cruel’: Washington Post journalist laid off while on maternity leave responds to 'go back to India' trolling
stories.summary: The Washington Post conducted its largest layoffs in history, impacting one-third of its staff, including a woman on maternity leave. After sharing her experience online, the former employee faced hateful and xenophobic attacks from internet users. She expressed her dismay at the cruelty she encountered, explaining why she limits personal posts.

stories.title: How a UK model swindled men with a £42m inheritance lie to bankroll a lavish lifestyle
